commits.pr_title: [KV Offload] Refactor cpu offloading - calculate gpu pointers and introduce fs ABC
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose
As described in RFC #54777, the kv OffloadingWorker interface passes logical device block IDs to workers, which then internally resolve them to device pointers. This duplicates tensor layout logic in every worker implementation. As part of our GDS implementation, we refactor the worker interface so that device pointer resolution happens once and workers receive pre-resolved device pointers.

We also introduce FSOffloadingWorker, an abstract base for file-based device offloading, so that different filesystem backends (GDS/cuFile, POSIX, NIXL, etc.) can be added without duplicating logic. Following this PR, we will introduce the GDS component as a concrete class inheriting from the FSOffloadingWorker ABC.

## Test Plan
- The connector worker tests (exercises _make_worker / _kv_caches fix)
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_worker.py -v

- The scheduler tests (exercises MockOffloadingWorker / _parse_transfers)
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py -v

- All offloading connector tests at once
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/ -v

- The CPU worker/handler tests
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/ -v

## Test Result
All pass clean.

commits.pr_title: [Metrics][Frontend] Expose request render duration metric
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

We're not tracking pre-processing/rendering time, interesting to spot tokenization bottlenecks, which can be a good signal when to switch to disagg renderer (cc @nt591 who authored).

Adds a `vllm:request_render_duration_seconds` Prometheus histogram measuring the full request render stage — chat templating, tokenization, and multimodal preprocessing — at the shared `OnlineRenderer` boundary, which serves both `/render` (scale-out / disaggregated) and ordinary `/v1/chat/completions` + `/v1/completions` requests. Motivation: render time is currently invisible to operators. Deployments that call `/render` separately (e.g. llm-d with KV-aware routing) pay this stage twice, so a duration metric for the shared stage is needed to attribute frontend latency.

## Claims

- New metric `vllm:request_render_duration_seconds`: histogram with buckets from 0.1 ms through 10 s and bounded `model_name` / `request_type` labels (`chat`, `completion`), exposed on `/metrics`.
- Observed on successful renders through `OnlineRenderer.render_chat` / `render_completion` — the single boundary shared by `/render`, OpenAI serving, and Anthropic serving paths.
- Purely additive: +140/−0 lines; no change to request handling behavior or model outputs.

## Validation

- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` on the changed files: passed.
- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/renderers/test_metrics.py -v`: 3 passed (lazy registration, label separation + count/sum accumulation, bucket range).
- Import smoke test of `vllm.renderers.online_renderer`: passed.
- Full pre-commit suite (ruff, mypy, SPDX headers, test tethering, sign-off) passed on commit.
- Model evaluation: not applicable — the change adds observability only and does not alter outputs, accuracy, or sampling. No GPU is available in this environment for an end-to-end serving run; the added cost is two `perf_counter()` calls and one histogram observe per successful request on the CPU frontend path.

## Details

- `vllm/renderers/metrics.py` (new): histogram definition with lazy registration (`lru_cache`), following the pattern of `vllm/parser/metrics.py` — registers on the default prometheus registry, which `/metrics` serves via `get_prometheus_registry()` in both single-process and `PROMETHEUS_MULTIPROC_DIR` modes.
- `vllm/renderers/online_renderer.py`: `time.perf_counter()` at the top of `render_chat` / `render_completion`; the observation is recorded just before the successful return. Early error returns are not recorded (successful-request semantics).
- `tests/renderers/test_metrics.py` (new): unit tests for the metrics module.

### Why this is not a duplicate

- No open PR adds a render-stage duration metric (searched open PRs for `request_render_duration` and `render duration`; no matches).
- Closest relative: #50875 (open) instruments finer-grained multimodal preprocessing phases (`vllm:mm_*` metrics). This PR instead measures the whole render stage at the `OnlineRenderer` boundary — including chat templating and tokenization — and covers `/render` requests. The two are complementary.
- #44404 (detailed multimodal preprocessing timing stats) is a profiling-stats mechanism, not a Prometheus serving metric.

### Limitations

- `render_responses` is not instrumented; the port stays faithful to the original PR scope (chat + completion). A follow-up could add `request_type="responses"`.
- The metric name intentionally describes the full render stage: requests that reuse token IDs (disaggregated decode-side reuse via `kv_transfer_params`) skip tokenization but are still timed end-to-end.

---

commits.pr_title: [Perf][KV Offload] Publish async lookup results per request group
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`AsyncLookupManager` batches each scheduler step's tier-existence probes, then checks request groups sequentially on its worker. This change publishes a request group's result as soon as that group's lookup finishes, so completed groups no longer wait for later groups before the scheduler can use their results.

## Claims

- A completed group can resolve at the next scheduler drain even while later groups are still being checked; a HIT can therefore become eligible to start promotion earlier.
- The worker remains FIFO and single-threaded. Each group's `batch_lookup()` must finish before its results are published; lookup verdicts and promotion policy are unchanged.
- Results remain grouped by `req_id`; this does not publish a partially consumed group.

## Validation

### Tests

The following results were recorded on PR commit `b117dd93`, before merging the latest `main` and before this test-only cleanup. They have not been rerun on the current PR head.

The current test diff keeps the blocked-group publication and lazy-iterator atomicity cases, folds FIFO ordering into the blocked-group test, and removes a standalone exception case already covered by the existing iterator-failure test.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_async_lookup.py -q
# 22 passed

.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_fs_tier.py \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_obj_tier.py -q
# 82 passed

.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_tiering_offloading.py -q
# 54 passed
```

### FS lookup timing replay

A scheduler-timing replay compared pre-PR aggregate publication with this PR's per-group publication while keeping submission at step end. It used the current `FsAsyncLookupManager`, the repository's `fs_io_C` batch lookup implementation, and existing files sharded 256 per directory. The model-execution windows were simulated as 5 ms or 20 ms sleeps; all keys were hits. `HIT step` is the first simulated scheduler step where a request group returned HIT and could initiate promotion.

The table reports step-1 HIT fraction and mean/median first-HIT step across request groups and measured runs. Brackets give the minimum and maximum observed first-HIT step. Sample counts are per configuration; 16K configurations used 10 runs, most 64K configurations used 4 runs, and 64 groups at 5 ms used 10 runs.

| Keys | Groups × keys/group | Step | Runs | Pre-PR: Step-1 HIT | Pre-PR: mean / median HIT step [range] | This PR: Step-1 HIT | This PR: mean / median HIT step [range] |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 16K | 16 × 1,024 | 5 ms | 10 | 0% | 12.50 / 13.0 [9–14] | 0% | 6.51 / 6.5 [2–13] |
| 16K | 16 × 1,024 | 20 ms | 10 | 0% | 3.70 / 4.0 [3–4] | 23% [19–25] | 2.20 / 2.0 [1–4] |
| 16K | 64 × 256 | 5 ms | 10 | 0% | 12.50 / 12.0 [10–15] | 0% [0–2] | 6.82 / 7.0 [1–16] |
| 16K | 64 × 256 | 20 ms | 10 | 0% | 3.40 / 3.0 [3–4] | 26% [22–30] | 2.17 / 2.0 [1–4] |
| 64K | 16 × 4,096 | 5 ms | 4 | 0% | 37.75 / 38.5 [35–39] | 0% | 19.77 / 20.5 [5–32] |
| 64K | 16 × 4,096 | 20 ms | 4 | 0% | 12.00 / 12.0 [11–13] | 0% | 6.55 / 7.0 [2–11] |
| 64K | 64 × 1,024 | 5 ms | 10 | 0% | 41.10 / 41.0 [38–44] | 0% | 22.10 / 22.5 [3–40] |
| 64K | 64 × 1,024 | 20 ms | 4 | 0% | 12.00 / 12.0 [12–12] | 0% | 7.27 / 7.0 [2–12] |

The mean reflects aggregate waiting across groups; the median reflects a typical group's wait. The ranges show that some groups still resolve much later than the typical group.

This replay isolates result-publication timing; it does not run the full scheduler, allocate primary-tier slots, or execute promotion transfers. Its step duration is simulated, so these results are directional and are not a serving-throughput claim. Absolute wall-clock timings varied. The scratch replay harness is not part of this PR.

No model evaluation was run because this change affects lookup-result publication timing, not model outputs or accuracy. No end-to-end serving benchmark was run.

## Details

The worker still receives the step's accumulated keys at `flush()` and groups them by `req_id`. Previously, it collected results from every group and posted one combined result batch after the last group completed. The new code posts each group's results immediately after fully consuming that group's `batch_lookup()` output. This removes the result-publication wait between independent groups; it does not start the worker earlier or parallelize the group lookups.

I found no open PR for this exact result-publication change. Related #61292 moves Mooncake connector lookups to the input thread, and #62615 protects primary-tier hits during promotion; both address different paths. #23622 is a non-merge PoC for different connector lookup semantics.

AI assistance was used. The human submitter is responsible for reviewing and defending the change.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][KV Offload][P2P] Clean up both roles on request finish
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fix a small but meaningful P2P lifecycle bug in the documented `remote_kv_source` + `remote_decoder` combination. When the upstream source and downstream decoder use different peer sessions, `on_request_finished()` returns after finishing the source-side consumer session, leaving the decoder-side `_kv_to_session` entry until session teardown and potentially delaying server-round cleanup; these stale entries accumulate on long-lived peers.

## Claims

- Finish the source and destination roles independently for dual-role requests.
- Remove the destination request from `_kv_to_session` when the request finishes.
- Avoid calling `finish_request` twice when both roles use the same session and request ID.

## Validation

<details>
<summary>Test commands</summary>

```bash
python -m pytest -q tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/test_manager.py
python -m pytest -q tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/test_sessions.py
python -m pytest -q tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering
pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/manager.py \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/test_manager.py
```

- The added regression test fails on `upstream/main` because the decoder-side
  session is skipped by the early return, and passes with this change.
- `test_manager.py`: 118 passed
- `test_sessions.py`: 150 passed
- `tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering`: 652 passed, 1 skipped
- Pre-commit checks: passed

</details>

## Details

`on_request_finished()` previously selected the source request ID first. With `remote_kv_source` present, it finished the source-side session and returned, so a legal dual-role request never removed its decoder-side `_kv_to_session` entry or finished the session serving that request.

The cleanup now handles both roles independently. The existing `P2PSession.finish_request()` path still performs the client and server role cleanup; the manager only routes each role to the correct session and suppresses duplicate cleanup when both roles share the same session and request ID.

No open PR covering this lifecycle bug was found.

---

commits.pr_title: [Feature] Support batch invariance for ShortConv (LFM2) models
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fix #61319. LFM2 models (`Lfm2ForCausalLM`, `Lfm2MoeForCausalLM`) can't use batch-invariant mode: with `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` the engine refuses to start with `RuntimeError: VLLM batch_invariant mode is not supported for SHORT_CONV_ATTN.` That leaves them without the documented way to get reproducible greedy outputs. This PR lets `SHORT_CONV_ATTN` declare batch invariance. `PLE_SHORT_CONV_ATTN` stays opted out.

## Claims

- LFM2 models start and are batch-invariant under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`. `LiquidAI/LFM2-8B-A1B` passes the full `tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py` suite (22/22) on an A40.
- The symptom in #61319 (round 0 of repeated `generate()` calls differs from later rounds) goes away in batch-invariant mode, with prefix caching on.
- No change when `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT` is unset.

## Validation

A40 (SM86), official image `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-39983a5e` (no upstream changes to the touched files between that commit and this branch's base). Probe: 8 prompts × 128 greedy tokens, 4 `generate()` rounds on one engine, then each prompt alone. Counts are prompts (out of 8) whose token ids differ. The `enforce_eager` / no-prefix-cache rows and the 22-test suite ran with an env-gated copy of the same one-line opt-in. The rest ran with this branch's file installed.

| model | config | round 0 vs rounds 1–3 | rounds 1–3 | batched vs alone |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| LFM2-8B-A1B | main, default | 8 | 0 | 8 |
| LFM2-8B-A1B | main, `enable_prefix_caching=False` | 0 | 0 | 6 |
| LFM2-8B-A1B | main, `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` | engine fails to start | | |
| LFM2-8B-A1B | this PR, `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` | **0** | **0** | **0** |
| LFM2-8B-A1B | this PR, BI + `enforce_eager` | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| LFM2-8B-A1B | this PR, BI + `enable_prefix_caching=False` | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| LFM2-1.2B | main, default | 2 | 0 | 3 |
| LFM2-1.2B | this PR, `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` | **0** | **0** | **0** |

Upstream BI suite with this change:

```bash
VLLM_TEST_MODEL=LiquidAI/LFM2-8B-A1B pytest -v tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py
# 22 passed in 1057s (FLASH_ATTN / FLEX_ATTENTION / TRITON_ATTN)
VLLM_TEST_MODEL=LiquidAI/LFM2-1.2B pytest -v "tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py::test_v1_generation_is_deterministic_across_batch_sizes_with_needle[default-FLASH_ATTN]"
# 1 passed in 35s
```

## Details

**Why #61319 happens.** LFM2 runs with prefix caching on by default (`mamba_cache_mode=align`, block size 16). From round 1 on, any prompt with a full block gets a cache hit, so the first prefill step shrinks (92 → 76 tokens in my probe, where only the 17-token prompt hits). Without batch invariance, kernel selection depends on batch shape. Every sequence in that step then moves by a few ULPs, and near-tied argmaxes flip later. In my runs, two warm rounds never disagreed. With prefix caching on but no prompt long enough to hit, all rounds match. This is the documented "no bitwise reproducibility by default" behavior, and the documented fix is batch-invariant mode, which LFM2 couldn't use. Setting `CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=:16:8 CUBLASLT_WORKSPACE_SIZE=1`, as #61440 does, still leaves 2/8 prompts differing, because this isn't run-to-run atomics.

**Why ShortConv qualifies.** `causal_conv1d_fn` (prefill) and `causal_conv1d_update` (decode) compute each output token from that sequence's own `L_cache` window plus its conv-state slot. There is no reduction across sequences and no split depending on batch size. The rest of the layer is `in_proj`/`out_proj`, which already go through the batch-invariant linear path, plus elementwise gating.

**Scope and limitations.**
- `PLE_SHORT_CONV_ATTN` (Qwen4Exp's dilated conv) inherits from `ShortConvAttentionBackend`. It is explicitly kept at `False`: it uses its own packing path, and I couldn't validate it.
- All runs used Model Runner V2 (the default). The check is shared with V1 through `get_mamba_attn_backend`, but V1 wasn't run.
- Spec decoding under batch invariance and LFM2-VL weren't tested.
- Only Ampere (SM86) was tested.
- I didn't add an end-to-end LFM2 line to CI. If you want one, `VLLM_TEST_MODEL=LiquidAI/LFM2-1.2B ... -k FLASH_ATTN` on the needle test costs ~35 s per variant, and I'm happy to add it.

**Not a duplicate.** The only PR linked to #61319 is #61440. It forces deterministic cuBLAS/cuDNN settings globally, which doesn't address this (see above), and its diff currently spans 891 files. I searched open PRs for `supports_batch_invariance`, `SHORT_CONV_ATTN`/ShortConv, and LFM2 batch invariance. #45819 (GDN) and the Mamba2 BI PRs touch other backends only.

---

commits.pr_title: [Fast Start] Support online FP8 and CUTLASS NVFP4 weight-cache restarts
commits.pr_body:
## Overview Allow the weight-cache daemon to reuse online FP8/MXFP8 linear weights and ModelOpt NVFP4 CUTLASS MoE weights across engine restarts. Related to #56049; this covers a subset of its quantization roadmap. ## Claims - Restore online quantization runtime state without quantizing or transforming shared weights again. FP8 is limited to CUTLASS; MXFP8 requires the selected kernel's pre-processed-weight capability. Requantization from serialized checkpoints and online MoE remain excluded. - Preserve the unpadded CUTLASS FP8 output width when IPC loading skips weight post-processing. - Restore ModelOpt NVFP4 CUTLASS MoE kernels without multiplying activation scales into shared weight scales a second time. ## Validation Current head `35711168b0135573234bbaa4bd8f9e8fe32647e8` includes main `914d61fc538a84e8487cb16fe8241a70f6f4bf9e`. October 29 agent-run validation after resolving the inherited online-FP8 import conflict with upstream #60163. The merge retains both CUTLASS and Humming imports, the upstream processed-dimension metadata, and upstream rejection of the unsupported Humming per-token/channel path. It adds no Humming IPC capability. | Check | Exact-head result | |---|---| | `online-units` | 108 passed, 685 deselected, 14 warnings in 98.42s (0:01:38) | | `online-models` | 4 passed, 30 warnings in 305.90s (0:05:05) | | `nvfp4-model` | 1 passed, 18 warnings in 99.83s (0:01:39) | | Full feature-file and commit hooks | Passed, including mypy and ruff | Runtime: NVIDIA B300, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, process-local CUDA 13.4 compatibility libraries. The two stable-libtorch extensions are from the official CUDA 13.0 wheel for main `914d61fc538a84e8487cb16fe8241a70f6f4bf9e`, checked against wheel RECORD hashes and linked only into task worktrees. The shared venv and host driver were unchanged. This does not validate the full upstream PyTorch 2.14 dependency matrix. Full-model checks use TP1, BF16, eager mode, CUTLASS and TRITON_ATTN, with the existing batch-invariant exact greedy-output comparisons. Each completed case checks ordinary load, missing-daemon fallback, IPC and a second IPC load; both IPC loads forbid fallback. commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Keep default max_tokens in rendered sampling_params
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

In scale-out serving, `/v1/chat/completions/render` and `/v1/completions/render` with `max_tokens` 16 return `sampling_params` without `max_tokens`, so `/inference/v1/generate` produces 700 (chat) and 40943 (completions) tokens instead of 16; a `/v1/completions/render` request without `max_tokens` defaults to 16 and takes the same path. `SamplingParams` omits fields equal to their defaults, and generate reads the absent key as not sent. `GenerateRequest` now writes `max_tokens` back into the dumped `sampling_params` when the request set it.

Fixes #65388

## Claims

- Render → generate with `max_tokens` 16 stops at 16 tokens with `length` on chat and completions, instead of 700 and 40943 tokens.
- `/v1/completions/render` with `max_tokens` omitted or `null` returns `max_tokens` 16, and generate stops at 16 tokens as coupled `/v1/completions` does, instead of 40943.
- `/v1/chat/completions/render` with `max_completion_tokens` 16, `/v1/messages/render` with `max_tokens` 16 and `/v1/responses/render` with `max_output_tokens` 16 return `max_tokens` 16 instead of leaving it out.
- No change for a generate body that omits `max_tokens`: its dump still omits the key, and generate applies the server default.

## Validation

Environment: vLLM main `66360a5cd0` (2026-11-03) and this branch `17a2bcd142`, Python 3.12.14, torch 2.13.0+cu132, msgspec 0.21.1, render server on CPU, engine on 1x RTX A6000, Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B at temperature 0.

No model eval: the change adds the `max_tokens` key to the serialized request body; sampling under a given limit is unchanged.
The new tests run in the `Entrypoints Integration (API Server)` CI step.

## Details

**Root cause.** `SamplingParams` is a `msgspec.Struct` with `omit_defaults=True` and `max_tokens` default 16, so `GenerateRequest.model_dump()`, which render returns, leaves out `max_tokens` when it is 16. Generate's `is_sampling_param_provided("max_tokens")` checks the keys of the raw `sampling_params` dict, so `serve_tokens` treats the absent key as not sent and replaces it with the `get_max_tokens` server default. `CompletionRequest.max_tokens` defaults to 16 and `normalize_null_max_tokens` maps `null` to it, so completions requests without `max_tokens` take the same path.

**Fix.** A wrap `model_serializer` on `GenerateRequest` writes `sampling_params.max_tokens` back after the normal dump when `is_sampling_param_provided("max_tokens")` is True and the key is missing. In-process requests (render) count every field as provided; a body parsed without `max_tokens` dumps unchanged.

**Related PRs.**
- #42329 — added `is_sampling_param_provided` and the server-side `max_tokens` default in `serve_tokens`. It introduced the fallback that the absent key triggers.
- #35684 — added `_serialize_msgspec`, which dumps `SamplingParams` with `msgspec.to_builtins`. It introduced the dump that leaves out default fields.


Only `max_tokens` is written back: `serve_tokens` is the only caller of `is_sampling_param_provided`, and other omitted defaults (`top_k` 0, `min_tokens` 0) parse back to the same value.
Generate cannot fix this on its side: once the key is absent, a resolved 16 and an unsent limit look the same.
The fix is on the serializing side, so a render server on main talking to a generate server with this PR still drops 16.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Pass the caller's prompt_token_ids to the chat derender parser
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Non-streaming chat derender passes the parser only `generate_response.prompt_token_ids`, which generate sets only when `return_token_ids` is on. In the usual render → generate → derender flow the parser therefore never sees the prompt. Since #61857, parsers read the prompt to tell whether it already closed reasoning, so they misclassify the output here. This affects response template parsers as well as Qwen3. For example, with Qwen3 and `continue_final_message` after a closed `</think>`, the answer comes back as `reasoning`.

## Claims

- The parser gets the engine's `prompt_token_ids` when the generate response has them and falls back to the caller's `prompt_token_ids` otherwise. The engine's take precedence because the caller may send only a suffix.
- `DerenderChatRequest.prompt_token_ids` and `derenderer.md` now say that chat derender with a parser needs the full prompt IDs in both modes. The docs also note that a suffix starting after the last reasoning marker still misparses, the same as sending no IDs.

## Validation

New E2E test through the render server (`Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --reasoning-parser qwen3`, no GPU):

CPU is enough here. Derender only decodes and parses token IDs that were already generated, and the render server loads just the tokenizer.

```
$ pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender.py::test_e2e_parser_uses_caller_prompt_token_ids
# without the fix:  AssertionError: assert None == ' is 42.'
# with the fix:     PASSED
```

Response template parser given a suffix (`test_prompt_suffix_parses_like_full_prompt_or_no_prompt`, a two-turn prompt whose generation prompt opens reasoning, output `plan<channel|>answer<turn|>`):

| prompt IDs given to the parser | reasoning | content |
| --- | --- | --- |
| none (before this PR) | `None` | `plan<channel\|>answer` |
| full prompt | `plan` | `answer` |
| suffix from the start anchor | `plan` | `answer` |
| suffix past the anchor, with the reasoning opener | `plan` | `answer` |
| suffix past the reasoning opener | `None` | `plan<channel\|>answer` |

A suffix parses like the full prompt while it still holds the opener and like no prompt after that. It is never worse than the empty prefix the parser had before.

The same holds through derender with a real checkpoint: `google/gemma-4-E2B-it`'s response template (`--reasoning-parser hf`), 15 suffix lengths (last 1–12, 16, 24 and 32 IDs) on 4 prompts (opening reasoning, mid-reasoning, closed reasoning, and the model writing its own). Every suffix parsed like either the full prompt or no prompt. For example, a prompt ending in `<|channel>thought\n` parses correctly from the last 3 IDs, the first that include `<|channel>`.

```
$ pytest tests/parser/test_response_template.py
75 passed
$ pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender.py tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_stream.py
214 passed, 1 xfailed
```

## Details

- #61857 made the parsers honor a prompt-closed reasoning block in non-streaming parse and reasoning token counts, but didn't touch derender.
- Not a duplicate: no open PR changes this call (searched "derender prompt_token_ids" and "derender reasoning"). #64041's reasoning counts build on it and #63357 touches the next line, so this should go in first.
- AI assistance (Claude Code) was used. I reviewed the changed lines and ran the tests above.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][Model] DeepSeek V4/V4.1 Vision: encode a call's images in packed passes
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

DeepSeek V4 and V4.1 Vision run the ViT and aligner once per image, even when a call carries several images. This PR encodes a call's images in one packed pass through `forward_packed`, the path V4.1's encoder CUDA graphs already use. No new flag.

## Claims

- Across 54 multi-image encoder calls, encoding is 2.0–2.6× faster on V4 and 1.6–2.1× faster on V4.1, on two H100 machines. No call got more than 2% slower.
- With the real V4 checkpoint on 2× B200, median TTFT drops from 367–378 ms to 271 ms for 4-image requests at concurrency 1, and from 914–959 ms to 548 ms on VisionArena at concurrency 16.
- MMMU-Pro scores match main within run-to-run noise (862 correct vs 861 / 860 on main; multi-image 75 vs 74 / 75) on a direct-answer setup described below. Startup KV-cache capacity is effectively unchanged in the tested configuration.
- Cost: peak encoder memory per call grows with the number of images, up to about 1.7 GB more on V4 and 2.0 GB on V4.1 for a 32-image call. Output is not bit-identical to the per-image path, and the PR disagrees with main on more answers than main does with itself (200 vs 96 of 1730), in both directions.

## Validation

**Encoder.** H100, FlashAttention, real tower weights, random patches at VisionArena sizes. 54 multi-image calls, 3 rounds, shuffled call order, alternating arm order. [Benchmark script](https://gist.github.com/subhashpolisetti/0f74ea61d8c3dbd32d7e5ef49a235f85). ms is the median across calls, and peak is the largest across calls, measured above the allocation just before the call. Per-image → this PR:

| images per call | V4 ms | V4 peak MiB | V4.1 ms | V4.1 peak MiB |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 59.6 → 29.9 | 141 → 142 | 59.6 → 30.1 | 120 → 189 |
| 4 | 119.2 → 47.0 | 79 → 281 | 118.8 → 57.9 | 132 → 371 |
| 8 | 237.6 → 88.8 | 87 → 450 | 236.3 → 101.8 | 110 → 530 |
| 16 | 483.0 → 172.2 | 105 → 883 | 481.6 → 219.2 | 148 → 1133 |
| 32 | 962.9 → 328.4 | 144 → 1832 | 961.2 → 418.6 | 190 → 2191 |
| **all 54 calls, total** | **2.61×** | | **2.10×** | |

The first version of this PR capped a pass at 8 images. In the same container, the capped version gave similar speedups of 2.55× and 2.08×, with lower peak memory on 16+ image calls.

**Accuracy.** MMMU-Pro standard (10 options), 1730 questions, 138 with more than one image. Real `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp`, 2× B200, TP2 + EP, FP8 KV cache, block size 256, greedy, thinking off, no speculative decoding, `max_tokens=32`, concurrency 32. Runs in the order main → this PR → main, with a fresh server each time and 0 failed requests.

| | main | this PR | main again |
|---|---|---|---|
| correct, all 1730 | 861 | 862 | 860 |
| correct, 138 multi-image | 74 | 75 | 75 |

| answers that changed | total | multi-image | right → wrong | wrong → right |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main vs main again | 96 | 7 | 21 | 20 |
| this PR vs main | 200 | 13 | 47 | 48 |
| this PR vs main again | 196 | 11 | 50 | 52 |

Scoring takes the option letter only from the start of the reply or after "answer is"; anything else counts as no answer. That leaves 131 / 136 / 135 replies with no answer (main / PR / main again), mostly step-by-step explanations at the 32-token limit, and the same 2 multi-image replies in every run. Finish reasons were not saved, so I can't confirm each one hit the limit. This is a direct-answer setup, not a full MMMU-Pro evaluation, so the scores aren't comparable with published results.

Most changed answers are single-image questions. Under concurrency, images from different requests share an encoder call, so they also take the packed path.

Encoder-level error against an FP32 per-image reference, on 3 multi-image calls built from 2 real photos, is unchanged from the capped version:

| model | per-image | packed | packed vs per-image |
|---|---|---|---|
| V4 | 3.29 / 3.84 / 5.47% | 3.28 / 3.85 / 5.47% | 0.39 / 1.33 / 0.16% |
| V4.1 | 2.19 / 2.03 / 2.02% | 2.19 / 2.03 / 2.01% | 0.04 / 0.16 / 0.24% |

**KV cache.** Startup KV-cache size on the same servers: 202,321 and 202,340 tokens on main, 202,335 with this PR.

**Serving.** Same servers, run after MMMU-Pro, 0 failed requests. Values are main / main again → this PR, one run each.

| workload | requests | median TTFT ms | p99 TTFT ms | req/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4 images, concurrency 1 | 100 | 378 / 367 → 271 | 413 / 431 → 311 | 2.51 / 2.56 → 3.44 |
| VisionArena, concurrency 16 | 500 | 959 / 914 → 548 | 9608 / 1012 → 652 | 10.0 / 16.0 → 24.6 |

The first main VisionArena run had a slow tail and lower throughput than the second, so I'd compare throughput and p99 against the second. The median is similar in both.

**Tests.** The unit test is removed, as requested. It compared packed and per-image output on H100 and passed there. Accuracy is covered by the MMMU-Pro run above.

**Revision.** All runs used the `190df0b900` main wheel with this PR's files on top. The PR is rebased on `bca1bc6516`, and the commits in between don't touch these files. The speedup depends on the machine: my first H100 run gave 2.01× and 1.63× (per-image 44.9 ms for 2 images, capped version, which runs within 2% of the uncapped one in the same container), this one 2.61× and 2.10× (59.6 ms). The per-image path is bound by kernel launches, so it is sensitive to the host. On one H100, the per-image path of the two main wheels (`2abde627d9`, `190df0b900`) differs by about 4%, close to the 2.6% between two runs of the same wheel, so the gap is mostly the machine.

<details><summary>Commands</summary>

```bash
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp --port 8000 --seed 0 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 --enable-expert-parallel --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 256 \
  --max-model-len 32768 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": 8}'

vllm bench serve --backend openai-chat --endpoint /v1/chat/completions \
  --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp --port 8000 --seed 0 \
  --dataset-name hf --dataset-path lmarena-ai/VisionArena-Chat --hf-split train \
  --hf-output-len 8 --num-prompts 500 --max-concurrency 16

vllm bench serve --backend openai-chat --endpoint /v1/chat/completions \
  --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp --port 8000 --seed 0 \
  --dataset-name random-mm --random-input-len 32 --random-output-len 8 \
  --random-mm-base-items-per-request 4 --random-mm-limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": 4, "video": 0}' \
  --random-mm-bucket-config "{(768, 1024, 1): 0.4, (434, 600, 1): 0.3, (512, 512, 1): 0.3}" \
  --num-prompts 100 --max-concurrency 1
```

MMMU-Pro prompt: the question, then the options as `A. ...`, then "Answer with the option's letter from the given choices directly.", with the question's images before the text. The answer is the option letter at the start of the reply or after "answer is"; any other reply counts as no answer.

</details>

## Details

`_process_image_input` loops over images, so each one pays for its own kernel launches through 32 blocks. `forward_packed` runs them together, with per-image attention through `cu_seqlens`.

- **Scope.** Packing applies only to FlashAttention with two or more images. One image gains nothing from it, and I didn't measure other backends, so both keep the per-image path. `run_dp_sharded_vision_tower` and the graph manager's eager fallback are unchanged.
- **Memory.** Peak encoder memory grows with the images in a call. The startup profile run encodes the maximum items per batch, and the KV-cache size above did not change.
- **Rounding.** Each matmul sees more rows, so packed output rounds differently. Together with batching, that can change generated answers; the evaluation above shows more disagreements with no net change in scores, but does not separate the two causes.
- **Not tested.** V4.1 serving and MMMU-Pro (encoder results only), AMD (it shares the helper), thinking mode, DSpark speculative decoding, and MMMU-Pro with a larger output budget.
- **Overlaps.** #62802 has since merged and this branch still merges cleanly with main. #57985 touches some of these files and merges cleanly too. It removes the patch dtype cast, which is why `merge_mask` takes its dtype from the aligner weights. #58782 conflicts in `amd/vl_model.py`. #64435 and #57872 also target V4.1 but don't touch these files.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Kernel] hadacore: fix skipped wait_group on partial-chunk warp for odd row counts (#63514)
commits.pr_body:
Fixes #63514

### Problem
When using INT4 per-token-head KV cache (`--kv-cache-dtype int4_per_token_head`), `reshape_and_cache_int4` rotates Key and Value tensors via `hadacore_transform`. 

For `head_dim = 256`, `num_chunks` is 2. When the row count (`num_tokens * num_kv_heads_per_rank`) is odd, the last warp receives only 1 chunk (`real_num_chunks = 1`).

`diff_num_chunks` was calculated as:
```cpp
int64_t diff_num_chunks = real_num_chunks - num_chunks; // 1 - 2 = -1
```
Because `diff_num_chunks` was negative, `switch(k + diff_num_chunks)` evaluated to `-1`. Since the switch statement only contains `case 0..31` and had no `default:` fallback, it silently skipped `cp.async.wait_group` completely. 

The warp proceeded to read shared memory before the asynchronous DMA copy completed, causing:
1. Silent data corruption (relative errors up to 10^36).
2. Intermittent `CUDA illegal memory access` crashes during prefill.

### Fix
1. Correct the difference to `num_chunks - real_num_chunks` so `k + diff_num_chunks` maps to the intended wait barrier count (`wait_group 0` for the single tail chunk).
2. Add `default: asm volatile("cp.async.wait_group 0;\n"); break;` so an unhandled case can never silently skip synchronization.
3. Add parameterized unit test in `tests/kernels/quantization/test_hadacore.py` covering odd and large row counts (`num_rows in [1, 17, 53, 65, 165, 173, 257, 513, 1025, 4097, 8193]`).

### Validation
Verified on NVIDIA A100-PCIE-40GB:
- **Full range test (`N = 1` to `512`):**
  - Unpatched `main` (`2c880f1e`): 39 failing row counts (all odd), errors up to 10^36.
  - With this fix: **0 failures out of 512** (100% bit-exact match against float64 reference).
- Tested small (`N <= 128`), medium (`128 < N <= 513`), and large (`1024 <= N <= 8193`) shapes across both odd and even counts.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction Script</summary>

```python
import math
import torch
from vllm import _custom_ops as ops

D = 256
H = torch.ones(1, 1, dtype=torch.float64, device="cuda")
while H.shape[0] < D:
    H = torch.cat([torch.cat([H, H], 1), torch.cat([H, -H], 1)], 0)
H = H / math.sqrt(D)

bad = []
for n in range(1, 513):
    torch.manual_seed(n)
    x = torch.randn(n, D, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
    y = ops.hadacore_transform(x.clone(), inplace=True)
    ref = (x.double() @ H).to(torch.bfloat16)

    rel_err = ((y.double() - ref.double()).abs().max() / ref.double().abs().max()).item()
    if rel_err > 2e-2:
        bad.append((n, f"{rel_err:.2e}"))

print(f"Tested 1..512 row counts: {len(bad)} failures")
if bad:
    print("Sample failing counts:", bad[:10])
```
</details>

commits.pr_title: [Mamba][MRV2] Plan Triton ReplaySSM decode on the GPU and support Model Runner V2
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Triton ReplaySSM (`--use-replayssm --mamba-backend triton`, #48018) was rejected on Model Runner V2: it planned each decode step on the CPU from a per-request ring origin that only the V1 input batch tracked. This PR moves that planning to the GPU using per-cache-slot ring counters (the same trackers the FlashInfer ReplaySSM backend from #52506 already uses), which enables MRV2 and deletes the runner-side plumbing.

## Claims

- Triton ReplaySSM now runs on MRV2, with logprob parity against the non-ReplaySSM baseline on both runners, with and without mamba `align` prefix caching.
- No runner changes are needed for V2; the V1-only `replayssm_decode_base_cpu` plumbing (in `CommonAttentionMetadata`, the V1 input batch, and the V1 runner) is removed.
- The per-step CPU planning in the Mamba metadata builder (about 70 lines, plus two `.tolist()` → H2D copies each step) is replaced by one small GPU kernel per KV-cache group per step.

## Validation

All runs were on GB200 (one GPU) with `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-4B-BF16`.

| Test | V1 | V2 |
|---|---|---|
| `test_replayssm_decode_matches_baseline` (Triton) | pass | pass |
| `test_replayssm_prefix_caching_matches_baseline` (Triton, align mode, asserts prefix-cache hits > 0) | pass | pass |
| Same two V2 tests with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` | n/a | pass |

```bash
pytest -v -s tests/v1/e2e/test_replayssm_decode.py \
  -k "(test_replayssm_decode_matches_baseline or test_replayssm_prefix_caching_matches_baseline) and not tp2"
```

Unit and kernel tests also pass: `tests/kernels/mamba/test_replayssm_plan.py` (new), `tests/kernels/mamba/test_replayssm_standard_decode_mamba2.py`, `tests/v1/attention/test_replayssm_metadata_builder.py`, `tests/model_executor/test_replayssm_warmup.py`, the tracker-sharing test in `tests/v1/worker/test_utils.py`, and the ReplaySSM config test in `tests/test_config.py` (168 tests).

The new kernel test drives the planner through whole decode runs and checks every step against the removed CPU formula. It covers none and align modes, buffer lengths 4, 6 and 16, align block sizes 16, 32 and 64, and prompts that end mid-block or on a block boundary. It also covers rows planned independently, padding rows, re-anchoring after a prefill reset (preemption-resume), and a stale slot counter at a prefix-cache block boundary.

Not run: the TP2 parity tests (V1 only, unchanged) and the FlashInfer ReplaySSM e2e tests (that path is unchanged apart from sharing tracker setup with Triton layers). CI's `replayssm-e2e` step (2×H100) covers both.

## Details

**Planning.** Each Mamba2 layer already gets per-slot `ring_start`/`prev_num_accepted`/`prev_query_len` tensors from `share_replayssm_ring_trackers`, shared within a KV-cache group; this PR extends that to Triton layers. For Triton, `ring_start[slot]` is the number of tokens buffered since the slot's last full-state write. The first ReplaySSM layer of each group calls `plan_replayssm_decode`, which writes that step's `write_pos`/`is_flush` into persistent builder buffers that every layer reads, then advances the counter (resetting it to 0 after a flush). Prefill resets the counters with the existing `reset_replayssm_ring_trackers`. The Triton SSU kernel is unchanged.

**Align mode.** The planner reads the GPU `seq_lens`, which both runners keep in persistent buffers. It restarts the ring on a block's first step and forces a flush on the step that completes a block, so the exact block-boundary state is materialized for prefix caching. That is what the CPU code did with `max(decode_base, block_start)`. Restarting at the block's first step also handles a prefix-cache hit on a reused slot whose counter is left over from a previous request, because such hits always land on a block boundary.

**CUDA graphs.** `write_pos`/`is_flush` were already persistent buffers for FULL graphs; they are now written on the GPU inside the graph instead of being copied in before replay. Padding rows have `NULL_BLOCK_ID` slots and are planned as no-ops.

**Behaviour change.** A one-token final prompt chunk that runs as a decode row (`prefill_to_decode`) now appends to the ring the previous chunk's prefill left empty, like any other decode step, instead of forcing a one-token flush. Both are mathematically equivalent, since the checkpoint is the state before that token. The planner unit test covers this case; the e2e tests don't deliberately trigger it.

**Limitations.** `mamba_cache_mode="all"` with Triton ReplaySSM is not rejected by config but was not handled correctly before this change either (the decode slot changes every block without a ring restart). This PR does not change that.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Watermarking] Skip incomplete opening contexts
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Skip watermarking until the response contains a complete generated-token context, across Gumbel and dual-key Gumbel standard and speculative sampling. Follow-up to the shared padded-opening issue discussed in #58426; that PR adds SynthID and leaves this behavior question separate.

## Claims

- The first `context_width` output tokens use ordinary sampling independently of context deduplication, including draft, recovery, and bonus tokens.
- Detection behavior and PRF mappings are preserved.

## Validation

- `../vllm_fork/.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/watermarking -q`: 134 passed, 61 accelerator-only tests skipped on macOS.
- All applicable pre-commit hooks passed, including mypy and test tethering.
- Rescored all 23 pre-change golden generations with the default detector: scores, p-values, scored-token counts, and decisions match within the existing 1e-9 tolerance.
- GPU engine validation remains pending. Retained model outputs establish detection compatibility only; they do not evaluate generation with this patch.

## Details

Response-local contexts are padded with -1 before enough output tokens exist. With a fixed key, this reuses the same opening watermark randomness across prompts and can reduce opening diversity. The patch combines an incomplete-context mask with the existing sampling masks; it adds no host read or device synchronization. Prompt tokens remain excluded from the seed under every deduplication setting; `all` still searches the prompt for repeated contexts.

Submitted detection text may be a fragment and need not start at the generation boundary, so this PR does not change detector preprocessing or add detector options. On new full responses, the unwatermarked opening positions can dilute the detector signal. Generation can diverge beyond the opening because later tokens depend on earlier choices.

Goldens reflect the new generation behavior. Engine reproducibility tests now pin request seeds because openings use ordinary randomness. The repetitive-fixture confidence guard allows a p-value ratio up to 0.6 rather than 0.5: one updated fixture has ratio 0.514 while remaining below the unchanged detection threshold.

AI assistance: implementation, tests, and this description were prepared with Codex (OpenAI).

commits.pr_title: [Spec Decode] Support XPress + Acceptance Estimator
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Adaptive verification does nothing for XPress today. The acceptance estimator is created, but XPress never feeds it, so the AV budget reads an uninitialised confidence buffer and prunes every draft after the first. Turning AV on makes XPress about 3x slower than leaving it off.

This wires XPress to the estimator, using the logits the draft tokens are sampled from.

## Performance

One H100, Qwen3-8B with the XPress b16 draft, 15 draft tokens, greedy, prefix caching off, SPEED-Bench throughput_1K shuffled with seed 42. AIPerf runs a concurrency grid of 1, 8, 32, 64 and 128 with 30 s cells and 3 trials. Throughput is output tokens in the steady window of each cell, median over the trials.

![Throughput-interactivity pareto](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tomasruizt/vllm/assets/xpress-av/xpress-av-pareto.png)

AV off is the same curve on both commits, within 1%, which is also the spread between trials. On main, AV on verifies one token per step and loses 26% to 71% of throughput. Here it costs 8% at c1 and c8, and from c32 up it is faster than AV off: the budget verifies fewer drafts (AL 3.0 to 3.3 against 3.5 to 3.7), which makes each target step cheaper and more than pays for the shorter accept run.

<details>
<summary>Per-cell results</summary>

| c | AV off tok/s | AV on, main | AV on, this PR | AL off | AL on, main | AL on, this PR |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 408 | 118 | 375 | 3.78 | 1.00 | 3.50 |
| 8 | 2,494 | 812 | 2,291 | 3.54 | 1.01 | 3.17 |
| 32 | 4,468 | 2,227 | 5,389 | 3.67 | 1.01 | 3.04 |
| 64 | 4,471 | 2,856 | 6,242 | 3.58 | 1.01 | 3.19 |
| 128 | 4,967 | 3,665 | 6,810 | 3.68 | 1.00 | 3.32 |

</details>

<details>
<summary>Server and client commands</summary>

```bash
VLLM_ADAPTIVE_VERIFICATION_PROFILE_CONTEXT_LEN=2048 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-8B --served-model-name qwen \
  --max-model-len 16384 --max-num-seqs 256 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 --no-enable-prefix-caching --disable-uvicorn-access-log \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8640 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dflash","model":"UIUC-SSAIL/Qwen3-8B-XPress-b16","num_speculative_tokens":15,"enable_adaptive_verification":true}'
```

```yaml
# aiperf profile --config sweep.yaml, one invocation per AV mode
sweep: {type: grid, parameters: {phases.profiling.concurrency: [1, 8, 32, 64, 128]}}
multi_run: {num_runs: 3, cooldown_seconds: 5}
benchmark:
  endpoint:
    url: http://127.0.0.1:8640
    type: chat
    streaming: true
    use_server_token_count: true
    extra: {temperature: 0, max_completion_tokens: 1024, chat_template_kwargs: {enable_thinking: false}}
  datasets:
    - {name: main, type: file, format: speed_bench_throughput_1k, path: throughput_1k.jsonl, sampling: shuffle, random_seed: 42}
  phases:
    - {name: profiling, type: concurrency, duration: 30, grace_period: 30, concurrency: 1}
```

</details>

## Claims

- AV on no longer collapses: acceptance length 1.08 to 7.26 on the e2e case (7.39 with AV off), acceptance rate 0.005 to 0.42.
- Throughput goes from a 26-71% loss on main to an 8% cost at c1 and c8, and a 21-40% gain from c32 up, because the budget spends fewer verified drafts per step.
- Accuracy is unchanged: GSM8K 0.885 with AV on and off, 1,319 questions.
- AV off is untouched. The draft is bit-identical, and both commits measure within 1% in every cell.

## Validation

The existing Qwen3-8B + XPress b16 case gets an `enable_adaptive_verification` variant in `tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/acceptance_rates/xpress/test_xpress.py`. It runs in the nightly XPress job, so no buildkite change is needed.

| commit | result |
|---|---|
| main `f9db1756e9` | `1 failed in 647.96s`, `acceptance_rate=0.005`, `acceptance_len=1.078` |
| this PR | `2 passed in 113.91s`, AV off `0.43 / 7.39`, AV on `0.42 / 7.26`, GSM8K `0.885` both |

<details>
<summary>Failure on main</summary>

```
E  AssertionError: method=dflash target=Qwen/Qwen3-8B, draft=UIUC-SSAIL/Qwen3-8B-XPress-b16, eager=False,
   acceptance_rate=0.005, acceptance_len=1.078; expected acceptance_rate >= 0.375
E  assert 0.005191845631765376 >= 0.375
```

</details>

Unit: `pytest -v tests/v1/spec_decode/test_xpress_head.py` gives 4 passed. It covers both `xpress_topc` paths and asserts the draft is unchanged when no logits are requested.

## Details

`draft_token_confidence_probs` is allocated with `torch.empty` and only written by `_maybe_predict_acceptance`. DFlash and DSpark call it, XPress did not, so the AV budget read uninitialised survivals and the estimator never saw a single feature or verdict.

`jacobi_refine_greedy` now returns the logits of its last pass next to the draft ids, and `XPressSpeculator` hands them to the estimator. Both paths return exactly the logits the argmax ran on, the summed bias over the vocabulary or the top-C candidate scores when `xpress_topc` is set. Nothing is computed when AV is off.

The draft is unchanged, so AV now only decides how many draft tokens to verify, which is what it was meant to do.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Preserve SWA null-page offsets after store retry
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

When a CPU offload store is retried after capacity exhaustion, SWA can release a GPU block and reallocate it for another logical position. The offloading scheduler marks the old position as `NULL_BLOCK_ID` but removes it from the source spec, so later pages shift into the wrong positions in the destination CPU chunk and can be loaded back as incorrect KV data.

## Claims

- Preserve the logical page layout of every full SWA chunk in the GPU-to-CPU store spec, including null blocks as placeholders for unreachable pages.
- Prevent store retries from corrupting the mapping between GPU source pages and CPU chunk offsets.
- Add a scheduler regression test with a mocked store failure and SWA block reuse.

## Validation

<details>
<summary>Test command</summary>

```bash
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py \
  -k test_swa_retry_keeps_internal_null_block_in_store_spec -q
```

With the fix:

```text
1 passed, 484 deselected, 14 warnings in 2.94s
```

With the regression test applied to the parent revision:

```text
At index 6 diff: 8 != 0
Right contains one more item: 9
1 failed, 484 deselected, 14 warnings in 2.90s
```

</details>

Without the fix, the generated store spec contains only 8 source pages and skips the internal null page. With the fix, it contains all 9 logical pages with `group_sizes=[9]` and `block_indices=[0]`.

A separate validation with the real `CPUOffloadingManager`, scheduler, offloading handler, and CUDA transfers reproduced the data error before the fix: loading logical pages 7 and 8 returned `[9, -99]` instead of `[8, 9]`. After the fix, the stored chunk was `[0, 8, 9]` and loading logical pages 7 and 8 returned `[8, 9]`.

No model-level evaluation was performed. The V1 KV Connectors GPU CI job is currently disabled, so the regression test was run manually.

## Details

`prepare_store()` can return `None` when all CPU chunks are held by in-flight loads and no chunk is free or evictable. During the retry window, SWA may release a GPU block and reallocate it for another position. The offloading scheduler then marks the old logical position as `NULL_BLOCK_ID`. `_build_store_jobs()` previously dropped that null block when building `GPULoadStoreSpec.block_ids`. The remaining pages were then packed without their original logical offset, although the destination CPU chunk still reserved a slot for every page in the full chunk.

The fix keeps null blocks as placeholders for unreachable pages in the source spec so source and destination chunk offsets remain aligned. Null blocks are excluded from the fence set because block 0 is the permanently reserved GPU null block and is not a live allocation.

Unlike #62932, which bounds secondary-tier loads by CPU capacity, this fixes GPU-to-CPU store page alignment after a retry.

The change is limited to source-spec construction in `OffloadingConnectorScheduler` and one focused regression test. It does not change admission, eviction, retry, or partial-tail behavior.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Scheduler] Don't split a multimodal item when a prefix cache hit ends inside it
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

With `disable_chunked_mm_input`, the scheduler still splits a multimodal item when a prefix cache hit ends inside it and the step has no room for the rest of the item. Models with bidirectional attention over the item then prefill its first part without seeing the rest.

#52306 reported these splits and #52412 and #59721 fixed them, but this path remained.

## Claims

- When a cache hit ends inside a multimodal item, the request waits for a step that can schedule the rest of the item.
- Adds tests for a cache hit inside an image, at the scheduler and end to end.

## Validation

On base `51c6dfd8c`:

```text
pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -k mm_input_chunking                                   # CPU
pytest tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_mm_prefix_lm.py -k cache_hit_inside_image      # L4
```

With the original `scheduler.py`, three of the new checks fail: the request that hit the cache is scheduled 39 tokens into the image, the guard returns 500 tokens for a chunk that starts inside the item, and end to end the 40 image tokens prefilled first differ from the request run alone (320 / 800 elements, max abs diff 8.5e-3). With the fix, all pass.

## Details

Root cause: the guard assumes a chunk never starts inside an item, which does not hold in these cases:

- The same image is followed by a different question. The last block of the image also holds the start of the question, so that block misses and the hit stops inside the image.
- The KV cache runs short. Blocks are reused tail first, so the hit can stop early in the image, leaving most of it.

With the flag on, startup checks that one item fits in a step (`max_num_batched_tokens`), so the request is not starved. A `long_prefill_token_threshold` smaller than the item stalls it, as it already does on main (#62031, #62030).

#62782 changes the same lines; the two combine in either merge order.

No open issue or PR covers this case (checked 2026-11-02).

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Disable CUTLASS FP4 MoE backend on sm_110
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`CutlassExpertsFp4` claims device capability family 110, so NVFP4 MoE auto-selection picks
`VLLM_CUTLASS` on sm_110 (Jetson AGX Thor) and faults in `profile_run` instead of falling
back to Marlin.

110 has been in this predicate since #33417 normalised it from
`has_device_capability((10, 0))`, a `>=` check that sm_110 already passed. That PR was about
SM120 and was tested on an RTX PRO 6000. Doesn't look like 110 was ever tried on Thor.

## Claims

- NVFP4 MoE auto-selection on sm_110 reaches a backend that works instead of one that faults.
- Scoped to the MoE predicate. Dense NVFP4 (`cutlass_scaled_mm_supports_fp4`) is untouched
  and still works on sm_110.
- No behavioural change elsewhere: sm_100 and sm_120 evaluate identically.
- No regression in `tests/kernels/moe/test_cutlass_moe.py`.

## Validation

Jetson AGX Thor, sm_110, 20 SMs, 122.8 GiB unified.

`CutlassExpertsFp4._supports_current_device()` returns True before, False after. Checked
against 837e87e1c5.

Before, serving `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4` (512 experts):

```
Error: Failed to initialize the TMA descriptor 700
RuntimeError: run_fp4_blockwise_scaled_group_mm_sm100,
  csrc/libtorch_stable/quantization/fp4/nvfp4_blockwise_moe_kernel.cu:410,
  Failed to initialize GEMM: status=7 workspace_size=261120
  num_experts=512 M=81920 N=1280 K=2560
```

After, the run gets through load, `profile_run` and KV alloc, then stops at an unrelated QSA
kernel on the same device (#56084). With that one fixed as well it serves: 0 errors, coherent
output at temperature 0.

Ran `test_cutlass_moe.py` on Thor before and after the patch, no failures either time. The
`[nvfp4]` padded-routes case goes from pass to skip, since the backend is no longer offered
on this device.

### Reproducing

You only need an sm_110 device to check the predicate.

The serving runs don't reproduce on stock vLLM. That checkpoint is ~126 GiB and the board has
122.8 GiB, so these runs mmap the 47.7 GiB PLE n-gram table from NVMe instead of holding it
resident. It's a lookup table, never a GEMM operand, so it can't affect which backend gets
picked. No upstream equivalent, #54129 was closed unmerged.

No sm_110 runner in CI, so no test added and everything above was run on hardware.

## Details

**Root cause.** `select_nvfp4_moe_backend` walks an ordered list and takes the first backend
that claims support. `VLLM_CUTLASS` sits above `MARLIN`. sm_90 falls through because it fails
the FP4 check; sm_110 passes and stops there. The fault lands in `profile_run`, after
selection, so there's no retry.

**Scope.** `cutlass_scaled_mm_supports_fp4(110)` is correct for dense, confirmed by calling
`cutlass_scaled_fp4_mm` on device. Only the grouped kernel is broken, so the MoE predicate is
the right place to fix it, not the global helper.

**Tradeoff.** Small shapes do work on CUTLASS here, the 4-expert unit test passes unpatched,
and those now go to Marlin, which is W4A16 and slower on prefill. Taking that: selection
happens once, before shapes are known, and it faults at real MoE sizes. The failure is
shape-dependent too, at 16k context the same call dies in the torch stable-ABI dispatcher
instead of TMA init.

**Why not `--moe-backend marlin`.** It's global, and this checkpoint leaves `mtp.*`
unquantized, so it dies earlier:

```
ValueError: moe_backend='marlin' is not supported for unquantized MoE.   (mtp.py:201)
```

Auto-selection has to be right because the flag can't express per-layer choice.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][LoRA] Account for CLIP CLS rows in LLaVA-NeXT-Video tower mappings
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes item 7 of #61608. With `--enable-tower-connector-lora`, LLaVA-NeXT-Video's `get_mm_lora_token_counts()` counts 576 tower rows per frame, but vLLM's CLIP tower prepends a CLS token, so its LoRA layers actually see 577. The tower LoRA buffer is sized from this count, so encoder profiling overflows it and the engine fails to start:

```
$ vllm serve llava-hf/LLaVA-NeXT-Video-7B-hf --enable-lora --enable-tower-connector-lora
...
  File "vllm/lora/ops/triton_ops/lora_shrink_op.py", line 291, in _lora_shrink
    assert token_lora_mapping.size(0) == M
AssertionError
...
RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed. See root cause above.
```

When startup does pass (e.g. `max_num_batched_tokens=16384`), the runtime mapping is still one row per frame short, so the last rows of each video get the next request's adapter, or none.

The fix adds `tower_tokens_per_frame` in `__init__`, computed with `get_num_image_tokens()` as in `llava_next.py` (577 for CLIP, unchanged for SigLIP), and the hook uses it instead of `patch_grid_length ** 2`. #61799 fixes the same bug in `llava.py`; no open PR touches these counts in `llava_next_video.py`.

## Validation

1x A100 80GB, base 5bf3d9f665, `llava-hf/LLaVA-NeXT-Video-7B-hf`:

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `vllm serve` command above (defaults otherwise) | assert at startup | starts |
| `LLM(...)`, `max_model_len=4096`, `max_num_batched_tokens` 2048 / 8192 | assert at startup | starts |
| `max_num_batched_tokens=16384` (default `max_model_len`), 70-frame + 43-frame video in one batch | assert at runtime | completes |
| no-LoRA requests in a batch with LoRA requests vs. the same batch without LoRA | one request's logprobs change | bit-exact |
| tower LoRA vs. the same adapter merged into the weights, max \|Δlogprob\| | 0.039 | 0.012 |

The last two rows use a random rank-8 adapter on the CLIP layers, with 4 eight-frame videos in one encoder batch and greedy decoding.

All GPU runs above used the first revision (fd4daa1), which computed the same count inside the hook; the review update only moves it to `__init__`.

`pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_llava_next_video.py`: 6 passed on e40576d.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][MRV2][LoRA] Disable KV-sharing fast prefill for LoRA batches
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

MRV2 KV-sharing fast prefill reduces the batch to logits rows while LoRA mappings still describe the full batch, causing incorrect outputs or CUDA illegal memory access. Following review, this PR chooses a batch-level fallback over additional LoRA metadata and graph-capture machinery: batches containing LoRA use regular prefill, while base-only batches retain fast prefill.

## Claims

- LoRA and mixed base/LoRA batches fall back; base-only batches retain fast prefill, including after LoRA requests.
- Removes the previous compact-metadata and graph-capture changes.

## Validation

- CPU mock regression: **1 passed**, with GPU visibility disabled. Verifies LoRA fallback and subsequent base fast-prefill recovery. Worker test file: **53 passed**.
- Local real-weight E2E: CUDA illegal memory access before the fix; passes afterward. Kept outside the repository CI tests.
- Gemma4 E2B on NVIDIA GB10: compile-only, breakable PIECEWISE, and FULL_AND_PIECEWISE each completed **20/20 requests** and **20/20 full-prefill controls**, with finite logits and correct fallback routing.
- Pre-commit and `git diff --check` pass.

<details>
<summary>Test commands</summary>

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py   -k test_fast_prefill_skips_lora_batches

.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py
```

</details>

## Details

`FastPrefillHelper.prepare()` returns `None` when `num_active_loras > 0`, preserving full-batch attention metadata and LoRA mappings. The tradeoff is losing fast-prefill savings for the entire mixed batch.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][LoRA] Scale embedding LoRA deltas by the base layer's embed_scale
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

On Transformers-backend models with a scaled input embedding (VaultGemma; Gemma with `--model-impl transformers`), an `embed_tokens` LoRA adapter gets only `1 / embed_scale` of its effect. This scales the LoRA delta by the embedding's `embed_scale`, matching PEFT.

## Claims

- For an embedding that carries `embed_scale` (a Transformers `*ScaledWordEmbedding` after the backend rebases it), the `embed_tokens` LoRA output now matches PEFT 0.21.1.
- Embeddings without `embed_scale` (all native vLLM models) are unchanged.
- No per-step cost: the scale is applied once in `set_lora`, in place on the device copy.

## Validation

Tiny VaultGemma (random weights saved with `save_pretrained`) and a PEFT 0.21.1 adapter with `target_modules=["embed_tokens"]`, same token ids on both sides. PEFT reference: `PeftModel.get_input_embeddings()(ids)`. vLLM: `EngineArgs(enable_lora=True)` -> `get_model` (`TransformersForCausalLM`, embedding `VaultGemmaTextScaledWordEmbedding`) -> `load_lora_model` -> `set_active_adapters` -> `embed_input_ids`.

| | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| LoRA delta, vLLM / PEFT | 0.0625 (`1 / embed_scale`, `embed_scale = 16`) | 1.0000 |
| max abs diff vs PEFT embeddings | 1.11 | 2.4e-07 |
| max abs log-prob diff (HF forward on each embedding) | 1.18 | 0.000 |

```
pytest tests/lora/test_layers.py -k test_embeddings
```
48 passed. The new `embed_scale=16.0` cases (24) fail on `main` with every element mismatched.

Full `tests/lora/test_layers.py` on CPU: the same 102 tests fail on `main` and with this change (`'OffsetReplicatedLinear' object has no attribute 'cpu_linear'`, from this machine's build), so no new failures.

Not run: a GPU end-to-end serving run (no GPU available).

## Details

Root cause: the Transformers backend rebases a HF `*ScaledWordEmbedding` onto `VocabParallelEmbedding` and keeps its `forward`, which returns `lookup * embed_scale` (`replace_embedding_class` in `transformers/utils.py`). `VocabParallelEmbeddingWithLoRA.forward` calls that `base_layer.forward` and then adds the unscaled LoRA delta. PEFT's LoRA `Embedding.forward` multiplies the adapter output by `embed_scale` (huggingface/peft#2825, released in 0.18.0), and a merged adapter is scaled by construction.

Fix: in `set_lora`, multiply the slot's `lora_b` by `embed_scale` after copying it to the device.

Affected: VaultGemma (Transformers backend by default) and Gemma 1 to 4 with `--model-impl transformers`, which is the only way to load an `embed_tokens` LoRA for Gemma since the native classes do not declare `embedding_modules`. Native models with an embedding multiplier (Granite, MiniCPM, Falcon-H1, HyperCLOVA X) apply it after the LoRA-wrapped lookup and are unaffected.

Limitation: adapters trained with PEFT 0.17 or earlier saw an unscaled delta in the unmerged training forward. This change follows current PEFT and merged-adapter behavior.

Duplicate check: no open or closed PR or issue covers this (searched `embed_scale lora`, `ScaledWordEmbedding`, `VocabParallelEmbeddingWithLoRA`, `vaultgemma lora`, `transformers backend lora embedding`, `lora embed_tokens gemma`).

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Add the stateless Responses API (streaming and non-streaming)
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Add the stateless Responses API (`POST /v1/responses`, streaming and non-streaming) to the Rust frontend on top of the existing `ChatLlm` pipeline.

The original stack split this endpoint into non-streaming (2/3, this PR) followed by streaming (vllm-project/vllm#63903). The Rust frontend is streaming-first: `ChatEventStream` is the primary interface, and non-streaming Chat Completions is a fold over it. As [agreed with @franciscojavierarceo](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63902#issuecomment-6538867465), this PR now carries both layers in that order: streaming first, then non-streaming as a fold over the same state machine. It supersedes vllm-project/vllm#63903. Layer 1/3 (vllm-project/vllm#63901) has merged.

## Commits

Each commit builds and passes its tests on its own.

1. `da7eeffe37` (@franciscojavierarceo) — stateless streaming Responses: request lowering into `ChatRequest`, `OutputItemStreamer` for the item lifecycle, store-dependent features rejected or 404. Squashes the streaming-first part of the original stack (listed in the commit message); non-streaming returns 400 at this point.
2. `7e41889ed4` — typed wire DTOs and stream events: tools and tool choice reuse the Chat Completions definitions, input items deserialize into typed items (a message item may omit `type`, like Python), and SSE events are a typed enum with `type` and `sequence_number` added by a wrapper.
3. `2ea078d012` — defer to shared layers: the response echoes the sampling values the engine actually uses (model defaults applied, `max_output_tokens` clamped to the context), like Python's `ResponsesResponse.from_request(sampling_params)`, via `ChatEventStream::sampling()`.
4. `1c1bbe1fe5` — the streamer is the only source of `output`; output indices and the deferred `output_item.done` derive from completed items.
5. `10448da198` (co-authored by @franciscojavierarceo) — non-streaming as a fold: drive the same `OutputItemStreamer`, discard its events, and return the terminal response. The Responses terminal event carries the complete response, so `output` follows one set of item rules in both modes. Errors still map to HTTP statuses (engine errors 400/503, a broken stream 500) instead of a `failed` response.
6. `8fbae250f3` — per-request timing `metrics`, as in Python Responses.
7. `4da559a6db` — a truncated reasoning item is also marked `incomplete`, as in Python.
8. `f28f024629` — remaining vLLM request controls: forward `min_p`; reject `spaces_between_special_tokens: false`, `media_io_kwargs`, `mm_processor_kwargs`, and `enable_response_messages: true` instead of dropping them.
9. `a1d8bd8364` — unset response fields serialize as `null`, as in Python.
10. `99446a2d75` — report `usage.input_tokens_details.cache_write_tokens`, as Python has since vllm-project/vllm#60973; the OpenAI SDK `Response` type requires it. Found by the e2e below.

The CI bot merged `main` into the branch as `be0cafa775` before commit 10.

## Behavior

- Stateless: clients replay the full history in `input`. `store: true` executes without storing (Python's implicit downgrade); `background: true` is 400; `previous_response_id`, retrieval, and cancellation are 404.
- `max_tool_calls` limits built-in tool calls only, so with function tools alone it is accepted and echoed.
- `reasoning.summary`, `text.verbosity`, `include: ["reasoning.encrypted_content"]`, and `service_tier` are accepted compatibility inputs (Codex sends them by default) without producing summaries, applying verbosity, encrypting reasoning, or scheduling guarantees.
- Deliberate difference from Python: a generation failure during streaming ends with `response.failed` carrying the partial output, instead of a generic error frame.
- Not supported: built-in, custom, and namespace tools, `allowed_tools`, and output logprobs (rejected with 400).

## Validation

Rebased onto `eb239e34c2`.

- Every commit: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features`, and the server Responses tests pass (45 → 52 tests across the stack).
- Tip: `cargo test --workspace` has 2483 passed; the same 27 tests also fail on `main` in this environment (grammar replay fixtures and two environment-dependent tests).

The only schema gap was the missing `cache_write_tokens`, fixed in commit 10.

commits.pr_title: [Recipes Tool][CPU] Remove obsolete TP/DP NUMA binding workaround
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Remove the temporary CPU TP/DP NUMA-binding workaround from Recipes, now that native DP NUMA affinity has been fixed by [vLLM PR #62867](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62867).

## Claims

- Remove the obsolete `--tp-dp-numa-bind-workaround` CLI option and binding override logic.
- Remove the unused `build_numa_omp_threads_bind()` helper.
- Rely on native vLLM CPU NUMA autobinding for TP/DP sweeps.
- Preserve recipe-provided CPU binding settings and existing sweep functionality.

## Validation

- Verify Recipes converter syntax and CLI help.
- Confirm no remaining references to the removed workaround.
- Run Xeon CPU sweeps using the latest nightly image with TP/DP configurations.
- Verify each DP rank binds to its assigned NUMA node through server logs.

## Details

The previous workaround generated explicit `VLLM_CPU_OMP_THREADS_BIND` values to avoid multiple DP ranks sharing the same NUMA node.

With PR #62867 merged, vLLM now handles per-DP-rank NUMA affinity natively. The workaround is no longer necessary and can interfere with automatic CPU reservation settings such as `VLLM_CPU_NUM_OF_RESERVED_CPU`.

This change simplifies Recipes and removes obsolete code without modifying vLLM's core CPU binding implementation. It assumes a vLLM build containing PR #62867.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Kimi-VL] Set pad_token_id explicitly in KimiVLConfig
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`KimiVLConfig` passed `pad_token_id` to `super().__init__` as a keyword argument. With the dataclass-based `PreTrainedConfig`, `pad_token_id` is not a declared field.

## Claims

- Fixes the `TypeError: __init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'pad_token_id'` raised when `KimiVLConfig` is constructed on a `PreTrainedConfig` base that does not forward unknown keyword arguments.
- `pad_token_id` is now assigned explicitly on `KimiVLConfig` before the `super().__init__` call, so the attribute exists regardless of how the base class handles unused kwargs.
- No change to the public constructor signature: existing callers passing `pad_token_id=` continue to work.
- No change to serialization behavior for the `pad_token_id` value itself; the fix only removes the reliance on an implicit `setattr` path.

## Validation

- Reproduction before the fix: construct `KimiVLConfig` on a base that rejects unknown kwargs (or monkeypatch the base `__init__` to not forward extras); observe `TypeError: __init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'pad_token_id'`.
- After the fix: the same construction succeeds, and `config.pad_token_id` returns the supplied value.

## Details

`PreTrainedConfig` is a dataclass, and `pad_token_id` is not a declared field on it; the field is only used by `KimiVLConfig` itself.

I've checked the code on [huggingface](https://huggingface.co/moonshotai/Kimi-VL-A3B-Instruct/blob/main/configuration_kimi_vl.py) and #16387, it can be confirmed that MoonshotAI has modified the base `PreTrainedConfig`.

commits.pr_title: [Model Loader] Direct reload: lay the checkpoint out where a relocated weight now starts
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

With `VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct`, a weight that post-load processing moves into another storage at an offset is reloaded into the wrong place.

`record_checkpoint_layout` records each weight's `storage_offset` before post-load processing. On a reload, `begin_direct_reload` views the weight back to that layout in the storage the weight lives in **now**. If post-load processing moved the weight into a different storage (e.g. `set_` into a fused buffer), the recorded offset belongs to the old storage. The new checkpoint is then written over the neighbouring weight, and the moved weight itself keeps its old bytes.

Example: on ROCm, `prepare_compressor_gemm_fusion` in DeepSeek-V4 does `indexer_weight.set_(fused_weight[main_size:])`. On a reload, the indexer compressor weight was written over the main compressor rows. DeepSeek-V4-Pro GSM8K after reloading the original weights dropped from 0.96 to 0.885.

## Fix

Also record the storage's `data_ptr`. If the weight's storage has changed by reload time, use its current `storage_offset()` instead of the recorded one. Only `reload/direct.py` changes (+4/−1).

## Test Plan

- New `test_reload_into_weight_moved_to_an_offset`. The toy model's post-load processing moves `proj.weight` into a new buffer at an offset. A reload must match a fresh cold start and keep every address.
- `tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_direct_reload.py` on GB300, run with this PR and with main's `direct.py`.
- DeepSeek-V4-Pro (heterogeneous, TP8, CUDA graphs, compressor GEMM fusion on) on MI355X with `VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct`: cold GSM8K (400, 5-shot), then reload original → perturbed → original, plus a `data_ptr` report. This also needs a separate fix for a `KeyError` in the DeepSeek-V4 ROCm preshuffle scales (stacked on #64692).

## Test Result

| | `test_direct_reload.py` |
|---|---|
| this PR | 36 passed |
| main `direct.py` | new test fails |

| DeepSeek-V4-Pro, MI355X | cold | reload orig | reload perturbed | reload orig | moved tensors |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| before (KeyError worked around) | 0.96 | 0.885 | – | – | 30 (indexer `compressor.fused_wkv_wgate.weight`) |
| this PR | 0.965 | 0.9675 | 0.035 | 0.9575 | 0 / 3480 |

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

commits.pr_title: [Model Loader] DeepSeek-V4 ROCm: keep the preshuffle scales out of the module's parameters
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

With `VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct`, DeepSeek-V4 on ROCm crashes on the first reload:

```
KeyError: 'layers.0.attn.fused_wqa_wkv.weight_scale_inv'
KeyError: 'layers.0.ffn.shared_experts.gate_up_proj.weight_scale_inv'
```

`prepare_attn_preshuffle` and `prepare_gateup_preshuffle` store the scale `nn.Parameter` itself as a module attribute (`self._wqa_wkv_scale = ws`, `self._gateup_scale = ws`). `nn.Module.__setattr__` then registers it as a second parameter under that name, which the reload does not know.

## Fix

- Store `ws.detach()`, a plain tensor on the same storage, so nothing new is registered.
- Assign it through `refill_derived`, so a reload refills it in place at the address the captured CUDA graphs read.
- Do the same for the other derived tensors of `_prepare_fp8_wo_a`: `_wo_a_e8m0_scale`, `_wo_a_cos_cache` and `_wo_a_sin_cache`.
- Move the `replace_parameter` / `refill_derived` imports to the top of both files.

## Test Plan

DeepSeek-V4-Pro (heterogeneous, TP8, CUDA graphs, compressor GEMM fusion on) on MI355X with `VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct`:

1. cold GSM8K (400, 5-shot)
2. reload the original weights
3. reload perturbed weights
4. reload the original weights again

Plus a `data_ptr` report against cold start. This was run together with #65281, which fixes the compressor-fusion offset on reload.

## Test Result

| tree | cold | reload orig | reload perturbed | reload orig | moved tensors |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| #64692 head | 0.9650 | `KeyError: 'layers.0.attn.fused_wqa_wkv.weight_scale_inv'` | – | – | – |
| + this PR + #65281 | 0.9650 | 0.9675 | 0.0350 | 0.9575 | 0 / 3480 |
