commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Benchmark] Fail streams that end in a server error event
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

`vllm bench serve` counts a request as successful when any token arrived, even if the stream then ends in a server error event. This fails those requests in the completions, chat and audio backends, in both `vllm/benchmarks/lib/endpoint_request_func.py` and the standalone `benchmarks/backend_request_func.py`.

Benchmark client only: no model, kernel or serving path is touched.

## Claims

- A stream that delivers tokens and then an `error` event is reported as failed, with the server's error object in `output.error`. Partial `generated_text` is kept for `--save-detailed`.
- The server's error takes precedence over "Never received a valid chunk to calculate TTFT", which names a symptom rather than the cause.
- Under a mid-run EngineCore kill at concurrency 64, the unpatched report overstates completed requests by 22% and output throughput by 14%, and understates mean E2EL by 8%.

## Validation

Unit (no GPU), at the rebased head `4a4eb4257`, on base `76c6f3f2a`. `test_error_event_stream_is_not_reported_as_success` and its legacy counterpart stream two tokens, then the error envelope, then `[DONE]`, over all three streaming endpoints.

```bash
pytest tests/benchmarks/test_endpoint_request_func_timing.py -k error_event
```

| Sources | Result |
|---|---|
| Base `76c6f3f2a` (new tests only) | 6 failed, each `AssertionError: assert not True` on `output.success` |
| This PR | 6 passed |
| This PR, full `test_endpoint_request_func_timing.py` + `test_responses_request_func.py` | 74 passed |

Those pytest runs used `--noconftest` in a CPU-only environment. `pre-commit run --hook-stage manual --files <changed>` passes, including mypy.

End-to-end on one RTX 3060 (clocks locked), Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct, `vllm bench serve --save-detailed`, random 512-token prompts, 128 output tokens, `--ignore-eos`; `kill -9` on EngineCore 20 s into the run. Measured at the original commit, before the rebase. Classifying one unpatched run's own requests by token count, at concurrency 64:

| Reported by the benchmark | Reported | Complete requests only | Error |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| completed | 274 | 225 | **+22%** |
| mean E2EL | 2,566 ms | 2,790 ms | 8% too fast |
| output tokens | 32,684 | 28,800 | +3,884 partial tokens |
| output throughput | 2,745 tok/s | 2,418 tok/s | **+14%** |

49 of the 274 "successful" requests (18%) never produced their 128 tokens; their counts run 1-127, median 121, so they do not stand out by eye. With the fix, the same fault reports 221 completed, all complete, and each failed request carries the server's error object.

Only a request that has already streamed a token and then receives the error event is miscounted, so the effect scales with in-flight streams at the fault: 49 at concurrency 64, 1-4 at concurrency 16.

Independent validation at the earlier commit `1e74a69c7`: [regression corpus](https://github.com/k21993/benchmark-stream-audit) from a comment on this PR.

No `RemoteOpenAIServer` regression test is added: a real server cannot deterministically emit this event mid-stream without fault injection, so the tests drive the real request functions over the existing fake session, and the end-to-end run above covers the real failure.

**Model evaluation:** not applicable; this only changes how the benchmark client classifies a response.

## Details

**Root cause.** A generation that fails after the response has started cannot change the HTTP 200 already sent, so the stream generators report the failure in-band:

```text
data: {"error": {"message": "EngineCore encountered an issue. ...", "type": "InternalServerError", "param": null, "code": 500}}
data: [DONE]
```

The clients read only `choices` and `usage`, so the truncated request joins `completed`, its partial tokens join `total_output` and `output_throughput`, and its short end-to-end time joins the E2EL statistics. The report is biased in the optimistic direction exactly when the server is failing.

**Design.** The same envelope is emitted for a dead engine, a failed tool parser and a generation error, so the fix keys on the `error` object rather than on one cause. It uses the same `stream_error` shape as the Responses backend.

**Not a duplicate.** Searched the PRs touching these files:
- #54708 (merged) fails streams with no token chunk; a stream that produces tokens and then fails still counted as a success.
- #55508 (merged) fixed TTFT/E2E latency accounting; it does not look at error events.
- #54628 (merged) handles error events for the Responses backend only.
- #62341 (merged) filters content-free chat chunks; this PR is rebased on it and keeps `_choice_has_streamed_output`.
- #64143 (open) changes SSE data-field parsing, not failure classification; it touches the same file, so whichever lands second needs a small rebase.

**Follow-up.** The Rust bench client (`rust/src/bench/src/backends/openai_completions.rs`, `openai_chat.rs`) has the same gap and is left out to keep this change in one language. #59736 covers token-less streams there, not this case. I can send it separately or fold it in here.

**How this was found.** While `SIGKILL`ing EngineCore under load to compare what each observer reports, requests in flight at the fault ended with HTTP 200 after 1-116 of their 128 tokens.

---

commits.pr_title: [Perf][Attention] Source Triton metadata builder geometry from kv_cache_spec
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`TritonAttentionMetadataBuilder` is built per KV-cache group but sizes its 3D-kernel threshold and split-K scratch from the model-wide KV head count and head dim, so on heterogeneous models such as Gemma 4 decode stays on the slower 2D kernel; this PR reads both from the group's `kv_cache_spec`, as `FlashAttentionMetadataBuilder` already does (#42650 did the same for `num_heads_q`).

`unified_attention` takes the 2D grid's `num_kv_heads` from `k.shape[2]`, the group's own count. On `gemma-4-26B-A4B-it` the full-attention group has 2 KV heads against a model-wide 8, so `seq_threshold_3D` is `128 // 8 = 16` instead of `128 // 2 = 64`: at batch 24 the grid is 48 blocks, below `MIN_LAUNCH_GRID_SIZE_2D = 128`, yet the builder stays on 2D. The sliding groups size `softmax_segm_output` for head dim 512 instead of 256.

The buffer uses `head_size`, the stride `unified_attention` applies (`next_power_of_2(q.shape[2])`); `head_size_v` belongs to the DiffKV path, which re-sizes its own buffer. Switching kernel changes the bf16 reduction order, so generated text can differ. Where the spec matches the model-global values, nothing changes.

#54191 changes `num_heads_kv` only. #57409 changes `headdim` only, inside a DFlash change. This PR does both, and the new tests fail on either half alone. #47520 rescales the grid-size target and keeps the divisor, so it composes with this.

## Claims

- Gemma 4 full-attention decode at batches 24–64 moves from the 2D to the 3D kernel: **+66%** at batch 24 (506 µs → 172 µs) and **+36%** at batch 64 on MI325X. Batches that keep their kernel are flat.
- On vLLM v0.29.0 (MI355X), `vllm bench serve` of gemma-4 at 32K input and concurrency 24 gives **+6.7%** total tok/s and **−11.5%** median TPOT, with TTFT flat. Not re-taken on this `main`.
- GSM8K strict-match on that build goes from **0.4155 to 0.4511**; a repeated base run is bit-identical.
- Affected locally: gemma-4-26B-A4B and gemma-4-31B, which `Gemma4Config` forces onto `TRITON_ATTN` on ROCm. Homogeneous models are unchanged.

## Validation

Base is `main@7128f568ac`; the patched arm adds only this diff.

| tree | Triton cases in `test_group_head_counts.py` |
|---|---|
| `main` | 3 failed |
| `num_heads_kv` only (#54191) | 2 failed: geometry, scratch stride |
| `headdim = head_size_v` | 1 failed: scratch stride |
| threshold capped before the capture snap | 1 failed: snaps to 48, not 64 |
| this PR | 4 passed, 12 skipped |

`test_triton_attn_metadata_builder.py` and `test_triton_attn_segments.py` pass 44/44 on both arms. One new case uses an off-grid `max_num_seqs=50`, where the threshold snaps to a capture size (64) before `max_num_seqs` caps the scratch rows.

Kernel, MI325X, `unified_attention` at the full-attention group shape (16 Q heads, 2 KV heads, head dim 512, block 16, ctx 4096, decode), median of five `do_bench` repeats, both run orders within 0.5 points:

| batch | main | this PR | gain |
|---:|:---:|:---:|---:|
| 8 / 16 | 3D | 3D | −0.1% / −0.3% |
| 24 | 2D | **3D** | **+66%** |
| 32 | 2D | **3D** | **+63%** |
| 48 / 50 | 2D | **3D** | **+49% / +48%** |
| 64 | 2D | **3D** | **+36%** |
| 96 | 2D | 2D | ~0 |

Outputs match exactly where the kernel is unchanged, and to 2.8e-3 relative L2 where it switches.

Serve on v0.29.0 (`98dff2a81d`), MI355X, six interleaved pairs, 32K input / 256 output, concurrency 24:

| metric | base | patched | Δ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Total tok/s | 25835 | 27574 | **+6.7%** |
| Median TPOT (ms) | 65.18 | 57.68 | **−11.5%** |
| Median TTFT (ms) | 13823 | 13793 | −0.2% |

GSM8K, 5-shot, greedy, 1319 items, `seed=1234`:

| comparison | identical text | strict-match |
|---|---:|---|
| base vs base | 100% | 0.4155 → 0.4155 |
| base vs base at `max_num_seqs=128` | 4.6% | 0.4155 → 0.4314 |
| base vs this PR | 12.7% | 0.4155 → 0.4511 |
| Qwen3-8B (never builds this) | 99.9% | 0.8726 → 0.8726 |

`main` alone at a different `max_num_seqs` already changes 95% of generations: the 2D/3D boundary is batch-dependent, and this PR moves it.

## Details

Of 17 local checkpoints, only Gemma 4 reaches this builder without an explicit backend selection; the others, forced onto it, match `main` in every builder field. Under full graph capture with an off-grid `max_num_seqs=50`, batches 49–50 pad to 56 tokens and stay on 2D on both arms; that sizing comes from `main`.

---

Found by [Hyperloom](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Hyperloom); reviewed and measured by hand.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Report the prompt cache split in the first streamed usage
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes #65035. The first continuous-usage chunk of a Chat Completions stream now carries `prompt_tokens_details`, so the Anthropic `message_start` reports the same split as `message_delta`.

## Claims

- With `--enable-prompt-tokens-details`, the first streamed usage chunk carries the same `cached_tokens` and `created_cache_tokens` as the final one.
- `message_start.usage.input_tokens` excludes cache reads and writes, matching `message_delta`.

## Validation

```
# unit test, base
pytest tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_serving_chat.py -k test_streaming_first_chunk_reports_prompt_tokens_details
E       KeyError: 'prompt_tokens_details'
1 failed, 221 deselected
# unit tests, this branch
pytest tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_serving_chat.py -k "usage or prompt_tokens_details"
124 passed, 98 deselected
```

End to end on v0.32.0 (MI300X, Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8, `--enable-prefix-caching --enable-prompt-tokens-details`), the issue's reproducer, second request:

| | `message_start` | `message_delta` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| v0.32.0 | `input_tokens` 3656, no cache fields | 520 uncached, 3136 cache read, 0 written |
| v0.32.0 + this patch | 520 uncached, 3136 cache read, 0 written | 520 uncached, 3136 cache read, 0 written |

`test_anthropic_streaming_cache_usage` now expects the split in `message_start`. It needs a GPU server, so I checked that behaviour with the run above instead.

## Details

The first iteration already reads `num_cached_tokens` and `num_cache_creation_tokens`, but only the final usage chunk passed them to `_make_prompt_tokens_details`. The first chunk now does too. With the flag off it still returns `None`, so cache fields stay absent as #40912 intends.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Don't count content-free chunks as streamed outputs in vllm-bench chat
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

The Rust `vllm-bench` `openai-chat` backend counts any chunk with non-empty `choices` as a streamed output. vLLM's chat stream opens with a role-only chunk, `{"role":"assistant","content":""}`, so TTFT is measured to a chunk with no token and the first real token adds a spurious ITL sample. #62341 fixed the same thing in the Python client; this ports its rule.

## Claims

- On 100 chat requests, `main` recorded one extra ITL sample on every request, a sub-0.1 ms first sample on all 100 (the role chunk arriving just before the first token), and on 22 requests more ITL samples than there are gaps between their tokens. With the fix all three are gone.
- `ChatDelta` now reads `role`, `reasoning`, `reasoning_content`, `tool_calls` and `function_call`, and a chunk counts when it carries content, reasoning or a tool call, or an empty `content` without `role` (a token that decodes to an empty string). Same rule as Python's `_choice_has_streamed_output`.

## Validation

Four new tests in `openai_chat.rs`, on the existing socket SSE server made scriptable: the role chunk, an empty mid-stream delta, an empty-string token, and reasoning plus tool call deltas. All four fail with the old gate. `cargo test -p vllm-bench` passes (217), and `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -p vllm-bench --all-targets -- -D warnings` are clean.

RTX 3080, `Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct`, random 256 in / 128 out, 100 prompts, concurrency 16, through a proxy that recorded every streamed chunk:

| | `main` | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| requests with one more ITL sample than token chunks on the wire | 100 | 0 |
| requests with a sub-0.1 ms ITL sample at position 0 | 100 | 0 |
| requests with `len(itl) == output_tokens` | 22 | 0 |

Forced tool calls through `openai-chat` still complete 100 of 100, with ITL counts matching the wire.

## Details

#59736 makes a token-less stream fail. With this change a stream carrying only the role chunk has no token, so the two fit together.

No issue or PR covers this. AI assistance (Claude) was used to write the change and tests. I reviewed every line and ran the tests and GPU comparison.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf] Triton sigmoid+bias top-k when MoE grouping eliminates nothing
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

AITER `biased_grouped_topk` runs an LDS group scan even when the grouping cannot eliminate any expert — that is, when `topk_group >= num_expert_group`, so every group is selected. This adds a register-resident Triton sigmoid+bias top-k and substitutes it at `rocm_aiter_ops.biased_grouped_topk`, the single call site both ROCm routers reach.

Previously this PR specialised `rocm_aiter_grouped_topk` only. Moving it to the wrapper came out of review (thanks @simondanielsson) and covers both paths without touching routing metadata:

| caller | group arguments it passes |
|---|---|
| `GroupedTopKRouter` | the model's own `1/1` for a degenerate router |
| `FusedTopKBiasRouter` | a count synthesised to fit an AITER kernel — measured `2/2` for a 64-expert router — with `topk_group == num_expert_group` |

`vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/rocm_aiter_moe.py` is no longer modified; the diff is three files, additions only.

## Claims

- 1.67×–2.15× on the routing op on gfx942, and 1.16×–1.57× per shape on gfx950, under CUDA graph replay, across the configurations listed below.
- The gate stops at 512 experts and top-8. On gfx950 the kernel loses at top-16 (896-expert top-16 down to 0.62×), so those routers keep AITER — see *Scope and bounds*.
- Equivalent to the call it replaces whenever no group is eliminated, including `num_expert_group == topk_group > 1`, which is the shape `FusedTopKBiasRouter` produces.
- Eager execution is **not** faster, so it is excluded by the substitution rather than claimed as a win.
- Selected expert ids match AITER on 3323 of 3328 routing calls in a live Moonlight-16B-A3B forward and on 1248 of 1248 in Kimi-VL-A3B.
- **Scope: single-token batches only (`_MAX_TOKENS = 1`), as suggested in review**, i.e. one request decoding without speculation, which is where the end-to-end gain is. Larger batches keep AITER.
- End to end on MI355X with current `main`, five models with 64 to 384 experts, 1k to 32k context: **single-request decode is 0.4% to 4.2% faster on every model**, and higher concurrency is within noise; nothing regresses beyond the same-arm drift. GSM8K is unchanged on GLM-5.3-Flash and Kimi-K2.6. Earlier gfx942 runs were within noise.
- No new env var, and no change to router selection or to the advertised routing method.

## Dispatch scope: why this is restricted to CUDA graph steps

The kernel's advantage is device time. Timed from a plain Python loop it is *slower* — it is a Triton launch from Python against a single C++ dispatch, and that overhead is not amortised.

Because the gate is a token-count bound rather than an execution-phase check, eager steps can reach it, so this was measured end to end with `--enforce-eager`, interleaved B-A-B-A on Moonlight:

| in / out | concurrency | AITER tok/s | ungated PR tok/s | Δ | same-arm drift |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 64 / 256 | 8 | 488.7 | 471.8 | **−3.5%** | 0.6% / 1.2% |
| 64 / 256 | 32 | 1910.4 | 1876.9 | **−1.8%** | 0.8% / 0.1% |
| 1024 / 1024 | 8 | 780.8 | 758.1 | **−2.9%** | 0.8% / 0.2% |
| 1024 / 1024 | 32 | 3008.8 | 2915.3 | **−3.1%** | 0.0% / 0.9% |

Consistent sign and a magnitude several times the drift, so this is a real regression, not noise. The dispatch therefore substitutes only while a CUDA graph is being captured, tested with `torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing()` as `custom_all_reduce.py` and `sparse_attn_indexer.py` already do, and eager steps keep AITER. An earlier revision tested `get_forward_context().cudagraph_runtime_mode` instead; that misses every FULL graph under the V2 model runner, which captures them with the forward context set to `NONE` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/cudagraph_utils.py`), so on current main it substituted only inside PIECEWISE graphs. Re-running the same eager A/B with the check in place:

| in / out | concurrency | AITER tok/s | this PR tok/s | Δ | same-arm drift |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 64 / 256 | 8 | 490.2 | 492.5 | +0.5% | 0.7% / 0.1% |
| 64 / 256 | 32 | 1934.9 | 1933.3 | −0.1% | 1.2% / 0.0% |
| 1024 / 1024 | 8 | 787.1 | 786.8 | −0.0% | 0.1% / 1.0% |
| 1024 / 1024 | 32 | 3018.7 | 3009.5 | −0.3% | 1.9% / 0.8% |

Instrumentation observed no Triton dispatches with `enforce_eager=True`. With graphs enabled, on current main and MI355X, a server records these substitution decisions while it captures its graphs:

| model | cudagraph mode | substituted with the forward-context check | substituted with the stream-capture check |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B | `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` (forced by the model) | 0 of 2912 | 494 of 2912 |
| Moonlight-16B-A3B | `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` | 988 of 8190 | 1482 of 8190 |

494 is 19 captured decode sizes up to 128 tokens times 26 MoE layers; the remaining decisions are larger captured sizes, the profiling run and warm-up runs, all of which keep AITER. Those counts are with the earlier `_MAX_TOKENS = 128`; with the current `_MAX_TOKENS = 1` a Moonlight server substitutes 78 of 8190 decisions, all of them in the 1-token graphs, and keeps AITER everywhere else.

## Validation

All runs on one MI300X (gfx942, 304 CUs), torch 2.10.0, triton 3.6.0.

Three checkpoints are used, all with `num_expert_group=1`, `topk_group=1`, a sigmoid router and a `noaux_tc` correction bias. Which one carries which measurement, since they differ:

| model | experts / top-k | context | used for |
|---|---|---|---|
| Moonlight-16B-A3B | 64 / 6 | 8192 | routing comparison, e2e ≤6k, NIAH 4096, GPQA |
| Kimi-VL-A3B-Instruct | 64 / 6 | 131072 | routing comparison, e2e 1k |
| Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B | **256 / 8** | 1M | e2e 1k, GPQA, and the 8k/64k attempt |

NIAH ran at 4096 and GPQA at roughly 1k prompts, both well under the 8192 input length at which the engine fault described below appears, so those results and that fault are not in conflict.

Which model carries which measurement, since they differ:

| measurement | model | context used |
|---|---|---|
| unit, micro | — (kernel in isolation) | n/a |
| routing comparison | Moonlight-16B-A3B **and** Kimi-VL-A3B | short decode rows |
| e2e 1k/1k, 6k/1k | Moonlight-16B-A3B | ≤ 7k |
| e2e 1k/1k | Kimi-VL-A3B | ≤ 2k |
| e2e 8k/1k, 64k/1k | **not obtained** — see below | — |
| NIAH | Moonlight-16B-A3B | 4096 |
| GPQA | Moonlight-16B-A3B | ~1k prompts |

NIAH and GPQA ran on Moonlight at 4096 and ~1k respectively, both well under the 8192 input length at which the engine crash below appears, so there is no contradiction between those results and that crash.

### Unit

Against upstream `db3b0f0fa`:

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_rocm_aiter_topk.py -k "flat_topk or substitutes"
# 61 passed on MI355X (gfx950), this PR at 7c6559d9 cherry-picked onto main 3966924d
```

Each correctness test compares against `rocm_aiter_ops.biased_grouped_topk(..., 1, 1, ...)` — the exact call being replaced — through the same wrapper production uses.

| test | coverage |
|---|---|
| `test_flat_topk_matches_aiter` | 40 cases: {bf16, fp32} × {renorm on, off} × 10 shapes, including primes/odd sizes that exercise the masked tail of `BLOCK_E = next_power_of_2(num_experts)`: `(3,257,8)`, `(7,131,5)`, `(13,509,7)`, `(1,2,1)`, `(5,65,3)` |
| `test_flat_topk_casts_bias_like_aiter` | bf16 gating with an fp32 bias — see *Bias dtype* |
| `test_flat_topk_matches_aiter_with_uneliminating_groups` | `num_expert_group == topk_group` ∈ {1, 2, 4, 8} × renorm on/off — the `FusedTopKBiasRouter` shape |
| `test_flat_topk_honours_routed_scaling` | `routed_scaling_factor` 1.0 / 2.446 / 2.827 |
| `test_biased_grouped_topk_substitutes_only_when_expected` | captures a real CUDA graph around the wrapper: it substitutes for `1/1` and `2/2` during capture, and not for `8/4` or in eager |

The rest of that file reports 34 failures in my container which reproduce identically on unmodified `db3b0f0fa` (34 failed / 5 passed before this change, 34 failed / 77 passed after it, measured before the review trim); this PR does not touch them.

```bash
pre-commit run --files vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/rocm_aiter_moe.py \
  vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/router/rocm_sigmoid_bias_flat_topk.py \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_rocm_aiter_topk.py
```

### Micro

Per-call **device** time under CUDA graph replay, 50 calls captured per graph so the replay overhead is amortised ~50× instead of landing on both arms.

| gating | experts | tokens | AITER (µs) | PR (µs) | speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| bf16 | 256 | 1 / 8 / 32 / 128 | 5.47 / 5.67 / 5.72 / 5.76 | 3.00 / 3.18 / 3.20 / 3.27 | 1.82× / 1.78× / 1.79× / 1.76× |
| bf16 | 384 | 1 / 8 / 32 / 128 | 6.80 / 7.03 / 7.07 / 7.14 | 4.01 / 4.14 / 4.16 / 4.26 | 1.69× / 1.70× / 1.70× / 1.67× |
| fp32 | 256 | 1 / 8 / 32 / 128 | 6.05 / 6.12 / 6.24 / 6.26 | 2.82 / 2.99 / 3.00 / 3.16 | 2.15× / 2.05× / 2.08× / 1.98× |
| fp32 | 384 | 1 / 8 / 32 / 128 | 7.33 / 7.54 / 7.61 / 7.62 | 3.56 / 3.70 / 3.73 / 3.79 | 2.06× / 2.04× / 2.04× / 2.01× |

That is gfx942 (MI300X) at 256 and 384 experts.

On gfx950 (MI355X), the same method over a wider range of shapes: bf16 gating, fp32 bias, `routed_scaling_factor` 2.446, renormalised, six random seeds per point, plus one input where a single row has an exactly tied top score. Expert ids matched a stable-sort reference on every input, and AITER's id set on all 192 random inputs.

| experts | top-k | AITER µs, 1 / 8 / 32 / 128 tokens | PR µs, 1 / 8 / 32 / 128 tokens | mean speedup | worst random launch | one tied row |
|---:|---:|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 64 | 6 | 5.40 / 5.79 / 5.85 / 5.77 | 3.45 / 3.65 / 3.72 / 3.74 | 1.57× | 1.51× | 1.33× |
| 256 | 8 | 5.21 / 5.35 / 5.46 / 5.51 | 3.99 / 4.27 / 4.26 / 4.45 | 1.27× | 1.06× | 1.06× |
| 384 | 8 | 5.36 / 5.88 / 5.93 / 5.97 | 4.62 / 5.12 / 5.12 / 5.13 | 1.16× | 1.13× | 0.92× |
| 512 | 8 | 5.50 / 6.11 / 6.17 / 6.23 | 4.56 / 5.20 / 5.20 / 5.45 | 1.18× | 0.98× | 0.95× |
| 512 | 16 | 6.59 / 7.11 / 7.17 / 7.24 | 5.36 / 5.85 / 5.92 / 6.97 | 1.18× | 0.80× | 0.78× |
| 768 | 16 | 11.36 / 12.37 / 12.42 / 12.45 | 6.75 / 7.26 / 7.29 / 8.06 | 1.67× | 1.04× | 0.98× |
| 896 | 16 | 6.97 / 7.66 / 7.72 / 7.75 | 6.79 / 7.26 / 7.29 / 8.07 | 1.03× | 0.65× | 0.62× |
| 1024 | 16 | 7.12 / 7.80 / 7.85 / 7.91 | 6.76 / 7.24 / 7.28 / 7.28 | 1.07× | 1.04× | 0.64× |

The advantage shrinks as the router widens on gfx950; it does not grow. The slow launches are the tie fallback: when a row has two experts with exactly equal biased scores among its top-k, the fast path picks more than k and that row redoes the selection, and the launch waits for its slowest row. bf16 logits make exact ties common enough at top-16 to matter (0.8% of rows at 896 experts, so about one 32-row launch in five), which is where the 0.6× launches come from. Rows above 512 experts or top-8 therefore stay on AITER.

### Routing comparison on live models

Comparing generated text between arms is not a usable instrument on this setup: it is not deterministic run to run — two baseline-only runs of the same four greedy prompts already diverge. Instead both kernels were run on identical inputs inside a live forward, AITER into the real buffers and the new kernel into scratch, with generation continuing on the AITER result so the measurement cannot perturb the run.

| model | calls compared | calls where **all** selected ids match | max abs weight delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Moonlight-16B-A3B | 3328 | 3323 | 4.77e-07 |
| Kimi-VL-A3B-Instruct | 1248 | 1248 | 4.77e-07 |

Both have `n_group=1`, `topk_group=1`, `scoring_func="sigmoid"`, `noaux_tc`, `norm_topk_prob=true`, 64 experts, top-6. The five differing Moonlight calls each carry a weight delta of 1.19e-07 or 4.77e-07; that is consistent with a near-tie in the biased score resolving to a different expert, but the weight delta alone does not prove the scores were exactly equal.

### End to end on MI300X (gfx942)

`vllm serve` + `vllm bench serve`, interleaved, one fresh server per block.

An initial sequential A/B (all of arm 0, then all of arm 1) showed +16–24% throughput. That did not reproduce under interleaved testing and has been withdrawn — the same AITER baseline measured 1789 tok/s sequentially and 2250 tok/s interleaved on a shared host.

| model | in / out | concurrency | Δ throughput | Δ TPOT | same-arm drift |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Moonlight | 1024 / 1024 | 8 | +0.7% | −0.8% | 0.4% / 1.4% |
| Moonlight | 1024 / 1024 | 32 | +0.8% | −0.9% | 1.1% / 0.6% |
| Kimi-VL | 1024 / 1024 | 8 | +0.4% | −0.6% | 1.0% / 0.9% |
| Kimi-VL | 1024 / 1024 | 32 | +0.7% | −0.9% | 3.6% / 0.7% |
| Kimi-Linear | 1024 / 1024 | 8 | +1.1% | −1.1% | 0.4% / 0.4% |
| Kimi-Linear | 1024 / 1024 | 32 | +0.1% | −0.1% | 1.1% / 0.7% |

Comparable to the same-arm variation, so no gfx942 end-to-end speedup is claimed. The Kimi-Linear rows discard the first repetition of each block: the very first benchmark run of the campaign returned 1066 tok/s against 1510-1543 for the other seven runs of that point, a warm-up artefact rather than a property of either arm.

**The 8k/1k and 64k/1k points are now measured.** The earlier report that they could not be served was wrong, and the reason is worth stating because it is a bug in the benchmark harness rather than in serving.

`vllm bench serve --dataset-name random` samples token ids from `tokenizer.vocab_size`. For this checkpoint that is **163842**, while the model's embedding has `config.vocab_size` = **163840** rows, so ids 163840 and 163841 index past the table and the embedding gather faults. The dataset emits a *contiguous run* of ids, so a 65536-token prompt covers 40% of the vocabulary and nearly always includes one of the two; an 8192-token prompt covers 5%, which is why 8k completed under some seeds and not others. On stock vLLM, with no part of this PR installed, the identical 8192 configuration completes 3/3 with `--seed 7` and faults 3/3 with `--seed 1234`:

| seed | completed | `Memory access fault` |
|---|---|---|
| 7 | 8, 8, 8 | 0 |
| 1234 | 0, 0, 0 | 1 |

That also explains the fault seen earlier on a different machine with Kimi-VL, where the kernel named in the HSA exception was `at::native::vectorized_gather_kernel` — the embedding gather.

Replacing the synthesised prompts with real text (a custom dataset whose maximum token id is 138177, verified below the embedding size) removes the fault entirely: 8 of 8 runs complete at 64k with zero faults.

| in / out | concurrency | AITER tok/s | this PR tok/s | Δ throughput | Δ TPOT | same-arm drift |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 8192 / 1024 | 4 | 4305.4 | 4466.3 | +3.7% | −4.0% | 4.1% / 1.7% |
| 8192 / 1024 | 8 | 6154.7 | 6162.5 | +0.1% | −1.2% | 1.4% / 1.8% |
| 65536 / 1024 | 1 | 13528.3 | 14305.7 | +5.7% | −7.0% | 8.6% / 8.4% |
| 65536 / 1024 | 2 | 18045.6 | 17927.5 | −0.7% | −1.6% | 1.7% / 0.9% |

Every point has a same-arm drift of the same size as the difference between arms, so these do not change the gfx942 conclusion. The 64k rows carry only 2 and 4 requests per run, which is why their drift is the largest in the table.

### End to end on MI355X (gfx950), current main: five models

These runs used `_MAX_TOKENS = 128`, so concurrency 8 and up also substituted. The PR now substitutes only for 1-token batches, which the concurrency-1 rows measure; the other rows show what the wider bound did and why it was dropped.

Asked for in review: short and long context across several models. Every model below has a sigmoid router with a `noaux_tc` correction bias whose grouping eliminates nothing, so it reaches the substitution; the probe column is how many of the routing decisions a server makes while capturing its graphs took the Triton path (the rest are larger captured sizes, the profiling run and warm-up, which keep AITER).

`main` 3966924d with this PR, `rocm/vllm-dev:nightly-aiter-854189c-vllm-3966924d`, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, default CUDA graph settings. The base arm is the same tree with the substitution helper returning `False`, so the arms differ only in the router kernel. Blocks PR, base, PR, base, a fresh server per block, four runs per point with the first discarded; a block reports the median of runs 2-4 and an arm averages its two blocks. Output is 1024 tokens; inputs are real text (vLLM docs) cut to the stated length with each model's tokenizer. "Overlap" says whether any base run falls inside the range of the PR runs.

| model | experts / top-k | groups | weights | TP | substituted during capture |
|---|---|---|---|---:|---:|
| Moonlight-16B-A3B-Instruct | 64 / 6 | 1/1 | bf16 | 1 | 1482 of 8190 |
| Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct | 256 / 8 | 1/1 | bf16 | 1 | 494 of 2912 |
| MiniMax-M3.1-Flash (amd/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Quark-MXFP4) | 128 / 4 | 4/4, synthesised by `FusedTopKBiasRouter` | MXFP4 | 2 | 2166 of 12768 |
| GLM-5.3-Flash | 288 / 8 | 1/1 | FP8 | 2 | 1596 of 9408 |
| Kimi-K2.6 (amd/Kimi-K2.6-MXFP4) | 384 / 8 | 1/1 | MXFP4 | 4 | 13680 of 75840 |

**Moonlight-16B-A3B-Instruct** (64 / 6)

| input tokens | concurrency | base tok/s | PR tok/s | Δ throughput | Δ median TPOT | base block-to-block | PR block-to-block | overlap |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 1024 | 1 | 253.0 | 259.7 | +2.62% | -2.49% | 1.19% | 0.71% | no |
| 1024 | 8 | 1448.6 | 1459.3 | +0.73% | -0.71% | 1.42% | 0.73% | yes |
| 1024 | 32 | 4127.3 | 4134.1 | +0.16% | -0.38% | 0.97% | 0.14% | yes |
| 6144 | 1 | 223.5 | 228.5 | +2.23% | -2.21% | 0.88% | 0.14% | no |
| 6144 | 8 | 1304.2 | 1307.6 | +0.26% | -0.20% | 0.71% | 0.43% | yes |

**Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct** (256 / 8)

| input tokens | concurrency | base tok/s | PR tok/s | Δ throughput | Δ median TPOT | base block-to-block | PR block-to-block | overlap |

As concurrency grows the router becomes a smaller share of the step and the difference shrinks into the noise. The four negative points (-0.21% at most) all overlap with the base runs. Nothing regresses outside the same-arm drift.

Accuracy on the same build, lm-eval 0.4.9 `gsm8k` (1319 questions, 5-shot, greedy) through `/v1/completions`:

| model | base | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| GLM-5.3-Flash | 92.12% ± 0.74 | 92.04% ± 0.75 |
| Kimi-K2.6 | 93.48% ± 0.68 | 93.71% ± 0.67 |

One question apart on GLM, three on Kimi-K2.6, both inside the standard error. MiniMax-M3.1-Flash routes through a group count `FusedTopKBiasRouter` synthesises (128 experts, top-4, 4/4); at that shape the kernel selects the same experts as AITER on all 17040 rows of a randomised check (fp32 and bf16 gating and bias, 1-128 rows), max weight difference 7.45e-08.

An earlier A/B on Kimi-Linear, taken before the graph-capture fix, measured +0.07% to +0.16%; the probe shows that run never substituted, so it is not used.

### Accuracy on MI300X (gfx942)

A/B on Moonlight through the served endpoint, lm-eval 0.4.13.

**NIAH** (RULER, 4096): the three reported task scores match between arms — `niah_multikey_1` 1.00/1.00, `niah_single_2` 0.94/0.94, `niah_single_1` 0.00/0.00. The subtask scoring zero on both arms is inconclusive; this is task-level agreement, not per-sample output agreement.

**GPQA** (`gpqa_diamond_zeroshot`, 198 questions, loglikelihood). A first single-run A/B looked like +2.0 points for this PR. Three interleaved runs per arm show the difference changes sign:

| run | AITER | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| 1 | 0.3131 | 0.3333 |
| 2 | 0.3384 | 0.3182 |
| 3 | 0.3485 | 0.3283 |

AITER alone spans 0.3131–0.3485 across its own three runs.

Repeated on Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B, three interleaved runs per arm:

| run | AITER | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| 1 | 0.3889 | 0.4040 |
| 2 | 0.3990 | 0.4192 |
| 3 | 0.3990 | 0.4091 |
| median | 0.3990 | 0.4091 |

Here this PR is nominally higher in all three runs, by 1.0 point. **That is not claimed as an accuracy improvement**: 1.0 point is 2 questions out of 198, well inside the ±3.4 point standard error, and a routing difference confined to 0.15% of calls has no mechanism by which it could make a model more accurate. Taken with the Moonlight runs, these results show no regression, but are not sufficient to establish accuracy equivalence.

### Bias dtype

`rocm_aiter_ops.biased_grouped_topk` casts `correction_bias` to the gating dtype before dispatching, because AITER raises on a mismatch. A bf16 gating output next to an fp32 correction bias is a common router layout, so without the same cast the new path would score experts at a precision the replaced path never uses, and could select different experts. `sigmoid_bias_flat_topk` therefore makes the same cast at its own entry; Removing the cast fails 4 of the 6 cases in `test_flat_topk_casts_bias_like_aiter`; the other two shapes happen not to be sensitive to the bias precision.

### Known behavioural differences

| input | result |
|---|---|
| well-formed gating | weights agree to 2e-3 in unit tests; selected ids match on 4571 of 4576 live routing calls across two models |
| near-ties in the biased score | weights agree to 1.19e-07; the index chosen among near-equal experts may differ |
| NaN in gating output | **materially different from AITER** (6/10 synthetic configs, max weight delta 0.93) |

If maintainers would rather the gate reject non-finite input, that is a small addition to `can_use_sigmoid_bias_flat_topk`.

## Details

### Why the substitution sits at the wrapper

Review asked whether a model with no grouping should simply not be routed to `GroupedTopKRouter`. Two things make the wrapper the better place.

First, the advertised routing method is not a label. `layer.py:378` takes it from `router.kernel_routing_method_type` and stores it on the MoE config, where the AITER mxfp4 expert kernels consume it: `_supports_routing_method` lists `[Renormalize, RenormalizeNaive, DeepseekV4, DeepSeekV3]`, `self.renormalize` is derived from the same tuple, and the apply path branches on `DeepSeekV3` to pick `score_mode="sigmoid"`. `MiniMax2` is in none of them, so degenerating `num_expert_group` 1 → None would make those backends refuse these models and would flip `renormalize` to False for a checkpoint whose config says `norm_topk_prob: true`.

Second, and more decisively, changing the router would not remove the op. Calling `fused_topk_bias` directly — the routine `FusedTopKBiasRouter` uses — with a 64-expert, top-6 sigmoid+bias router on ROCm with AITER enabled:

```
synthesised group count for 64 experts: 2
biased_grouped_topk CALLED 1x with (num_expert_group, topk_group) = (2, 2)
```

`_aiter_get_num_expert_group` picks a divisor AITER has a kernel for, with `topk_group == num_expert_group` so the grouping is a no-op. A model moved off `GroupedTopKRouter` would still reach the grouped kernel, with a fabricated two-group configuration in place of its real single group.

Specialising at `rocm_aiter_ops.biased_grouped_topk` covers both callers, needs no routing-metadata change, and generalises the condition from "one group" to "no group is eliminated".

### Relation to #49870

[#49870](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49870) short-circuits the same degenerate shape for the case where AITER fused MoE is **not** enabled, which this PR does not touch.

### Scope and bounds

`can_use_sigmoid_bias_flat_topk` requires `topk_group >= num_expert_group`, a contiguous bias of exactly `num_experts`, and bounded token/expert/topk counts. The scoring function is not checked: at this call site the op is AITER's biased (sigmoid) top-k by construction, so matching that op is the contract. `_MAX_EXPERTS = 512` and `_MAX_TOPK = 8` are where the gfx950 measurements above stop showing a win: up to there the mean per shape is 1.16×–1.57× and no launch falls below 0.92×, even with a forced tie; at top-16 single tied rows pull launches to 0.62×–0.78×. An earlier revision of this PR accepted up to 1024 experts and top-32, set to cover the widest router in this family without having measured it there; the gfx950 sweep showed that was wrong, and those routers, Kimi-K3 (896 / top-16) among them, now keep AITER. `_MAX_TOKENS = 1` restricts it to single-token batches, one request decoding without speculation, where the end-to-end sweep shows a gain on every model; at larger batches the gain was within noise, so those keep AITER.

### Limitations

- Micro and unit tests on gfx942 and gfx950. The MI355X e2e and GSM8K runs are on current `main`; the gfx942 e2e, NIAH and GPQA runs are on an older build, see the next point.
- The e2e and accuracy comparisons used the container's own older vLLM build for both arms, because today's `main` cannot start against this image's AITER (`aiter.ops.flydsl.moe_common` missing, `fused_moe()` without `swiglu_limit`). Both arms are that same build differing only in this kernel. Unit and micro results are against `db3b0f0fa`.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Pooling] Fix scoring token limits with MistralTokenizer
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes #65075. Bi-encoder scoring with a positive `max_tokens_per_query` or `max_tokens_per_doc` failed with a `TypeError` for models served with `MistralTokenizer`, because `truncate_text_to_tokens` always requested `return_offsets_mapping=True`. For `MistralTokenizer`, the cut point now comes from the decoded token prefix instead.

## Claims

- `max_tokens_per_query` and `max_tokens_per_doc` now work with `MistralTokenizer` in `LLM.score()`, `/score` and `/rerank`. Before, any positive limit failed (HTTP 400 online), even one that truncated nothing.
- A binding limit cuts the text to a prefix of the original with at most that many tokens. On every input tested, the cut lands at the same point as the HF `offset_mapping` path for the same model. A non-binding limit leaves the text unchanged.
- HF tokenizers are unaffected: they keep the existing `offset_mapping` code.

## Validation

**Reproducer.** `mistralai/Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3` with the default `--tokenizer-mode auto`, which selects `MistralTokenizer`. Only tokenization matters, so dummy weights and one layer are enough:

```bash
vllm serve mistralai/Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3 --runner pooling --convert embed \
  --load-format dummy --hf-overrides '{"num_hidden_layers": 1}' \
  --enforce-eager --max-model-len 1024

curl localhost:8000/rerank -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
  "model": "mistralai/Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3",
  "query": "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog",
  "documents": ["A fox is a small omnivorous mammal."],
  "max_tokens_per_query": 3
}'
```

The same requests were also sent to `/score`, using `"queries"` instead of `"query"`. Both endpoints gave identical results:

| Limits in the request | `main` (76c6f3f2a9) | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| none | 200, 26 prompt tokens | 200, 26 prompt tokens |
| `max_tokens_per_doc: 100` (does not bind) | 400 | 200, 26 prompt tokens |
| `max_tokens_per_query: 3` | 400 | 200, 18 prompt tokens (query cut from 11 tokens to 3) |

Each 400 was `MistralTokenizer.__call__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'return_offsets_mapping'`.

**New tests.** Both fail on `main` with that `TypeError` and pass with this PR:

```bash
pytest tests/entrypoints/pooling/scoring/test_utils.py -k mistral -v               # main: 2 failed; PR: 2 passed
pytest tests/entrypoints/pooling/scoring/test_bi_encoder_offline.py -k mistral -v  # main: 1 failed; PR: 1 passed
```

<details>
<summary>Regression suites, cut-point comparison with the HF path, and the issue's script</summary>

Regression suites, all passing with this PR:

```bash
# 34 passed: the new unit tests plus the existing scoring unit tests
VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn pytest -v \
  tests/entrypoints/pooling/scoring/test_utils.py \
  tests/entrypoints/pooling/scoring/test_io_processor_unit.py \
  tests/entrypoints/pooling/scoring/test_jina_ranking_io_processor_unit.py

# 11 passed, including the moved Mistral test
VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn pytest -v \
  tests/entrypoints/pooling/scoring/test_bi_encoder_offline.py \
  tests/entrypoints/pooling/scoring/test_cross_encoder_offline.py

# 20 passed: exact prompt-token counts through /rerank with HF tokenizers on
# jina-reranker-v2, jina-reranker-v3, Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B, multilingual-e5-small
# and answerai-colbert-small-v1
pytest -v tests/models/language/pooling/test_max_tokens_per_doc.py
```

`pre-commit run --files` on the three changed files passes.

To compare cut points with the HF path, each repo was loaded with both `tokenizer_mode="mistral"` and `tokenizer_mode="hf"`. `truncate_text_to_tokens` then ran at every limit from 1 to the full length on 10 strings covering English, whitespace runs, newlines, accented Latin, CJK, emoji, code and punctuation:

| Model | Tokenizer | Identical cut points |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `mistralai/Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3` | SentencePiece | 164 / 164 (one string skipped: the two tokenizers already split its leading spaces differently) |
| `mistralai/Mistral-Nemo-Instruct-2407` | Tekken | 134 / 134 |

The issue's script calls `BiEncoderIOProcessor._truncate_scoring_data` with limits 0, 1 and 100. On `main`, 1 and 100 raise the `TypeError`. With this PR, 1 gives `['The']` / `['A']`, and 0 and 100 return the input unchanged.

</details>

**Model evaluation.** Not run. Outputs change only for requests that used to fail, and the HF path is untouched (see `test_max_tokens_per_doc.py` above).

## Details

**Root cause.** `truncate_text_to_tokens`, added in #38827, calls `tokenizer(text, add_special_tokens=False, return_offsets_mapping=True)` before checking the length. vLLM's `MistralTokenizer.__call__` has a fixed signature without that argument, so every positive limit raised, even for text already within it. Forwarding the argument would not help, because transformers' `MistralCommonBackend` raises a `ValueError` for `return_offsets_mapping=True`. This went unnoticed because `test_max_tokens_per_doc.py` only covers HF tokenizers.

**Who is affected.** Pooling models that end up with `MistralTokenizer`: either `--tokenizer-mode mistral`, or the default `auto` on official Mistral repos, such as `--convert embed` on `mistralai/Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3`. Bi-encoder, late-interaction and Jina-ranking scoring all go through `_truncate_scoring_data`, so they share the fix. Cross-encoder scoring already rejects `MistralTokenizer`. Popular Mistral-based embedding models (e5-mistral, SFR-Embedding-Mistral, Linq-Embed-Mistral) ship HF tokenizers and were never affected.

**Fix.** For `MistralTokenizer`, the helper encodes the text, decodes the first `max_tokens` ids, and cuts the original text at the length of that decoded prefix. The existing loop then re-encodes and repeats until the text fits, as on the offsets path. The result is therefore always a prefix of the original text and never exceeds the limit. `skip_special_tokens=True` is required: without it, `MistralTokenizer.decode` returns raw SentencePiece pieces (`'▁line▁one<0x0A>line'`), whose length doesn't match the original text.

**Why `is_mistral_tokenizer`.** `MistralTokenizer.is_fast` is `True`, so an `is_fast` check (what `HfRenderer._can_produce_offsets` uses) would still send it down the offsets path. The renderer's private method also isn't reachable from this helper. The cross-encoder processor uses the same `is_mistral_tokenizer` check to reject Mistral.

**Cost.** A binding limit usually takes two encodes, one to find the cut and one to confirm it, plus one decode of at most `max_tokens` ids. The worst case on the strings above was four passes. Only `MistralTokenizer` takes the new branch.

**Tests.** The unit test covers both Mistral tokenizer formats, SentencePiece and Tekken. The end-to-end test, in `test_bi_encoder_offline.py`, goes through `LLM.score()` with `PoolingParams(extra_kwargs=...)`. It checks that the prompt token ids match scoring `"What is the"` against the unchanged document. It uses dummy weights and one layer, so it downloads only config and tokenizer files (about 620 KB). It sets `gpu_memory_utilization=0.3` so it fits next to the file's module-scoped e5 engine. Both tests run in the "Entrypoints Integration (Pooling)" CI step.

**Not a duplicate.** No open PR references #65075. Two open PRs touch `return_offsets_mapping`, #61363 and #62691, but both change only renderer and tokenizer code, not the scoring helper. #62691 adds `return_special_tokens_mask`, not offsets, to `MistralTokenizer.__call__`.

No docs change: this adds no options, and the docs don't say Mistral tokenizers are unsupported.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Stop offline beam search at the context limit
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fix offline `LLM.beam_search()` raising `VLLMValidationError` when a beam reaches the model's context limit during generation. Return the completed beams instead of submitting another token step.

## Claims

- Mark beams that reach the context limit as completed with `finish_reason="length"`, preserving their tokens, logprobs and cumulative scores.
- Other prompts in the same batch continue generating.
- Candidate ranking and EOS handling remain unchanged.

## Validation

GPU validation used DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B with `max_model_len=128`, prompt lengths of 127, 124 and 16 tokens, and `max_tokens=8`.

- On base `c817cc0f8b`, the regression fails when beam search submits a subsequent request with 128 prompt tokens.
- With the fix, the three prompts return 1, 4 and 8 generated tokens per beam, respectively. Assertions cover token/logprob lengths, cumulative scores and `finish_reason="length"` for beams reaching the context limit.
- Existing beam-search tests: **74 passed, 5 deselected**.
- All applicable pre-commit hooks pass.

Original error:

```text
vllm.exceptions.VLLMValidationError: The decoder prompt (length 128) plus the number of requested output tokens (at least 1) is longer than the maximum model length of 128. Make sure that `max_model_len` is no smaller than the number of text tokens (prompt + requested output tokens).
```

Local validation used the branch's Python source with existing `d14f72c7fe` build artifacts, rather than a full native rebuild. TinyLlama and ROCm were not run locally.

The regression is included in the existing NVIDIA/AMD Samplers CI jobs:

```sh
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/samplers/test_beam_search.py \
  -k stops_at_context_limit_per_prompt -v
```

## Details

Offline beam search repeatedly submits one-token requests. Previously, candidates remained active after reaching the context limit, so the next request failed input validation.

After the existing candidate sort and beam-width selection, move full-context beams into the completed list with `finish_reason="length"`. This keeps termination independent for each prompt and reuses the existing final ranking. Initial prompts that leave no room for generation remain subject to the existing input validation.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Kernel] Fill K-padded output in silu_and_mul_nvfp4_quant
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes #48898. Under torch.compile, NVFP4 models whose per-rank MLP width K is 16 mod 32 (e.g. Qwen2.5-72B / Qwen2.5-VL-72B at TP=8, K = 3696) produce garbage once a batch has more than one token. The SiluMul+NVFP4 fusion replaces the K-padded `scaled_fp4_quant` of the CUTLASS NVFP4 linear (#42774) with `silu_and_mul_nvfp4_quant`, which writes that buffer with the unpadded row pitch. #63382 fixed the padded scale factors of this kernel; the row pitch is what remains.

## Claims

- `silu_and_mul_nvfp4_quant` writes a K-padded output the way `scaled_fp4_quant(..., padded_n=...)` does: row pitch and scale tile from the output width, zero data in the padding.
- Compiled output matches eager again on a padded-K model (perplexity 1290959 → 29.45, eager 29.43).
- Unpadded outputs keep the same addressing, and the kernel is not slower on any of the 24 shapes timed (−13% to +0.3%).

## Validation

RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (SM120), CUDA 13.4, torch 2.14.0+cu130. Base is main at 08e3f26, built in the same cmake tree.

| Check | Base | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Kernel test (`test_silu_mul_nvfp4_quant.py`) | 10 failed, 20 passed | 30 passed |
| Fusion pass tests (`test_silu_mul_quant_fusion.py`, `test_silu_mul_quant_manual_fusion.py`) | | 154 passed, 48 skipped |
| GEMM reproducer (K = 3696 → 3712, M = 4): relative error per row vs BF16 | 0.127, **1.533, 1.556, 1.532** | 0.127, 0.134, 0.138, 0.128 (same as unfused) |
| WikiText-2 perplexity, padded K = 4848, eager / compiled | 29.430 / **1290959** | 29.430 / 29.451 |
| Same, unpadded K = 4864, eager / compiled | 24.855 / 24.833 | 24.855 / 24.833 |

The perplexity model is `Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct` with its MLP narrowed to 4848 channels so that `down_proj` needs K padding on one GPU (ModelOpt `NVFP4_DEFAULT_CFG`, `--linear-backend cutlass`, 64 test texts).

<details>
<summary>Kernel time</summary>

`silu_and_mul_nvfp4_quant` in µs per launch: BF16 input, one CUDA graph of 200 launches whose inputs rotate through more than three times the 128 MB L2 (where memory allows), timed with CUDA events, mean of three alternating base/fix rounds; output buffers padded as the fusion allocates them. The base time for K = 3696 is for reference only, since that kernel writes the wrong layout.

| M | K = 3696 → 3712 | K = 4864 | K = 7392 | K = 14336 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1.27 → 1.24 | 1.39 → 1.34 | 2.01 → 1.97 | 1.82 → 1.79 |
| 16 | 1.38 → 1.31 | 1.54 → 1.45 | 2.07 → 1.98 | 2.93 → 2.60 |
| 128 | 2.70 → 2.60 | 2.89 → 2.64 | 4.50 → 3.91 | 6.43 → 6.09 |
| 1000 | 11.58 → 11.00 | 14.70 → 14.04 | 23.10 → 20.66 | 39.57 → 39.19 |
| 1024 | 11.90 → 11.35 | 15.02 → 14.27 | 23.36 → 21.11 | 40.67 → 40.19 |
| 8192 | 91.09 → 91.15 | 123.8 → 123.6 | 187.6 → 187.3 | 361.1 → 362.1 |

Both builds use 40 registers per thread.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Commands and GEMM reproducer</summary>

```bash
# Both arms from one build tree (only the kernel file differs)
cmake --build cmake-build-release --target _C_stable_libtorch -j 44

pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_silu_mul_nvfp4_quant.py
pytest tests/compile/passes/test_silu_mul_quant_fusion.py tests/compile/passes/test_silu_mul_quant_manual_fusion.py

# Kernel timing: for each (M, K) above, a CUDA graph of 200
#   torch.ops._C.silu_and_mul_nvfp4_quant(out, out_sf, x_i, global_scale) launches over rotating inputs x_i,
#   with out, out_sf from ops.create_fp4_output_tensors(M, K, device, True, padded_n=round_up(K, 32));
#   CUDA-event time of a replay / 200, median of 7 replays

# Model check: LLM(model, quantization="modelopt_fp4", linear_backend="cutlass", enforce_eager=True/False);
#   perplexity from prompt_logprobs over 64 WikiText-2 test texts
```

```python
import torch
from vllm import _custom_ops as ops
from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.nvfp4_utils import (
    pad_nvfp4_weight_for_cutlass, swizzle_blockscale)

rows, k, n = 4, 3696, 512
x = torch.randn(rows, 2 * k, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
weight = torch.randn(n, k, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda") * 0.02
y = torch.empty(rows, k, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
torch.ops._C.silu_and_mul(y, x)
w_gs = (448.0 * 6.0 / weight.abs().amax().float()).reshape(1)
w_fp4, w_sf = ops.scaled_fp4_quant(weight, w_gs, is_sf_swizzled_layout=False)
w_sf = swizzle_blockscale(w_sf.view(torch.float8_e4m3fn))
w_fp4, pad = pad_nvfp4_weight_for_cutlass(w_fp4)
x_gs = (448.0 * 6.0 / y.abs().amax().float()).reshape(1)
alpha = 1.0 / (x_gs * w_gs)
eager = ops.scaled_fp4_quant(y, x_gs, padded_n=k + 2 * pad)
fused = ops.create_fp4_output_tensors(rows, k, y.device, True, padded_n=k + 2 * pad)
torch.ops._C.silu_and_mul_nvfp4_quant(*fused, x, x_gs)
ref = y.float() @ weight.float().T
for name, (a, a_sf) in {"eager": eager, "fused": fused}.items():
    out = ops.cutlass_scaled_fp4_mm(a, w_fp4, a_sf.view(torch.float8_e4m3fn), w_sf, alpha, torch.bfloat16)
    print(name, [round(float((out[r].float() - ref[r]).norm() / ref[r].norm()), 3) for r in range(rows)])
```

</details>

## Details

**Root cause.** The fused kernel writes into the buffers allocated for the padded quant: `[M, (K + 16) / 2]` data and a 128x4 scale tile. It used K instead of K + 16 as the row pitch, so every row after the first is shifted against its scales. Single-token checks still pass. It also left the padded scale columns and rows unwritten (the stale-column failure analysed in #48898), which #63382 has since fixed.

**Fix.** The launcher passes the output width. The kernel takes the row pitch and the scale tile from it and writes the zeros it already computes for padded positions into the K padding. For an unpadded output the width equals K, so the addressing is the same as before. A `TORCH_CHECK` requires the output width to be a multiple of 16 that holds the input.

**Scope.** In practice only the down_proj input (K = intermediate size / TP) gets padded; the other quant fusions feed K = hidden size or heads × head_dim and are unchanged. Skipping the fusion for padded outputs would be simpler but would drop it on exactly these layers.

**Duplicate check.** #63382 fixed the padded scale factors but not the row pitch, so #48898 still reproduces on main (table above). #49092 and #49093 came out of the same investigation and fix other problems. #59467 (open) rewrites this kernel to add GELU-tanh; whichever lands second carries the padded-output handling, and I can rebase this one onto it.

**CI coverage and limitations.** The kernel test needs SM100+ and is skipped on CI's L4 runners; the `(B200) Fusion and Compile` job runs the two fusion tests. I validated on SM120 only, with a CUDA 13.4 build (16-element path; the 8-element path of CUDA < 12.9 builds has the same change but was not run). The model-level check used the narrowed 0.5B model on one GPU, not a TP=8 72B deployment.

**AI assistance.** This PR was prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code), which traced the root cause, wrote the fix and tests, ran the validation above and drafted this description.

commits.pr_title: [Kernel] Enable CuteDSL GDN prefill on SM110
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Lets the opt-in CuteDSL GDN prefill backend (`--gdn-prefill-backend cutedsl`) run on SM110 (Jetson Thor), and fixes its kernel launch on GPUs with fewer SMs than value heads. Related: #63284 rewrites the same selector function, so whichever PR merges second will need a small rebase. #62149 is a separate Thor GDN warmup crash that this PR does not fix.

## Claims

- `--gdn-prefill-backend cutedsl` now runs on SM110. Before, the selector fell back to Triton/FLA.
- On GPUs with fewer SMs than value heads, the CuteDSL kernels failed to launch with `CUDA_LAUNCH_INVALID_CONFIG`. Thor has 20 SMs and Qwen3.8-27B has 48 value heads. The kernels now launch at least one CTA per head.
- On Thor with `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B`, cutedsl lowers TTFT on 16k-token prompts by about 6% compared with triton. GSM8K is within error.
- `auto` makes the same choice as before on every platform. On SM10x, the larger grid size only takes effect for models with more than 148 value heads.

## Validation

Jetson AGX Thor (SM110, 20 SMs), CUDA 13.2, `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B` (BF16, `head_k_dim=128`, 48 value heads).

**Kernel test** (`tests/kernels/mamba/test_gdn_prefill_cutedsl.py`):

| | Result |
|---|---|
| Without the `num_sms` fix | 6 failed, 7 passed: every `num_v_heads=160` case raises `CUDA_LAUNCH_INVALID_CONFIG` in `kkt_inv_uw_cutedsl` |
| With the fix | 13 passed |

**End to end**, `--gdn-prefill-backend triton` vs `cutedsl` (startup logs confirm the selected kernel):

| Backend | GSM8K strict | GSM8K flexible | Mean TTFT (ms) | Median TTFT (ms) | P90 TTFT (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| triton | 0.7058 | 0.7339 | 16573.6 ± 8.9 | 16563.6 ± 11.8 | 16634.4 ± 14.0 |
| cutedsl | 0.6990 | 0.7240 | 15555.3 ± 1.0 | 15551.1 ± 1.6 | 15565.8 ± 6.6 |

- GSM8K: full 1319-question set, 5-shot. lm-eval reports a standard error of ±0.012–0.013 per score, so the −0.7 / −1.0 point differences are within noise.
- TTFT: 16k-token random prompts, 1 output token, concurrency 1, 16 prompts per run, 3 runs with seeds 1–3 (mean ± stdev). `max_num_batched_tokens=8192`, so each prompt is prefilled in two chunks.
- All 48 benchmark requests succeeded on both backends, and neither server log has errors.

CI has no SM110 runner. The B200 `Kernels` job runs the updated test, and its `num_v_heads=160` case exceeds the B200's 148 SMs, so it covers the grid fix.

<details>
<summary>Commands</summary>

```bash
pytest -v tests/kernels/mamba/test_gdn_prefill_cutedsl.py

vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B --max-num-seqs 8 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.8 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 --language-model-only --gdn-prefill-backend {triton,cutedsl}

lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k \
  --model_args model=Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B,base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=8,max_retries=3,tokenized_requests=False

vllm bench serve --model Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 16384 --random-output-len 1 --num-prompts 16 \
  --max-concurrency 1 --seed {1,2,3} --percentile-metrics ttft,e2el --metric-percentiles 50,90
```

</details>

## Details

- **Root cause:** `kkt_inv_uw_cutedsl` and `o_cutedsl` launch `grid = (num_sms // Hv, Hv, 1)`. When `num_sms < Hv`, the first grid dimension is 0 and CUDA rejects the launch. Both kernels now clamp the first grid dimension to at least 1 (`cutlass.max(num_sms // Hv, 1)`), which gives one CTA per head and also covers direct callers of the kernels. Both kernels loop over chunks with a stride equal to the grid size (`range(bid, num_global_chunks, grid_x)`), so the grid size doesn't affect results. `kernel_h` uses a `(Hv, N)` grid and isn't affected.
- **Selector:** SM11x with `head_k_dim == 128` and CUDA 13+ now allows CuteDSL. It doesn't allow FlashInfer, so `auto` still resolves to Triton on SM110.
- **Not a duplicate of #63284:** that PR splits "can run" from "preferred" for FlashInfer and CuteDSL, but doesn't add SM110 or touch the kernel grid size. If it merges first, this PR only needs SM110 added to its `can_run_cutedsl` check and its "targets SM100" error text updated.
- **Test gap:** no unit test checks that the selector picks CuteDSL on SM110. CI has no SM110 GPU, and faking the GPU type would need mocks. The startup log line from the Thor run is the evidence instead.
- **Docs:** the `--gdn-prefill-backend` help text now says where `cutedsl` works.
- AI assistance (Claude) was used to write and validate this change. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests and benchmarks above.

commits.pr_title: [Attention][DCP] Support DCP on the FlashMLA sparse bf16 KV path
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Enables decode context parallelism (DCP) for `FLASHMLA_SPARSE` with a bf16 KV cache. Until now the bf16 path raised `NotImplementedError` under DCP.

Related: #46514 (DCP for the `fp8_ds_mla` mixed-batch path, which added the bf16 guard), #61285 (`a2a` comm backend for the same backend).

## Claims

- `--kv-cache-dtype bfloat16` with `--decode-context-parallel-size > 1` now runs on `FLASHMLA_SPARSE`. On Hopper, no other sparse MLA backend supports DCP.
- GSM8K accuracy matches DCP1: 0.904 at DCP4 vs 0.894 at DCP1 on GLM-5.3-Flash.
- bf16 is not bound by the fp8 DCP limits (mixed-batch only, head envelope). For example, 32 local heads at DCP4 and 16 at DCP8 are accepted.
- On GLM-5.3-Flash, DCP4 holds 1.40× the KV tokens of DCP1.

## Validation

**Setup.** One GH200 node, 4× GPUs (96 GB, SM90). `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash`, TP4, `--quantization fp8` (weights only; the KV cache stays bf16).

**Unit tests.** `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py -k dcp`: 10 passed, 3 of them new.

**GSM8K.** `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py`, 500 questions, 5-shot, greedy, seed 42, CUDA graphs on. Both runs set `sparse_mla_force_mqa`, so prefill rows also take the changed path; otherwise GSM8K prompts (shorter than `index_topk`) would go to dense MHA and only decode would be tested.

| DCP | Accuracy | Invalid | Output tok/s |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 0.894 | 0.000 | 833 |
| 4 (`ag_rs`) | 0.904 | 0.000 | 726 |

The difference is within the ~1.3-point standard error at n=500.

**KV-cache capacity.** Same per-rank KV memory budget in each row.

| Mode | DCP1 tokens | DCP4 tokens | Ratio |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| eager | 225,475 | 315,665 | 1.40× |
| CUDA graphs | 216,892 | 302,557 | 1.39× |

<details>
<summary>Reproduction</summary>

```bash
# DCP1: drop the three DCP flags on the second line
vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --decode-context-parallel-size 4 --cp-kv-cache-interleave-size 4 --dcp-comm-backend ag_rs \
  --kv-cache-dtype bfloat16 --attention-backend FLASHMLA_SPARSE \
  --attention-config '{"sparse_mla_force_mqa": true}' \
  --quantization fp8 --max-model-len 8192 --max-num-seqs 128 --port 8000

python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 \
  --num-questions 500 --num-shots 5 --max-concurrency 64 --seed 42
```

- `--cp-kv-cache-interleave-size 4`: required by GLM-5.3-Flash's indexer KV compression (`compress_ratio=4`) under DCP.
- `--max-num-seqs 128`: keeps the per-request state blocks within memory for CUDA graph capture.

</details>

## Details

- **Root cause.** Under DCP each rank holds a shard of the KV cache, but the indexer emits global token ids. The bf16 path converted them with `triton_convert_req_index_to_global_index`, which treats every index as local, so it would read slots owned by other ranks. #46514 enabled DCP for fp8 only and added a guard rejecting bf16.
- **Fix.** `_forward_bf16_kv` converts top-k with `triton_filter_and_convert_dcp_index`, as the fp8 path and the sparse MLA base already do. Its compacted output and valid counts map directly onto `flash_mla_sparse_fwd`'s `topk_length`.
- **Empty rows.** For a row where this rank owns none of the selected tokens, `flash_mla_sparse_fwd` returns `lse=+inf` (FlashMLA `tests/ref.py`). Those rows are set to `-inf`, the identity of the cross-rank merge, as the fp8 path does. The output is made contiguous for the combine.
- **Guards.** The bf16 kernel returns the LSE for every token and pads the gathered heads itself, so the builder's mixed-batch and head-envelope checks now apply to fp8 caches only. PCP+DCP with bf16 and HiSparse+DCP are still rejected.
- **Cost.** bf16 KV is ~1.75× the size of `fp8_ds_mla`, so fp8 stays preferable where its DCP path applies. This PR covers the configs it rejects and deployments that need a bf16 cache.
- **Not a duplicate.** Searched open PRs and issues for "DCP FlashMLA sparse bf16" and "DCP sparse bf16 fp8_ds_mla". #54541 touches the same conversion but backports to v0.28.0, which predates #46514's guard.
- **Tests.** `test_bf16_dcp_skips_fp8_guards` covers the builder and `test_bf16_dcp_filters_topk_and_neutralizes_empty_rows` covers the forward path, both in `test_sparse_mla_backends.py`.

commits.pr_title: [UMBP][7/10] Add standalone mode backed by a node-local server
commits.pr_body:
This PR is split from the original full PR: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58568

Add the node-local UMBP server runtime and its endpoint and startup checks.
Share one DRAM pool across engines and DP ranks. vLLM does not start the server, and KV bytes stay on HIP IPC instead of the Unix socket.
Fail closed when the server is unreachable, reject pool-sizing and `dram_*` options, and hold stores while the shared pool is blocked.
Key the shared namespace on the effective model config (dtype, quantization, and `hf_config` after `hf_overrides`), so engines that share a model path but produce different KV never read each other's blocks.
Fail transfers queued behind a blocked store instead of waiting on them forever, and bound shutdown so a stalled server cannot hang worker close or process exit.

Implementation only. Usage is in the Standalone mode section of `docs/features/umbp_store_connector_usage.md`. Tests are in the next PR.

Commit: `e02b5bccd8`. Review slice of [vllm-project/vllm#58568](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58568) for [RFC #57187](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/57187). Related upstream draft: [vllm-project/vllm#59275](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59275).
