commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Attention] Bound SM100 decode indexer logits with query-row chunks
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

On SM100, compute the sparse indexer's decode logits in chunks of query rows, each at most `VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_MAX_DECODE_LOGITS_MB` (default 2 GiB), instead of one tensor for all decode rows of a step. This applies to every model that uses this indexer (DeepSeek-V3.2, V4, V4.1, GLM-5.x (`GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`), HY-V4), with either the FP8 (default) or the MXFP4 indexer cache.

It removes most of the memory these logits take at long context, and it unblocks the CUDA graph refactor (#63406), whose wide decode graphs would otherwise hold the full logits.

### Motivation

The sparse indexer scores every cached KV position of a request for each query row and keeps the top-k (512 for DeepSeek-V4/V4.1, 2048 for V3.2 and GLM-5.x). On SM100, the decode scores come from one DeepGEMM `fp8_fp4_paged_mqa_logits` call, which writes a dense BF16 tensor of shape `[decode rows, W]`:

- `decode rows` = requests × (1 + speculative tokens);
- `W` = `max_model_len / compress_ratio`, fixed by the model length, not by the requests' actual context.

At 1M context with 8192 decode rows this tensor is 16 GiB, and main's memory profile reserves it plus an FP32 copy (48 GiB). The copy is no longer made at runtime, since persistent top-k reads BF16 (#64138). The tensor costs memory in two places:

- **Eager and PIECEWISE steps** (mixed prefill + decode steps, and decode steps wider than the largest FULL graph) allocate it at runtime. So the memory profile reserves the worst case, and that memory is taken from the KV cache.
- **FULL CUDA graphs** allocate it inside the graph memory pool, which grows with the widest captured decode graph. #63406 captures decode graphs up to the full `max_num_seqs`.

### Change

When a step's decode logits would exceed the budget, the decode rows are split into balanced, 16-row-aligned chunks. Each chunk runs the same operations as the unchunked path on its own rows, and writes its rows of the shared top-k output:

1. DeepGEMM schedule metadata for the chunk;
2. logits;
3. V4.1 candidate-block selection or masking;
4. top-k.

Rows are independent, so nothing is merged across chunks. A step that fits the budget runs the existing single call unchanged, and so do prefill rows (already chunked by `VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_MAX_LOGITS_MB`). The memory profile reserves one BF16 chunk instead of every decode row plus an FP32 copy.

## Results

In every table, **Baseline** means decode logits are not chunked (main, or budget `0` on the same build), and **After PR** means this PR with the default 2 GiB budget. Unless noted: one GB200 node (4 GPUs), FP8 KV cache, DSpark with 7 speculative tokens for DeepSeek-V4.1, MTP with 5 for GLM-5.3, and ShareGPT prompts with their recorded output lengths. Memory numbers come from the startup log and are deterministic.

### Memory

On main (default memory settings, extensible KV cache):

| Model and config | | Baseline | After PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, FP8 indexer cache (default), 1M, TP4+EP, `max_num_seqs` 512 | memory-profile activation peak | 26.31 GiB | 5.23 GiB |
| | KV cache per GPU | 49.67 GiB | **86.02 GiB (+73%)** |
| DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, MXFP4 indexer cache, dense candidate consumers (`indexer_sparse_logits=false`), 1M, `max_num_seqs` 1024 | memory-profile activation peak | 49.49 GiB | 4.41 GiB |
| | KV cache per GPU | 7.62 GiB | **86.51 GiB** |
| GLM-5.3-NVFP4 (FP8 indexer cache), 256K, TP4+EP | memory-profile activation peak | 11.39 GiB | 4.37 GiB |
| | KV cache per GPU | 38.93 GiB | **51.25 GiB (+32%)** |

With #63406 (decode graphs up to `max_num_seqs`), CUDA graph memory per GPU, KV cache fixed:

| Model and config | Baseline | After PR |
|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, FP8 indexer cache, 1M, TP4+EP, 512 seqs | 22.36 GiB | **12.36 GiB** |
| DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, MXFP4 indexer cache, 1M, TP4+EP, 512 seqs | 22.35 GiB | **12.35 GiB** |
| DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, MXFP4 indexer cache, 1M, DP4+EP, 1024 seqs per rank | 39.70 GiB | **15.71 GiB** |

For GLM-5.3 at 256K with #63406, the widest decode graph (4092 rows) already fits the budget, so graph memory is unchanged (12.35 GiB). The smaller profile reservation still raises its KV cache from 590,464 to 745,984 tokens.

### Performance

Output tok/s; each cell lists every server launch, and the change is between the means. Launches of the two versions run on the same node unless noted.

| Setting | Workload | Decode rows per step | Baseline | After PR | Change |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| #63406, V4.1 FP8, TP4+EP | 512 concurrent | up to 4096, chunked | 13114 / 12939 | 13008 / 12834 | −0.8% |
| | 32 concurrent | up to 256 | 4045 / 4055 | 4050 / 3994 | −0.7% |
| #63406, V4.1 MXFP4, TP4+EP ¹ | 512 concurrent | up to 4096, chunked | 12828 / 12938 / 12808 | 12858 / 12759 / 12840 | −0.3% |
| | 256 concurrent | up to 2048, chunked | 11803 / 11772 | 11833 / 11848 | +0.4% |
| | 32 concurrent | up to 256 | 4091 / 4106 / 4076 | 4135 / 4097 / 3958 | −0.7% |
| #63406, V4.1 MXFP4, DP4+EP, AV ² | random 128 in / 512 out, 2048 concurrent | up to ~4096 per rank, chunked | 57855 / 55920 | 56854 / 56687 | −0.2% |
| | same, 4096 concurrent | up to 8192 per rank, chunked | 62059 / 61396 | 61297 / 61948 | −0.2% |
| #63406, GLM-5.3, TP4+EP | 256 concurrent | up to 1536 | 7155 | 7034 | −1.7% |
| | 32 concurrent | up to 192 | 2569 | 2597 | +1.1% |
| main, V4.1 FP8, TP4+EP | 512 concurrent | up to 4096, chunked | 5799 / 5920 | 5890 / 6067 | +2.0% |
| | 32 concurrent | up to 256 | 3509 / 3643 | 3548 / 3648 | +0.6% |
| main, V4.1 MXFP4, dense consumers, 1024 seqs | 512 concurrent | up to 4096, chunked | 5666 | 5550 | −2.0% |
| | 32 concurrent | up to 256 | 3324 | 3398 | +2.2% |
| main, GLM-5.3, TP4+EP | 256 concurrent | up to 1536 | 3966 | 4043 | +1.9% |
| | 32 concurrent | up to 192 | 2368 | 2409 | +1.7% |

¹ Budget sweep below; KV fixed at 16 GiB. ² Adaptive verification on, KV fixed at 16 GiB.

Steps that do not chunk run the same code as Baseline, so single-launch differences of about ±2% in those rows are run-to-run noise.

<details>
<summary>Other runs: long outputs, and a worst-case graph setup</summary>

Long outputs on main (V4.1 MXFP4, default candidate logits, 1M, TP4+EP, random 1K in / 4K out, one launch each):

| Concurrency | Chunked | Baseline | After PR | Change | TPOT p50 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 32 | no | 5280 | 4873 | −7.7% | 5.39 → 5.14 ms |
| 128 | no | 9972 | 9713 | −2.6% | 10.45 → 10.60 ms |
| 256 | yes | 4596 | 4488 | −2.3% | 46.2 → 49.0 ms |

The 32 and 128 rows run identical code in both versions, so they bound the noise of these short runs.

Worst case: `cudagraph_mode=FULL_DECODE_ONLY` with sparse capture sizes `[8, 128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192]` on main, V4.1 MXFP4, adaptive verification, KV fixed at 16 GiB, random 128 in. Every mixed step runs the whole model eagerly, so each extra chunk adds host launches.

| Topology | Workload | Baseline | After PR | Change |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DP4+EP, 1024 seqs per rank | 2048 concurrent, 512 out | 39226 / 40143 | 37518 / 36456 | −6.8% |
| | 4096 concurrent, 512 out | 34566 / 35732 | 24452 / 34633 | −16% (−1.5% without the 24452 launch) |
| TP4+EP, 1024 seqs | 1024 concurrent, 1024 out | 17054 / 15729 | 15973 / 16658 | −0.5% |

Deployments with this setup and workload should use the default `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` CUDA graphs, or raise `VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_MAX_DECODE_LOGITS_MB` (e.g. to 4096). Graph memory in this setup: DP4 36.46 → 12.44 GiB, TP4 32.08 → 10.12 GiB per GPU. With 2048 seqs, TP4 Baseline cannot start on main (its profile reserves 96 GiB for decode logits).
</details>

<details>
<summary>Choosing the 2 GiB default</summary>

#63406, V4.1 MXFP4, TP4+EP, 512 seqs, KV fixed at 16 GiB; one column per budget.

| | Baseline (0) | 1 GiB | **2 GiB** | 4 GiB | 6 GiB |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| CUDA graph memory | 22.35 GiB | 10.36 GiB | **12.35 GiB** | 14.35 GiB | 20.35 GiB |
| CUDA graph memory, adaptive verification | 22.51 GiB | 10.52 GiB | **12.52 GiB** | 14.51 GiB | 20.51 GiB |
| 512 concurrent | 12828 / 12938 / 12808 | – | 12858 / 12759 / 12840 (−0.3%) | 12906 / 12926 (+0.3%) | 12931 / 12757 (−0.3%) |
| 32 concurrent | 4091 / 4106 / 4076 | – | 4135 / 4097 / 3958 (−0.7%) | 4050 / 4095 (−0.6%) | 4114 / 4084 (0.0%) |
| adaptive verification, 512 concurrent | 16573 / 16815 / 16690 | – | 16149 / 17112 / 16944 (+0.3%) | 16819 / 17007 (+1.3%) | 16495 / 17060 (+0.5%) |
| adaptive verification, 512 concurrent, 9216 prompts | 18121 / 17942 / 17971 | 18059 / 18209 / 17912 (+0.3%) | 18082 / 17990 / 18041 (+0.1%) | – | – |
| adaptive verification, 128 concurrent | 10037 / 10134 / 10045 | 10245 / 10250 / 10098 (+1.2%) | 10224 / 10179 / 10150 (+1.1%) | – | – |

2 GiB is the smallest budget that leaves every step with up to 1024 decode rows at 1M (128 requests × 8 tokens) unchunked. 1 GiB saves 2 GiB more but chunks from 512 rows. 4 and 6 GiB keep 2 and 8 GiB more graph memory without a measurable gain.
</details>

### Correctness

**Chunked vs single call, on the real kernels.** A standalone check on GB200 runs DeepGEMM logits, candidate selection or masking, and the `auto` or `persistent` top-k. It compares chunking against a single call for FP8 and MXFP4 caches, 1000–8192 rows, W from 256K to 1M, and chunks down to ≤ 64 rows (which take the cooperative top-k and an FP32 upcast):

- chunked logits are bit-identical to the single call;
- candidate blocks are identical;
- the selected top-k values match an exact `torch.topk` on the same logits in every row (indices may differ only among tied scores).

The same check shows that main's single call returns a wrong top-k once one call exceeds 2^32 logits elements. At 1M context this happens above about 4094 rows: 4097 of 8192 rows were wrong, for both cache types and both top-k backends, while the logits themselves were correct. At the default budget a chunk holds at most 2^30 elements, so this PR avoids it. A separate fix for the top-k kernel's addressing will follow.

**GSM8K** (1319 questions, greedy). Same build launched repeatedly varies by up to ~1.8 points.

| Setting | Baseline | After PR |
|---|---|---|
| #63406, V4.1 FP8 | 0.904 / 0.901 | 0.898 / 0.899 |
| #63406, V4.1 MXFP4 | 0.900 / 0.904 / 0.897 | 0.913 / 0.897 / 0.895 |
| #63406, GLM-5.3 | 0.907 | 0.904 |
| main, V4.1 FP8 | 0.895 / 0.903 | 0.911 / 0.894 |
| main, V4.1 MXFP4, dense consumers | 0.897 | 0.893 |
| main, GLM-5.3 | 0.916 | 0.918 |

GSM8K runs 256 concurrent requests (up to 2048 decode rows for V4.1), so these runs exercise chunked steps.

**Unit tests.** `pytest tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py -k "decode_chunk or sparse_indexer or persistent"` on GB200: 348 passed, 4 skipped. The new tests check that chunks cover every row once, respect alignment, balance and the budget, and handle zero, fitting and invalid budgets.

## Details

- **Where it applies:** SM100, top-k backend `auto` or `persistent`, top-k ∈ {512, 1024, 2048}, no decode or prefill context parallelism. Both indexer cache types, and V4.1's candidate source and masked candidate consumer layers. V4.1's compact sparse consumers (`indexer_sparse_logits`) already score only candidate blocks and are unchanged.
- **Mixed steps:** chunking depends only on the number of decode rows, so it also applies to the decode rows of a mixed prefill + decode step; prefill rows are unchanged. These steps run PIECEWISE or eager, where each extra chunk adds a few kernel launches.
- **When to raise the budget:** a step chunks once its decode rows exceed `budget / (2 bytes × W)` on the widest indexer layer (1024 rows at 1M with the default). If running requests × (1 + speculative tokens) is usually above that and the KV cache is not the bottleneck, raise `VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_MAX_DECODE_LOGITS_MB` (for example to 4096). At 1M, keep it below 8192, where one call would exceed 2^32 elements; `0` turns chunking off.
- **Disaggregated prefill/decode:** prefill rows are unchanged, and prefill instances also get the smaller reservation. The decode instance produces the first token, so time to first token includes one decode step, which pays the chunking cost above if that step is wider than the limit.
- **Interaction with #64580:** #64580 would make SM100 logits FP32 again by default. Whichever PR lands second must pass the logits dtype to the chunk's `mqa_logits_mx_inputs` call and size the budget by the logits element size.
- **Models measured:** DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (FP8 and MXFP4 indexer caches) and GLM-5.3-NVFP4. DeepSeek-V3.2, V4 and HY-V4 run the same indexer code but were not measured end to end; at their usual context lengths (≤ 256K) decode steps chunk only above 4096+ rows, so the main change for them is the smaller memory-profile reservation.
- **Not covered:** decode context parallelism, non-default top-k backends (e.g. `deep_select`), the V4.1 GB300 specialized decode path, and indexers with their own implementation (GLM-5-Next, MiniMax-M3) keep their current path.

## Not a duplicate

#62169 chunks the SM90 / SM120 uniform decode path by request, and excludes SM100 varlen decode. No other open PR bounds the SM100 decode logits.

- build.sh: new `prebuild` mode that builds only the ROCm stack, from main, with the `Dockerfile.rocm_base` and `therock_wheels.py` of a maintainer-approved PR merged in, and pushes it only to the trusted repo
- build.sh: refuses to run if the PR moved past the approved SHA or if the stack inputs don't merge cleanly into main

When a PR changes the ROCm stack, main cold-builds it after merge (about 162 minutes for the AITER bump in #63774), and PR builds started in that window rebuild the same stack in parallel. #63949 stops the parallel rebuilds. commits.pr_title: [Perf][DCP] Sparse indexer: read the rank-major DCP top-k gather in place
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

The DCP sparse-indexer top-k merge (`_merge_dcp_topk_global`) all-gathers each rank's packed `(score, global_id)` candidates along dim 1. Since NCCL gathers along dim 0, `GroupCoordinator.all_gather` then reorders the result into `[rows, world_size * topk, 2]`: a full extra copy of every candidate. This PR gathers along dim 0 and lets the CuTeDSL selector read the rank-major `[world_size, rows, topk, 2]` buffer in place. The selected set is unchanged.

With `W` ranks, `R` rows and `K = topk` candidates per rank:

```python
# Before
packed = pack(local_topk)                    # [R, K, 2]  (score, global_id)
buf = nccl_all_gather(packed)                # [W*R, K, 2]  rank-major
gathered = buf.view(W, R, K, 2)              #              (free view)
           .movedim(0, 1)                    # [R, W, K, 2]
           .reshape(R, W*K, 2)               # [R, W*K, 2]  <-- full copy
selector(gathered)                           # one CTA per row r:
    for key_idx in range(W*K // 512):
        col = tid + key_idx * 512
        key = gathered[r, col]

# After
packed = pack(local_topk)                    # [R, K, 2]
buf = nccl_all_gather(packed)                # [W*R, K, 2]  rank-major
gathered = buf.view(W, R, K, 2)              # free view, read in place
selector(gathered)                           # one CTA per row r:
    for key_idx in range(W*K // 512):        # same loop, same keys
        rank = (key_idx * 512) // K          # compile-time constant (K % 512 == 0)
        cand = tid + (key_idx * 512) % K     # compile-time constant + tid
        key = gathered[rank, r, cand]
```

## Claims

- Removes the reorder copy from every DCP top-k merge (prefill and decode) of DSA models with a sparse indexer under DCP (DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5.x).
- Kernel level on B200 (6710 rows, DCP8, top-2048): the merge's gather-side work drops from 1438 µs (reorder copy + selector) to 839 µs (selector on the rank-major input; 838 µs on the row-major input, so reading in place costs nothing).
- End to end, in a downstream fork (internal DSA model, 8×B200, TP8 × DCP8, top-2048): prefill throughput +5–6% (TTFT −5 to −6%) over 5k–100k-token prompts.

## Validation

- `tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_dcp_localize.py`: 114 passed on B200. The selector test now feeds the rank-major layout and compares it with an fp64 reference over all candidates. The faked-gather merge tests follow the dim-0 gather.
- Downstream end-to-end benchmark (same container for both runs, 64 generated tokens, 3 iterations):

  | prompt | batch | prefill tok/s before | after | ratio |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | 5k | 1 | 12,746 | 13,411 | 1.05× |
  | 5k | 16 | 12,677 | 13,312 | 1.05× |
  | 20k | 1 | 14,356 | 15,218 | 1.06× |
  | 20k | 16 | 14,153 | 15,011 | 1.06× |
  | 50k | 4 | 13,554 | 14,334 | 1.06× |
  | 100k | 16 | 13,391 | 14,148 | 1.06× |

  Decode was unchanged there, but that fork serves decode-sized batches through a separate symmetric-memory exchange. Upstream's decode path goes through this merge too, and is not measured here.
- No public-model end-to-end run yet (e.g. DeepSeek-V3.2 or GLM-5.x with DCP).

## Details

- The selector's only caller is `_merge_dcp_topk_global`, which already requires `topk ∈ (512, 1024, 2048)`. So each rank contributes `topk` candidates, a multiple of the 512-thread block, and every 512-wide slice of a row's candidates falls inside one rank. Each thread key's `(rank, candidate)` is then a compile-time constant plus the thread index: no runtime division. The `CompileKey(topk, num_candidates)` and the selector's radix passes are unchanged.
- `stable_topk_from_gathered_candidates_cutedsl` now takes only the rank-major layout, asserting its shape.
- `get_warmup_keys` skips a pooled top-k (kpool indexers) that isn't a multiple of 512. The merge rejects such a top-k at runtime anyway, so warmup no longer compiles a kernel that can never run.
- Related open PRs touching the same code:
  - #59367 gathers into a rank-major buffer, then copies it to row-major for the selector. With this PR the selector could read that buffer directly and drop the copy.
  - #64129 changes the selector's key bits in the same kernel and merge function; whichever lands second will need a small rebase.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] FlashInfer: declare only KV layouts it can address
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes #59998. On non-SM100 GPUs, declare the five KV cache layouts FlashInfer can address, so layout resolution can no longer pick LHBNC.

### User case

1. FlashInfer on SM80/SM90/SM120 with `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=LHBNC`.
2. `FlashInferBackend.supported_kv_cache_layouts()` returns `None` there, so `resolve_kv_cache_layout` accepts LHBNC.
3. FlashInfer only takes NHD/HND pages; `get_flashinfer_layout_string` has no LHBNC entry.
4. The engine dies at startup on `AssertionError: KV cache layout LHBNC has no FlashInfer equivalent` (A100, Llama-3-8B) instead of rejecting the layout at resolution.

The fix returns the default preference order without LHBNC (LBNHC, LBHNC, BLNHC, BLHNC, BHLNC) instead of `None`.

Unchanged: the default layout (still LBNHC), the SM100 set, connector preferences (LBHNC and BLHNC stay valid), and every layout FlashInfer could already run.

Not a duplicate: no open issue or PR covers this. #46329 and #56550 add an SM120 branch to the same function but keep the `None` fallback. Related: #55431, #55312.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_attention_backends.py \
  -k test_flashinfer_declares_only_layouts_it_can_address
ruff check vllm/v1/attention/backends/flashinfer.py tests/v1/attention/test_attention_backends.py
ruff format --check vllm/v1/attention/backends/flashinfer.py tests/v1/attention/test_attention_backends.py
git diff --check
```

The new test patches the device capability to SM80/90/100/120 and checks that every declared layout maps through `get_flashinfer_layout_string` and that LHBNC is not declared.

## Test Result

```text
4 passed; on main 3 fail (SM80/90/120: supported_kv_cache_layouts() is None)
ruff check, ruff format --check (v0.14.0), git diff --check: passed
```

| A100, Llama-3-8B-Instruct, FlashInfer | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=LHBNC` | `AssertionError` during startup | `ValueError` at resolution listing the 5 valid layouts |
| default | LBNHC, serves | LBNHC, serves |

<details>
<summary>Test environment</summary>

- A100 80GB PCIe, driver 575.51.03, torch 2.13.0+cu129, flashinfer-python 0.6.18.post1.
- Unit test: main (1388100) with this patch, compiled extensions from the v0.30.0 wheel, run with `--noconftest` because the env lacks `tblib`; the test only uses `monkeypatch`.
- Engine check: v0.30.0 (ced6857) with the same patch. `supported_kv_cache_layouts` and `get_flashinfer_layout_string` are identical on v0.30.0 and main.
- The other five layouts also run in FlashInfer's attention benchmark on A100; LHBNC is the only one that asserts.

</details>

AI assistance (Claude) was used for the investigation, code and tests. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests on my own hardware.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][CI] Print the native backtrace of a fault in AMD CI pytest runs
commits.pr_body:
- `amd_ci_fault_trap.c`: a SIGSEGV, SIGBUS and SIGABRT handler that prints the native backtrace, naming the library that faulted, and then lets the fault proceed as before
- `amd_ci_fast_exit.py`: load it underneath Python's faulthandler, so a fault prints the Python traceback and then the native one; an image without the library runs as before, with a one-line warning
- `Dockerfile.rocm`: build the library into the test image (one `cc` call, cached unless the source changes)
- `test_amd_ci_fast_exit.py`, CI configs: tests for the report and for a missing library, run when the `.c` file changes

When an AMD CI job crashes in native code, Python's faulthandler shows only the Python frames, so the log does not say whether the fault came from HIP, the ROCm runtime, Ray or a vLLM extension; now every native fault in a pytest run also prints the native frames, while the job's result stays exactly what it was. This PR first also turned a fault after pytest's summary into pytest's own exit status, because of [vllm/ci #96786](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/96786), where every test passed and the process then died in interpreter teardown. #61939's fast exit now skips that teardown, no fault after the summary shows up in the AMD builds that ran with it ([15532](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/15532), [15739](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/15739)), and the mapping would also have turned a teardown SIGABRT green, so that part is dropped. The plugin keeps its name, so this does not conflict with #64132, which changes how the same plugin is installed. Follow-up to #61939; `pytest tests/tools/test_amd_ci_fast_exit.py` passes 11 tests (3 new) in 10 runs out of 10, and the library has not been built in AMD CI yet.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Step5] Require CDNA3 or newer for the sparse attention layers
commits.pr_body:
- model.py: `_validate_sparse` raises `NotImplementedError` when `get_cdna_version() < 3`.
- supported_models.md: the ROCm Step-5 note states the CDNA3 requirement.

Follow-up to #61837. The Step-5 entry point sends every ROCm GPU to `amd/`, so on CDNA2 or RDNA the model builds and loads its weights, then fails at the first CSA forward inside the FP8 indexer kernels with an error that never mentions the hardware. The NVIDIA path already raises at startup for unsupported compute capabilities. This does the same on ROCm. `< 3` keeps gfx1250, which reports CDNA5, eligible, since `_validate_sparse` already has a gfx1250-specific check. No open PR touches this check; #61945 changes the shared Step-5 kernels, not `amd/model.py`.

Tested on MI350X: `get_cdna_version()` returns 4, so the guard passes, and pre-commit is clean. The Step-5 model tests have not been rerun yet because the GPUs on my node are busy; I will add the results before marking this ready.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][Kernel][DSv4.1] Copy-based Q zero-pad for large eager mega-attention steps
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

  Makes the per-layer Q pad + KV insert of DeepSeek-V4.1 mega-attention layers **1.9-2.15x faster** on eager steps of 2048 tokens or more at TP2, with bit-identical outputs. On layers with 32 live heads padded to 64 (TP2 of a 64-head model), those steps
  now run the fused insert op in its existing KV-only mode and build the zero-padded, chunk-interleaved Q with a contiguous Triton copy, instead of padding Q inside the fused op.
  Part of #57448, on top of FlashMLA mega attention (#56935) and the interleaved V4.1 KV records (#61371); related: #58872, #55654, #60076 (see *Not a duplicate*).

  ## Claims

  - **1.9-2.15x faster Q pad + KV insert per layer** on eager steps of 2048-16384 tokens (2.10x at 8192 tokens; table below). With 32 live heads padded to 64, the Q half of the fused op reads 32 KiB and writes 64 KiB per token, against about 1.8 KiB for
  its KV half, and it writes Q one (token, head) slot per warp, in 16-element pieces `64 * 16` elements apart. The copy writes each token's 32 rows of 1024 elements contiguously.
  - **Bit-identical results:** the padded Q and the sliding-window KV cache bytes equal those of the fused launch (for NaN-free Q), so model outputs do not change.
  - **Narrow, automatic dispatch:** only eager steps with at least 2048 query tokens on mega-attention layers with 32 of 64 padded heads take the new path. Captured CUDA graphs, smaller steps, other shards (TP1/TP4/TP8 of a 64-head model), other attention
  backends and other platforms run exactly as before. There is no new flag, env var or config option.
  - **No new sync or memory:** the per-step decision reads only host metadata, and the padded Q tensor has the shape the op would have allocated itself. A full GSM8K run against a server started with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` detects no host sync.

  ## Validation

  **Kernel time** of the Q pad + KV insert per layer, fused op vs KV-only launch + copy (bf16, 32 live / 64 padded heads, `python bench_q_pad_copy.py` below: each arm replayed as a CUDA graph and timed with CUDA events, median; correctness asserted before
  timing; two runs agree to within 0.1%):

  | Tokens | **Speedup** |
  | ---: | ---: |
  | 512 | 1.61x (below the 2048-token threshold: keeps the fused op) |
  | 1024 | 1.87x (also below the threshold: the copy's extra eager launch eats this; see the 64-16384 sweep in the comments) |
  | 2048 | **1.93x** |
  | 4096 | **2.06x** |
  | 8192 | **2.10x** |
  | 16384 | **2.15x** |

  The shipped copy launch config (`BLOCK_ROWS=4`, 4 warps) is the fastest of the 12 configurations swept at 2048 tokens and tied fastest at 8192.

  <details>
  <summary>bench_q_pad_copy.py</summary>

  ```python
  """Fused Q pad + KV insert vs KV-only insert + _pad_interleaved_q (32 of 64 heads)."""

  import statistics

  import torch
  from flashinfer.testing import bench_gpu_time_with_cupti

  from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.attention import (
      _pad_interleaved_q,
      _pad_interleaved_q_kernel,
  )
  from vllm.triton_utils import triton

  LIVE, PADDED, D, ROPE, BLOCK, REC = 32, 64, 512, 64, 64, 528
  op = torch.ops._C.fused_deepseek_v4_qnorm_rope_kv_rope_quant_insert
  # After q_head_padded: eps, block_size, then the mega-attention layer's flags
  # apply_q_norm, kv_mxfp8, apply_q_rope and is_q_interleaved.
  TAIL = (1e-6, BLOCK, False, True, False, True)


  def bench_us(fn):
      times = bench_gpu_time_with_cupti(fn, use_cuda_graph=True, cold_l2_cache=True)
      return statistics.median(times) * 1e3


  def compare(n):
      q = torch.randn(n, LIVE, D, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
      kv = torch.randn(n, D, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
      pos, slots = torch.arange(n), torch.arange(n)
      cos_sin = torch.randn(n, ROPE)  # values do not affect timing
      cache_a = torch.zeros(n // BLOCK + 1, BLOCK * REC, dtype=torch.uint8)
      cache_b = torch.zeros_like(cache_a)
      out = torch.empty(n, PADDED, D, dtype=torch.bfloat16)

      def fused():
          return op(q, kv, cache_a, slots, pos, cos_sin, PADDED, *TAIL)

      def kv_only():
          op(q, kv, cache_b, slots, pos, cos_sin, 0, *TAIL)

      def copy():
          _pad_interleaved_q(q, out)

      # Correctness before timing: same cache bytes and Q bits as the fused launch.
      want = fused()
      kv_only()
      copy()
      assert torch.equal(cache_a, cache_b)
      assert torch.equal(out.view(torch.int16), want.view(torch.int16))

      t_fused, t_kv, t_copy = bench_us(fused), bench_us(kv_only), bench_us(copy)
      t_new = bench_us(lambda: (kv_only(), copy()))
      # Every byte read or written once: Q in, padded Q out, KV row, position,
      # slot and cos/sin row in, KV record out.
      nbytes = n * ((LIVE + PADDED) * D * 2 + D * 2 + 16 + ROPE * 4 + REC)
      print(
          f"{n:6d} {t_fused:9.1f} {t_kv:11.1f} {t_copy:8.1f} {t_new:11.1f} "
          f"{t_fused / t_new:7.2f}x {nbytes / t_fused / 1e3:11.0f} "
          f"{nbytes / t_new / 1e3:9.0f}"
      )


  def sweep(n):
      """Time the copy alone per launch config; the PR ships BLOCK_ROWS=4, 4 warps."""
      q = torch.randn(n, LIVE, D, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
      want = torch.empty(n, PADDED, D, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
      _pad_interleaved_q(q, want)
      rows = n * (D // 16)
      for block_rows in (1, 2, 4, 8):
          for num_warps in (2, 4, 8):
              out = torch.empty_like(want)
              run = _pad_interleaved_q_kernel[(triton.cdiv(rows, block_rows),)]
              args = (q, out, rows)
              kwargs = dict(
                  LIVE=LIVE * 16,
                  PAD=(PADDED - LIVE) * 16,
                  BLOCK_ROWS=block_rows,
                  num_warps=num_warps,
              )
              run(*args, **kwargs)
              assert torch.equal(out.view(torch.int16), want.view(torch.int16))
              t = bench_us(lambda run=run, args=args, kwargs=kwargs: run(*args, **kwargs))
              print(f"{n:6d} {block_rows:10d} {num_warps:9d} {t:8.1f}")


  torch.set_default_device("cuda")
  torch.manual_seed(0)
  print(torch.cuda.get_device_name(), "torch", torch.__version__)
  print("tokens  fused_us  kv_only_us  copy_us  kv+copy_us  speedup  GB/s(fused, new)")
  for n in (512, 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192, 16384):
      compare(n)
  print("tokens  BLOCK_ROWS  num_warps  copy_us")
  for n in (2048, 8192):
      sweep(n)
  ```

  </details>

  **In serving** (TP2, mega attention selected explicitly, Engram offload and indexer settings as in the DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash recipe). 8192-token steps are above the default CUDA-graph capture sizes, so they run eagerly and take the new path: the torch
  profiler of an 8192-token prefill shows `_pad_interleaved_q_kernel` (server flag `--profiler-config '{"profiler": "torch", "torch_profiler_dir": "./prof"}'`, then the bench command below with `--profile --num-prompts 2`).

  ```bash
  vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 2 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
    --attention-config '{"backend":"FLASHMLA_MEGA_ATTN_DSV41","indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4","indexer_sparse_logits":true}' \
    --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}' \
    --max-model-len 16384 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --no-enable-prefix-caching

  vllm bench serve --backend vllm --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
    --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1 \
    --num-prompts 128 --max-concurrency 16
  ```

  **Correctness: unit tests** (CUDA GPU with the `_C` extension built):

  ```bash
  pytest -v "tests/kernels/test_fused_deepseek_v4_qnorm_rope_kv_insert.py::test_q_interleaved_pad_copy_matches_fused_insert"
  pytest -v tests/kernels/test_fused_deepseek_v4_qnorm_rope_kv_insert.py
  pytest -v "tests/kernels/test_compressor_kv_cache.py::test_v41_pcp_swa_cache_matches_non_pcp_writer"
  ```

  | Test | Result |
  | --- | --- |
  | `test_q_interleaved_pad_copy_matches_fused_insert` (new) | 6 passed |
  | `test_fused_deepseek_v4_qnorm_rope_kv_insert.py`, whole file | 221 passed |
  | `test_v41_pcp_swa_cache_matches_non_pcp_writer` | 2 passed |

  The new test runs the KV-only launch plus `_pad_interleaved_q` and the fused launch on the same input at 17, 1024 and 2049 tokens (both sides of the op's `NUM_TOKEN_CUTOFF`), with and without 5 trailing DP-padding rows that have no slot. It requires
  identical cache bytes and identical padded-Q bits, with the copy writing into a NaN-filled buffer.
  **Lint:** `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` (0.14.0), `typos`, `py_compile` and the local pre-commit hooks (`check_spdx_header`, `check_forbidden_imports`, `check_torch_cuda`, `check_boolean_context_manager`, `check_init_lazy_imports`,
  `validate_config`, `check_test_tethering`) pass on the four changed files, and so does the pre-commit mypy hook (`tools/pre_commit/mypy.py`, Python 3.11).

  **CI coverage:** the new test is in `tests/kernels/test_fused_deepseek_v4_qnorm_rope_kv_insert.py`, which `:nvidia: (H100) DeepSeek V4 Kernels`, `:nvidia: (B200) DeepSeek V4 Kernels` and the `:amd: (MI355 DPX) DeepSeek V4 Fused Kernels` mirror run. This
  PR's test change triggers them, but their `source_file_dependencies` do not list `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/attention.py`, so a later change to the copy alone would not re-run the test; I can add it if wanted. `test_compressor_kv_cache.py` runs in
  `:nvidia: (B200) Miscellaneous Kernels`. No CI job serves mega attention at TP2 (the DeepSeek-V4.1 GSM8K config in CI is TP4, where the copy is off), so the serving check above is a manual run.

  ## Details

  **Motivation.** Mega attention applies Q RoPE itself and reads Q chunk-interleaved: per token, 32 chunks of `[heads, 16]` with the padding heads at the tail of every chunk. The V4.1 layer norms `qr` before `wq_b`, so the Q half of
  `fused_deepseek_v4_qnorm_rope_kv_rope_quant_insert` is a pure zero-pad in that layout. With 32 live heads padded to 64 it reads 32 KiB and writes 64 KiB per token, against about 1.8 KiB for the KV half sharing the launch, so on large steps the op's time
  is mostly the Q pad. The op processes Q one (token, head) slot per warp, and in this layout a head's 16-element lane chunks sit `padded_heads * 16` elements apart; the copy instead writes each (token, chunk) row of 1024 elements contiguously.

  **Design.**
  - `_pads_q_by_copy` is set once per layer: the layer reads Q interleaved (`accepts_unnormed_unroped_query`), has 32 live heads padded to 64, and `max_num_batched_tokens >= 2048`. Such layers register `_pad_interleaved_q` for JIT warmup, so the first
  long prefill does not compile it.
  - Per step, `_fused_qnorm_rope_kv_insert` takes the copy when the layer qualifies, the step has at least 2048 tokens and the current stream is not capturing. The op then runs with `q_head_padded=0`, the KV-only mode TP1 mega attention already uses on
  main: it schedules no Q slots and runs the same per-token RoPE, MXFP8 quantization and paged insert, skipping DP-padding rows as before (`fused_deepseek_v4_kv_rope_insert` launches the same KV kernel; passing 0 keeps the existing call).
  `_pad_interleaved_q` then writes the padded Q into a fresh `[num_tokens, 64, 512]` tensor.
  - `_pad_interleaved_q` is a Triton kernel over `num_tokens * 32` rows, one per (token, 16-dim chunk): 512 live elements copied, then 512 zeros. It goes through `triton_kernel_dispatcher_with_warmup` like other warmed Triton launchers.
  - 1024 equals the op's `NUM_TOKEN_CUTOFF`, where it switches to its reduced-grid kernel; smaller steps keep one launch. The copy would also win at 512 tokens (1.61x above), but steps that small normally run inside captured CUDA graphs, which keep the
  fused pad.
  - The branch lives in the shared `_fused_qnorm_rope_kv_insert`, next to the existing interleaved-Q handling; a mega-attention override would have to duplicate that method's KV-insert setup.

  **Exactness.** With norm and RoPE off, the op's live-Q path converts bf16 to fp32 and back with no arithmetic in between, which reproduces every non-NaN value bit for bit, and it stores +0.0 in the padding slots. The copy moves the bits unchanged and
  stores the same +0.0. The KV half runs the same code in both modes, and the test compares the cache bytes with `rtol=0, atol=0`.

  **Tradeoffs and limitations.**
  - Eligible steps issue two launches instead of one; the extra Triton launch is host-side overhead that large prefill steps hide.
  - Only the 32-of-64 shard qualifies: with 16 or 8 live heads a chunk's padding is 768 or 896 columns, not the power of two `tl.arange` needs, so TP4/TP8 keep the fused pad.
  - Work captured into a CUDA graph keeps the fused pad, so the copy applies only where this method runs outside stream capture: by default, steps above the largest captured size; under Model Runner V1, whose wide eager region spans this method, also
  captured sizes of 1024 tokens or more.
  - Deployments that select another attention backend (for example FlashInfer sparse MLA) are unaffected.
  - The CUDA op is unchanged; reworking its interleaved Q stores would keep a single launch, but in a kernel shared by every DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 backend.

  **Compatibility.**
  - Backends and platforms: the FlashMLA sparse, FlashInfer and ROCm layers do not read Q interleaved, so `_pads_q_by_copy` is false for them; mega attention itself is SM10x-only. DeepSeek-V4 (non-4.1) code is untouched.
  - TP sizes (64-head model): TP1 (64 live heads) already skips the pad; TP2 takes the copy; TP4 and TP8 are unchanged.
  - Prefill context parallelism (#59857) selects the FlashMLA layer, so it never reaches the copy; the stand-in layer of `test_v41_pcp_swa_cache_matches_non_pcp_writer` now declares `_pads_q_by_copy=False`, since that test calls
  `_fused_qnorm_rope_kv_insert` on it. The SM90-only token-sharded `fused_wqa_wkv` (#58872) never meets mega attention, and `forward_kv` (decoder replay) builds no Q.
  - CUDA graphs: capture keeps the fused pad, so captured graphs are unchanged. Batch invariance: both paths produce the same bits, so taking the copy (which depends on the step's token count) changes no result.
  - CPU/GPU sync: none added; the decision reads `q.shape[0]`, a flag set at init and the stream's capture state.

  **Not a duplicate.** On 2026-10-18 I searched open PRs and PRs since 2026-08-15 for "pad interleaved q", "qnorm rope kv insert", "Q pad mega" and "heads padded 64 decode"; none moves the mega-attention Q pad out of the fused insert. Related work: #56935
  added mega attention and the fused interleaved pad this PR bypasses on large eager steps; #61371 changed the V4.1 KV record, which both launch modes share; #58872 added the token-sharded `fused_wqa_wkv` whose `_SHARD_FUSED_WQA_WKV_MIN_TOKENS` sits next
  to the new constant; #60076 (open) switches the ROCm DSpark context-KV insert to the existing KV-only `fused_deepseek_v4_kv_rope_insert` and touches neither mega attention nor its Q pad (it and this PR edit different tests in
  `tests/kernels/test_compressor_kv_cache.py`). #55654 (open) adds KV-only insert ops (`fused_deepseek_v4_kv_rope_quant_insert`, and `fused_deepseek_v4_kv_norm_rope_quant_insert` with kv_norm folded in) so DeepSeek-V4's DSpark `_insert_context_kv` no
  longer builds a dummy query. This PR adds no KV op and touches neither DSpark nor DeepSeek-V4: it calls the existing `q_head_padded=0` mode of the fused op from the V4.1 attention layer. That path also sees DP-padding rows (more KV rows than slots),
  which the fused op's KV-only mode skips and #55654's ops reject. The only file both PRs touch is `tests/kernels/test_fused_deepseek_v4_qnorm_rope_kv_insert.py`, where each adds tests.

  **AI assistance.** AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to develop this change, port it onto current main, run vLLM's `pr-checklist` skill and draft this description. I reviewed every changed line and ran the validation reported above.

  ---

  <details>
  <summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>
  <summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

  - [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][HiSparse] Avoid the MNNVL FlashInfer all-reduce with HiSparse
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes #64327. Unblocks #63801.

FlashInfer's MNNVL fused all-reduce + residual + RMSNorm has a cluster-barrier race (flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#7782). The vLLM default single-node backend has been MNNVL since #61989. With HiSparse running host-memory gathers on its copy stream, the race fires and the engine dies with `CUDA error: unspecified launch failure` (Xid 13 `CTA Not Present`).

With HiSparse enabled and `VLLM_FLASHINFER_ALLREDUCE_BACKEND=auto`, backend selection now:
- single node: uses `trtllm`;
- multi-node: disables FlashInfer all-reduce, since `trtllm` doesn't support multi-node groups.

An explicit `VLLM_FLASHINFER_ALLREDUCE_BACKEND` setting is still respected. This is temporary: the check should be removed once vLLM picks up a FlashInfer release with #7782.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/distributed/test_comm_ops.py -k "flashinfer_auto_backend or workspace_failure or standalone_workspace"
```

## Test Result

Server check that the new path runs: 4× H100 (driver 580.126.09), `main` + #63801 (Python side; kernels from the `main` precompiled wheel) + this PR, GLM-5.3 config with dummy weights cut to 5 layers, HiSparse with spec decode. Same build, same load; the only difference is the backend env var.

```bash
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 VLLM_FLASHINFER_ALLREDUCE_BACKEND={mnnvl,auto} \
vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3 -tp 4 --enforce-eager --load-format dummy \
  --hf-overrides '{"num_hidden_layers": 5, "first_k_dense_replace": 5, "indexer_types": ["full", "full", "full", "shared", "shared"]}' \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla --kv-cache-memory-bytes 4G \
  --max-model-len 67584 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-num-seqs 32 --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}' \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"HiSparseConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"host_pool_gib":16}}'

# 6 waves, seeds 1..6
vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 52000 --random-output-len 1024 \
  --random-range-ratio 0.25 --num-prompts 32 --max-concurrency 32 --ignore-eos --seed $seed
```

| `VLLM_FLASHINFER_ALLREDUCE_BACKEND` | Fused AR workspace | Result | Output tok/s (mean of 6 waves) |

commits.pr_title: [MiniMax-M3.1][P/D] NIXL KV-head re-sharding for per-head-contiguous NVFP4 pages
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

NIXL can now move MiniMax-M3.1's NVFP4 KV cache between prefill and decode instances that run different TP, e.g. prefill TP1 and decode TP4. Split out of #63232 (MiniMax-M3.1-Flash). Based on `main`; it does not depend on the other PRs of that split.

## Claims

- **Heterogeneous-TP NVFP4 transfers:** NIXL re-shards an NVFP4 KV page across heterogeneous TP when the attention spec declares that the page is laid out by KV head (`AttentionSpec.kv_head_major_slots`). MiniMax-M3's MSA NVFP4 backend declares it.
  - Today every NVFP4 cache is rejected under heterogeneous TP (#61865), because in FlashInfer's NVFP4 page a head's bytes are not contiguous.
  - FlashInfer NVFP4 stays rejected.

## Validation

Unit tests on GB200:

```bash
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_desc_geometry.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py
```

573 passed. In this environment, the two `test_abort_timeout_on_prefiller` cases need the venv's `ninja` on `PATH`.

New tests:

- `test_nvfp4_kv_head_major_slots_match_insert` checks the layout claim on real bytes.
  - It runs the fused QK-norm/RoPE/KV-insert kernel for a TP1 page, and again for each decode rank's subset of KV heads.
  - Slicing the TP1 page at the spec's per-head byte offsets must give each rank's page byte for byte.
  - Passed on GB300 with the first revision. The review fixes do not touch the kernel, the spec or this test, and it was not re-run.
- `test_attention_merge_preserves_kv_head_major_slots` checks that every spec merge keeps the flag.
- `test_handshake_rejects_nvfp4_kv_head_split` now also covers heterogeneous TP (4→1 and 1→4) with the flag set, which the handshake accepts.

End to end: MiniMax-M3.1 NVFP4 KV with P/D, prefill TP1 → decode TP4 on GB300. The P/D result matched the non-P/D run:

| | P/D | non-P/D |
|---|---|---|
| passkey | 9/9 | – |
| gsm8k | 0.97 | 0.97 |

That run used an earlier revision of this change, in which the backend exposed an attribute that the connector looked up, instead of the spec flag. It was not re-run on this branch. The MSA NVFP4 backend supports only LBHNC, so the BLHNC packed-row code removed during review was never on that run's path.

## Details

A request's KV path under P/D, as this PR changes it:

1. Prefill (TP1, Hkv KV heads) writes NVFP4 pages with 2·Hkv slots. Slot 2h holds head h's K (E2M1 data, then scales) and slot 2h+1 its V. Each head is therefore one contiguous run of S = page_size / Hkv bytes.
2. The NIXL handshake compares the specs. With `kv_head_major_slots`, the NVFP4 heterogeneous-TP guard from #61865 is skipped, and descriptors are registered per KV head at byte offset h·S, the same as for a dense page.
3. Decode rank r (TP4, Hkv/4 heads) reads its heads' contiguous byte range of each prefill page into its own page, which has the same layout.

- **Where the flag lives:** on `AttentionSpec`, so the connector needs no backend lookup. Every spec merge copies it. ROCm's MSA NVFP4 (FlyDSL layout) does not set it.
- **Review changes:**
  - The first revision also sent the packed BLHNC rows of non-MLA models as whole rows. That broke heterogeneous TP for dense BLHNC caches (e.g. FlashInfer on SM100, P TP1 → D TP2): the peers' `packed_member_layouts` differ, and the handshake rejects the connection. Before this PR, per-layer descriptors handled it. That part is reverted, so non-MLA BLHNC registers per layer as before. MiniMax NVFP4 needs LBHNC and does not use it.
  - The local `packed_storage` in `register_kv_caches` is renamed to `replicated_shared_storage`, because `_has_packed_cache` already means packed storage.
- **Not a duplicate:** no open PR touches NIXL NVFP4 heterogeneous TP. #62107 (separate K/V head slots for unquantized FlashInfer KV) is a different layout.

Credits: Dao Le (per-head NVFP4 page layout) is a co-author in the commit. AI assistance (Claude) was used to split this change out of #63232, to address review comments and to draft this description. The submitter reviewed the change and ran the tests above.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Keep GPTQ linear layers batch invariant
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

With `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, `AutoGPTQLinearMethod` still runs the Marlin GEMM. Marlin picks its tiling and K-split from the number of tokens, so the reduction order changes with the batch size and the logprobs depend on the batch.

This PR makes the GPTQ path use `matmul_batch_invariant` directly: in batch-invariant mode it skips the Marlin kernel selection and repacking, keeps the checkpoint layout in memory, and unpacks the weight in `apply()`.

(The matching AWQ change was part of this PR until 2026-10-19 and was dropped: on current `main` the AWQ fallback is already batch invariant through #52231, which overrides `aten::mm.out`/`aten::addmm.out`; #60013, which this PR deferred to, was closed for the same reason.)

## Claims

- On `main`, `tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py` fails for `Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-GPTQ-Int4` (14 of 22 ids). With this PR all 22 ids pass.
- Accuracy is unchanged: `lm_eval` gsm8k on the batch-invariant path matches the Marlin path within noise, and the top-1 tokens of the two GPTQ paths agree on a fixed prompt set.
- Without `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT` nothing changes: the same Marlin kernel is selected.
- Throughput in batch-invariant mode is lower than on `main` (numbers below): the GPTQ weight is dequantized on every forward and the model uses the batch-invariant Triton matmul instead of Marlin.
- New unit test checks the GPTQ unpack against vLLM's reference packer bit for bit.

**7. Unit test**

```text
python -m pytest -v tests/kernels/quantization/test_gptq.py
======================= 14 passed, 14 warnings in 5.62s ========================
```

## Details

**Root cause.** `vllm/model_executor/determinism/batch_invariant.py` overrides `aten::mm`/`aten::matmul` through `torch.library` and exposes `matmul_batch_invariant` for callers; linear methods that run their own kernels have to opt in. `AutoGPTQLinearMethod` never did: it always builds a Marlin `MPLinearKernel`. The same pattern is why `UnquantizedLinearMethod` calls `linear_batch_invariant` explicitly.

**Change.**
- `auto_gptq.py`: with `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, `AutoGPTQLinearMethod` skips `verify_marlin_supported` / `choose_mp_linear_kernel`, leaves `qweight`/`scales`/`qzeros` in the checkpoint layout, and `apply()` unpacks the weight (`(q - bias) * scale` in the scales dtype, the same arithmetic as the Marlin dequantization) and calls `matmul_batch_invariant`. Without the flag the code path is unchanged.
- `tests/kernels/quantization/test_gptq.py`: `_dequantize_gptq_weight` is compared bit for bit against `gptq_quantize_weights` + `gptq_pack` for 4/8 bit, group sizes -1/32/128, fp16/bf16.

**Trade-offs and limitations.**
- The GPTQ weight is unpacked on every forward in batch-invariant mode, and the model runs the batch-invariant Triton matmul instead of Marlin. On the A10 this costs throughput in batch-invariant mode (blocks in section 6): the decode-heavy benchmark takes about 2.5x longer than `main`'s non-invariant Marlin path, the prefill-heavy one about 1.4x. Keeping a dequantized copy would be faster but would need the memory of the unquantized model, which is usually why a GPTQ checkpoint is used. A fused batch-invariant W4A16 Triton kernel would remove the cost; I kept that out of this PR.
- Only symmetric GPTQ without act-order is covered, which is what `AutoGPTQLinearMethod` supports today (`desc_act=True` is rejected at config time).
- `AutoGPTQMoEMethod` (GPTQ MoE experts) still uses Marlin MoE and is not batch invariant; #46639 covers that kernel. (The compressed-tensors wNa16 dense scheme was fixed separately in #60524.) This PR covers the dense GPTQ path that was tested.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][Kernel] Convert two FP8 values per cvt in the FP8 quant kernels
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Follow-up to #60927: the FP8 `cvt` instruction converts two values at once, but our scalar helper issues it with a zero partner. On sm_100+ this change quantizes pairs with `__nv_cvt_float2_to_fp8x2` and lets the saturating `cvt` replace the explicit clamp. Output is bit-identical to `main`.

## Claims

- **Speedup, bit-identical output:** RMSNorm + FP8 per-token/per-block quant is 1.05–1.24x faster; static, dynamic per-tensor and per-token `scaled_fp8_quant` are 1.00–1.08x faster; `merge_attn_states` with FP8 output is up to 1.03x faster. All measured on B300 with bf16/fp16/fp32 inputs.
- **No meaningful small-batch regression:** among bf16 cases, the worst at ≤128 rows is 0.98x.
- **One arch gate:** the switch is `VLLM_FP8_CVT_X2` in `csrc/core/cuda_compat.h` (`VLLM_FP8_CVT_X2_MIN_ARCH 1000`, matching #60927). The per-token-group packed path from #60927 now uses it too, with identical SASS. Hopper and older keep today's code; ROCm is unchanged.
- **All-zero input:** dynamic per-tensor quant of an all-zero tensor now writes zero bytes. On `main` it writes 448 with a 0 scale: `0 * (1/0)` is NaN, and only the clamp turned that into 448.

## Validation

**Bit-exactness.** I dumped the raw outputs (FP8 bytes and scales) of every touched op from a build of `main` and from this branch, then compared them exactly. Coverage: bf16/fp16/fp32 inputs, hidden sizes 17/1030/2048/4096/5120, aligned and unaligned views, static, per-tensor, per-token (with and without `scale_ub`), 1x128 groups, fused RMSNorm (FP8 and int8, with and without residual) and `merge_attn_states`. Result: 0 of 515 output tensors differ.

I also checked all 2^32 fp32 bit patterns: clamp-then-`cvt` and `cvt` alone agree on every non-NaN input, and the software `c10::Float8_e4m3fn` cast matches the hardware `cvt` on every non-NaN input. NaN is the only difference: it now stays FP8 NaN instead of becoming +448.

**Tests** (B300):

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_fp8_quant.py tests/kernels/core/test_fused_quant_layernorm.py \
  tests/kernels/core/test_fused_silu_mul_block_quant.py tests/kernels/core/test_layernorm.py \
  tests/kernels/attention/test_merge_attn_states.py tests/kernels/test_fused_quant_activation.py \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_block_fp8.py
# 5118 passed, 164 skipped
```

The new `test_dynamic_per_tensor_fp8_quant_all_zero` fails on `main` and passes here.

After rebasing onto `main` with #60927 and switching its gate, the per-token-group SASS is byte-identical to the old gate. Re-ran tests on that build:

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_per_token_group_quant.py tests/kernels/quantization/test_fp8_quant_group.py \
  tests/kernels/quantization/test_fp8_quant.py tests/kernels/attention/test_merge_attn_states.py
# 3704 passed
```

Re-validated after merging `main` at e92bac311c, on a B300: 5803 passed across the FP8 quant, group quant, fused quant, layernorm and `merge_attn_states` kernel suites. Raw outputs again match a build of that `main`, 0 of 515 tensors differ. The performance numbers below are from the original branch; the kernel sources are unchanged since then.

**Performance.** FlashInfer `bench_gpu_time_with_cupti` with CUDA graphs and cold L2, median, on one B300. 526 cases: batch 1–8192, hidden sizes 4096/5120/7168/2880/1030/1025/17, bf16/fp16/fp32, plus unaligned views. Each build ran twice in alternating order (base, new, new, base); I report the min of the two runs. Run-to-run variation was ≤1% in nearly every case. Overall geomean is 1.023x.

Speedup vs `main`, bf16, geomean over hidden sizes:

| op | 1 row | 32 | 128 | 512 | 2048 | 8192 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `scaled_fp8_quant` static | 1.01 | 1.01 | 1.01 | 1.01 | 1.02 | 1.05 |
| static, 1x128 group scales | 1.04 | 1.04 | 1.04 | 1.03 | 1.03 | 1.02 |
| dynamic per-tensor | 1.01 | 1.01 | 1.00 | 1.02 | 1.03 | 1.04 |
| dynamic per-token | 1.00 | 1.00 | 1.00 | 1.01 | 1.02 | 1.02 |
| `rms_norm_dynamic_per_token_quant` | 1.05 | 1.04 | 1.04 | 1.08 | 1.10 | 1.10 |
| `rms_norm_per_block_quant` (1x128) | 1.11 | 1.10 | 1.10 | 1.18 | 1.20 | 1.24 |

Example absolute times (bf16, hidden 4096):

| op | rows | `main` (us) | this PR (us) |
|---|---|---|---|
| static quant | 8192 | 20.96 | 19.39 |
| dynamic per-tensor | 8192 | 37.12 | 34.75 |
| `rms_norm_dynamic_per_token_quant` | 2048 | 32.67 | 27.62 |
| `rms_norm_per_block_quant` | 8192 | 102.91 | 83.75 |
| `merge_attn_states` FP8 (2048 tok, 128 heads x 128) | — | 42.88 | 41.60 |

Hidden sizes 1030, 1025 and 17 are flat (1.00x geomean): they mostly take the unchanged scalar prefix/tail path.

<details>
<summary>CUPTI benchmark script</summary>

```python
"""CUPTI + CUDA-graph, cold-L2 timing of the FP8 quant ops. usage: cupti_bench.py out.json"""
import json, os, statistics, sys
OPS = os.environ.get("OPS")
OPS = OPS.split(",") if OPS else None
import torch
from flashinfer.testing import bench_gpu_time_with_cupti
from vllm import _custom_ops as ops

FP8 = torch.float8_e4m3fn
torch.manual_seed(0)
dev = "cuda"

def bench_us(fn):
    for _ in range(25):
        fn()
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    t = bench_gpu_time_with_cupti(fn, use_cuda_graph=True, cold_l2_cache=True,
                                  repeat_time_ms=150)
    return statistics.median(t) * 1e3

ROWS = [1, 2, 8, 32, 128, 512, 2048, 8192]
HIDDEN = [4096, 5120, 7168, 2880, 1030, 1025, 17] if not OPS else [4096, 2880, 5120]
res = {}
for dtype in (torch.bfloat16, torch.float16, torch.float32):
    dn = str(dtype).split(".")[-1]
    hiddens = HIDDEN if dtype == torch.bfloat16 else [4096, 1030]
    rows_l = ROWS if dtype == torch.bfloat16 else [1, 32, 2048]
    for hidden in hiddens:
        for rows in rows_l:
            x = (torch.randn(rows, hidden, device=dev) * 3).to(dtype)
            w = (torch.rand(hidden, device=dev) + 0.5).to(dtype)
            out = torch.empty(rows, hidden, device=dev, dtype=FP8)
            sc = torch.tensor([0.0371], device=dev)
            dsc = torch.empty(1, device=dev)
            tsc = torch.empty(rows, 1, device=dev)
            resid = (torch.randn(rows, hidden, device=dev)).to(dtype)
            tag = f"{dn}/{hidden}/{rows}"
            cases = {
                "static": lambda: torch.ops._C.static_scaled_fp8_quant(out, x, sc, None),
                "dyn_tensor": lambda: torch.ops._C.dynamic_scaled_fp8_quant(out, x, dsc),
                "dyn_token": lambda: torch.ops._C.dynamic_per_token_scaled_fp8_quant(out, x, tsc, None),
                "rms_static": lambda: torch.ops._C.rms_norm_static_fp8_quant(out, x, w, sc, 1e-6),
                "add_rms_static": lambda: torch.ops._C.fused_add_rms_norm_static_fp8_quant(out, x, resid, w, sc, 1e-6),
                "rms_dyn_token": lambda: torch.ops._C.rms_norm_dynamic_per_token_quant(out, x, w, tsc, 1e-6, None, None),
            }
            if hidden > 64:
                xv = x[:, 1:-15] if hidden % 16 == 0 else x[:, 1:]
                outv = torch.empty(xv.shape, device=dev, dtype=FP8)
                cases["static_unaligned_view"] = lambda: torch.ops._C.static_scaled_fp8_quant(outv, xv, sc, None)
            if hidden % 128 == 0:
                gsc = torch.rand(rows, hidden // 128, device=dev) * 0.05 + 0.01
                bsc = torch.empty(rows, hidden // 128, device=dev)
                cases["static_group128"] = lambda: torch.ops._C.static_scaled_fp8_quant(out, x, gsc, (1, 128))
                cases["rms_block128"] = lambda: torch.ops._C.rms_norm_per_block_quant(out, x, w, bsc, 1e-6, None, None, 128, False)
            if dtype == torch.float32:
                cases.pop("add_rms_static", None)
            for name, fn in cases.items():
                if OPS and name not in OPS:
                    continue
                try:
                    res[f"{name}/{tag}"] = bench_us(fn)
                except Exception as e:
                    print("skip", name, tag, type(e).__name__, str(e)[:80])

# merge_attn_states with fp8 output
for T, H, D in [] if OPS else [(1, 16, 512), (64, 16, 512), (4096, 16, 512), (2048, 128, 128)]:
    p = (torch.randn(T, H, D, device=dev) * 0.1).bfloat16(); s = (torch.randn(T, H, D, device=dev) * 0.1).bfloat16()
    pl = torch.randn(H, T, device=dev); sl = torch.randn(H, T, device=dev)
    o = torch.empty(T, H, D, device=dev, dtype=FP8); ol = torch.empty(H, T, device=dev)
    sc = torch.tensor([0.02], device=dev)
    res[f"merge_fp8/bfloat16/{H}x{D}/{T}"] = bench_us(lambda: ops.merge_attn_states(o, p, pl, s, sl, ol, None, sc))

json.dump(res, open(sys.argv[1], "w"))
print("cases", len(res))
```

</details>

## Details

- **Design:** `scaled_fp8_conversion_vec<is_scale_inverted, fp8_type, N>` in `w8a8/fp8/common.cuh` is the one helper. It pairs elements under `VLLM_FP8_CVT_X2` and otherwise, or for an odd tail, falls back to the existing scalar `scaled_fp8_conversion`. That scalar function is unchanged.
- **Call sites:** `common.cu` reaches the helper through a small functor that passes both a scalar op and a 16-wide op to `vectorize_with_alignment`. The fused RMSNorm kernels reach it through a new `ScaledQuant::quant_vec_fn` (a plain loop for int8).
- **Zero scale:** skipping the clamp means `0 * inf` would yield FP8 NaN, so every site that feeds an inverted scale into the paired path uses `fp8_reciprocal_scale`, which returns 0 for a zero scale. It measured as free.
- **Left out after measuring:**
  - Pairing in `rms_norm_static_fp8_quant` gained 3–6% at ≥512 rows but cost 1–3% at small batches.
  - Pairing in `fused_add_rms_norm_static_fp8_quant` gained nothing.
  - Removing the clamp from the scalar path was about 2% slower in those kernels.
  - Pairing while keeping the clamp was up to 15% slower on small static quant.
  - `silu_and_mul_quant` and SiTU quant were flat.
- **Known regression:** static quant on fp32 input with hidden 1030 at 2048 rows is 4.5% slower (9.54 → 9.98 us). That branch's source is unchanged, so this is a codegen side effect of the neighbouring changes in the same kernel. bf16/fp16 on the same shape are 1.01x.
- **Hopper:** the instruction exists from sm_89, but I could only validate on Blackwell. Lowering `VLLM_FP8_CVT_X2_MIN_ARCH` is the one change needed once validated on other GPUs.
- **CI coverage:** the quantization kernel tests run on L4 (sm_89) and MI300, which take the unchanged path. The sm_100+ path was validated locally on B300 as above.
- **End to end:** no serving benchmark. Output is bit-identical, so accuracy evals are unchanged by construction. The gains are prefill-weighted; decode-size launches move by ≤11% on the fused RMSNorm quant ops and ≤4% elsewhere.
- **Not a duplicate:** #60927 (merged) covers only `per_token_group_quant`. The open #41115 changes the per-token kernel's launch configuration on a since-moved file, not the conversion.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Core] Keep KV cache zeroing for mixed-precision UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs groups
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Preserve KV cache zeroing when mixed-precision `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs` groups are reduced for the scheduler. Resolve the zeroing decision across workers so pipeline stages agree even when only one stage has mixed precision. Split out of #63232 (MiniMax-M3.1-Flash); this change remains independent of the other split PRs.

## Claims

- Scheduler projection preserves the decision to zero newly allocated attention blocks.
- All PP workers initialize zeroing when any worker requires it. This prevents MRV2 from receiving zeroing work on a stage without a zeroer.
- Uniform-precision attention-only configurations continue to skip zeroing.

## Validation

The same regression tests were run on original PR head `998f165a2ab0ce47f63ff280b96a600901c7d914` and this revision.

| Check | Original PR head | This revision |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Config matrix: uniform, mixed first stage, mixed second stage | 1 passed, 2 failed (`False is True` on a uniform worker) | 3 passed |
| Related scheduler, Mamba, and PP config tests | Not rerun | 7 passed |
| Qwen3-0.6B, MRV2, PP=2, FP8 KV, BF16 layer 0 | Worker_PP1 asserted that `kv_block_zeroer` is not None; first completion returned HTTP 500 | 1 passed; PP=2 and PP=1 first-token top-5 logprobs match at the helper's precision |
| Pre-commit on the seven changed files | Not rerun | Passed |

CPU commands (with `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 PYTHONPATH=$PWD CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=''`):

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py \
  -k test_generate_scheduler_kv_cache_config_keeps_zeroing -q
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_planning.py \
  -k 'test_generate_scheduler_kv_cache_config or test_wrapped_mamba_group_requires_block_zeroing or test_get_kv_cache_configs_pp_sharding' -q
```

GPU command, run through Slurm with two visible GB200 GPUs and cached real weights (before: job 40854, 1 failed; after: job 40859, 1 passed in 171.17 s):

```bash
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 PYTHONPATH=$PWD CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/distributed/test_pipeline_parallel.py \
  -k test_pp_mixed_precision_kv_cache -v -s --tb=short
```

The regression compares PP=2 against PP=1 using the existing `generate_close` helper: greedy first-token top-5 logprobs rounded to two decimal places. Both revisions use the same existing native build. This validates the Python configuration/zeroing path with Qwen, not MiniMax native operators or model accuracy on a benchmark. No performance claim is made.

The E2E test is included in the existing pipeline/context parallelism CI steps, with dependencies added for the changed core files. NVIDIA coverage is in the existing optional nightly step; AMD coverage uses its existing PR step. AMD was not run locally.

## Details

`generate_scheduler_kv_cache_config` reduces each `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs` to one layer spec. Recomputing mixed precision after that reduction loses information. Saving only worker 0's mixed-precision result also leaves PP workers inconsistent: a uniform stage skips zeroer initialization although it receives the scheduler's `new_block_ids_to_zero`.

`has_mixed_precision_kv_cache` remains a local fact. `needs_kv_cache_zeroing` becomes a stored execution decision, initialized from each worker's full configuration. The planner ORs that decision across workers after final replanning, and scheduler projection preserves it through deepcopy. The tradeoff is that uniform stages also zero new attention blocks when another stage requires zeroing.

This extends the metadata-preservation fix in #49623 to intra-group precision and PP worker agreement. It is not a duplicate of the open fixes for transfer destinations/tails (#62313, #55085), backend-specific block reuse (#58716), or initial allocation zero fill (#59432).

AI assistance was used: Claude for the original split, and OpenAI Codex for this follow-up implementation, regression tests, and validation.

commits.pr_title: [Model Loader] Refill weight-derived tensors in place on every post-load rerun
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Keep tensors derived from weights (kernel constants, inverse scales, decode copies) at their startup addresses when post-load processing reruns on a weight reload, so captured CUDA graphs read the new values instead of freed memory. Part of the direct weight reload work (RFC #54477, rule 3). Builds on #64357 (merged); replaces aoshen02/vllm#180.

> **Direct reload.** #64336 (direct reload core) is now in main, and this branch has main merged. The direct reload tests that waited on it are back in this PR (see Validation). Results marked "direct" were measured with #64336 on both arms, before it merged.

## Claims

- After a weight reload with CUDA graphs on, MoE models whose post-load step derives kernel tensors serve the same output as before the reload. Without this PR they collapse:
  - gpt-oss-20b (TRT-LLM MXFP4, direct reload): GSM8K 0.39 → 0.01;
  - Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4 (CuteDSL): 0.90 → 0.01 with direct reload, 0.93 → 0.00 with layerwise reload.
- With direct reload (#64336), every tensor the MoE kernel reads keeps its cold-start address across a reload on these backends: TRT-LLM MXFP4/NVFP4, CuteDSL NVFP4 (including per-locality-domain shards), FlashInfer CUTLASS NVFP4/FP8, and per-tensor FP8 (including TRT-LLM FP8 per-tensor's shuffled weights).
- After a draft-model weight update, the tensors the V2 speculator's FULL CUDA graph reads (DFlash/DSpark context K/V weights and norms, including Beam's DFlash2 and Kimi-K3's DSpark drafters) keep their addresses. Without this PR, Beam DFlash2 acceptance fell from 7.03 to 4.89 after an update.
- The same holds for linear kernels that derive tensors in their post-load step (CUTLASS/Triton INT8 asymmetric `azp_adj`, CUTLASS W4A8, Marlin W4A8-INT8/FP8, b12x NVFP4 W4A16, ModelOpt block-quant), for the ROCm gpt-oss MXFP4 AITER shuffles, Kimi-K3 AMD `_w_fold` and the bf16x3 router split, and for MXFP4 MoE on Marlin (gpt-oss-20b GSM8K 0.43 → 0.00 after a reload without this PR, 0.45 → 0.43 with it).
- Humming MoE: its post-load step runs once per quant method; direct reload refuses it (in main with #64336).
- Across 17 served models with direct reload (3 full-checkpoint updates each, measured by aoshen02), GSM8K holds after every update with this PR; on main it collapses on 8 of them (e.g. gpt-oss-120b 0.80 → 0.006, Kimi-K3 0.95 → 0.25).
- No cold-start change: GSM8K, throughput and KV cache match the base on 12 model/backend configurations, all within noise.

## Validation

All runs are on GB200 with nightly `4b47db922` plus this branch's Python files. "Base" = main `255431b5e` + #64357 + #64336.

**Reload with CUDA graphs on.** Start a server on a checkpoint, then record greedy tokens and top-1 logprobs on 8 fixed prompts (one request at a time) and a 300-question GSM8K slice. Push 2 weight updates through the NCCL weight-transfer engine and record the same again. "Greedy = fresh" compares with a fresh server on the last checkpoint sent; for a same-weight update the fresh server is the one before the update.

| Model, MoE backend, reload mode | Update | Base: GSM8K pre → post, greedy = fresh | This PR: GSM8K pre → post, greedy = fresh |
|---|---|---|---|
| gpt-oss-20b, TRT-LLM MXFP4, direct | same weights ×2 | 0.390 → **0.013**, 0/8 | 0.393 → 0.413, **8/8** |
| gpt-oss-20b, TRT-LLM MXFP4, direct | 2 perturbed variants | → 0.007 (fresh 0.007), **0/8** | → 0.003 (fresh 0.003), **8/8** |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4, CuteDSL, direct | same weights ×2 | 0.903 → **0.007** | 0.927 → 0.900 |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4, CuteDSL, layerwise | same weights ×2 | 0.927 → **0.000** | 0.923 → 0.910 |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 (block), TRT-LLM FP8, direct and layerwise | same weights / perturbed | 8/8 | 8/8 |

- The "this PR" MXFP4/NVFP4 rows ran on `a4a859064`; the FP8 rows ran on this PR's first commit (`deaba72c6`). Since then the FP8 and MXFP4/NVFP4 paths changed only in comments and type annotations, and the direct-reload-only branch of `replace_parameter` moved to #64336.
- The perturbed variants flip the low bits of every FP4/FP8 payload and scale the scales by 2^k. These models score ≈0 themselves, so those rows are judged by token equality with the fresh server.
- One perturbed gpt-oss run (job 41424) gave 0/8 against the fresh server. This was not reproducible: three reruns gave 8/8.
- **NVFP4 CuteDSL** is not bit-reproducible across servers: two cold starts agree on 0–2 of 8 greedy sequences. GSM8K is its signal.
- **FP8 block quant** has no per-tensor derived constants, so it is a no-regression row.

**Served reload across models (aoshen02, [review](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64692#issuecomment-6543567448)).** Direct reload, GSM8K before → after 3 full-checkpoint updates, main vs this PR plus the review commits (aoshen02/vllm#227, now on this branch). Model runs used the tree before the final simplification commit, and before the ModelOpt gather-copy fix.

| Model | Cluster | main | This PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| gpt-oss-120b | GB300 TP2 | 0.803 → **0.006** | 0.807 → 0.813 |
| gpt-oss-120b (chat) | GB200 | 0.940 → **0.005** | 0.939 → 0.941 |
| gpt-oss-20b | GB300 | 0.422 → **0.017** | 0.425 → 0.423 |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4 (CuteDSL) | GB300 | 0.908 → **0.000** | 0.903 → 0.903 |
| Muse Spark NVFP4 | GB200 TP4 | 0.949 → **0.002** | 0.945 → 0.951 |
| Beam NVFP4 (TRT-LLM) | GB200 | 0.941 → **0.019** | 0.945 → 0.945 |
| Kimi-K3 (MXFP4 TRT-LLM MoE) | GB300 TP8×2 | 0.954 → **0.246** | 0.954 → 0.948 |
| Step-5 NVFP4 (CUTLASS) | GB300 TP4 | 0.930 → **0.014** | 0.925 → 0.933 |
| DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash | GB300 TP2 | 0.897 → 0.909 | 0.902 → 0.904 |
| Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 | GB300 | 0.466 → 0.475 | 0.460 → 0.470 |
| GLM-5.3-Flash FP8 | GB200 | 0.921 → 0.923 | 0.920 → 0.916 |
