commits.pr_title: [ROCm][CI] Gate MoRI EPv2 modular-kernel cases on the production EPv2 checks
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Since #61361, `:amd: (MI300) MoE Kernels Multi-GPU` fails on main ([amd-ci#15761](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/15761)): all 3 `MoriEPv2PrepareAndFinalize` cases hit a MoRI assertion on MI300X. This test-only PR registers MoRI EPv2 in the modular-kernel harness only where production would select it.

## Claims

- The MI300 Multi-GPU step passes again. The MoRI EPv1 and DeepEP cases are unchanged.
- MoRI EPv2 cases are generated only on gfx950/gfx1250 with MoRI >= 1.2.4, the conditions `RocmPlatform.check_and_update_config` uses.

## Validation

MI300X, `rocm/vllm-dev:ci_base` with MoRI 1.2.3.post1 (as in CI), 2 GPUs:

```bash
cd tests
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 pytest -v -s kernels/moe/test_modular_kernel_combinations.py -k multigpu
```

| | main | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| Collected | 33 | 30 |
| MoRI EPv2 / EPv1 cases | 3 / 8 | 0 / 8 |
| Result | 3 failed, 30 passed | 30 passed |

On main, the EPv2 cases fail locally with the CI error: `AssertionError: combine block_num 304 exceeds xdb_flag_slots 256`.

## Details

The harness sets `mori_ep_v2=True` for the `"mori"` backend. That skips the EPv1 fallback production uses unless MoRI >= 1.2.4 is installed and the GPU is gfx950/gfx1250. On MI300X, MoRI's untuned EPv2 path uses one combine block per CU (304), above its fixed limit of 256. [ROCm/mori#876](https://github.com/ROCm/mori/pull/876) fixes this, but no MoRI release includes it yet.

AI-assisted tooling was used to analyze the CI logs, write the change, and run the validation. The change and the results were manually reviewed.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][MM] Keep FlashInfer cu_seqlens halves aligned in Qwen3-VL encoder CUDA graph replay
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

With `mm_encoder_attn_backend=FLASHINFER` and encoder CUDA graphs enabled, Qwen3-VL image replays copy the packed FlashInfer `cu_seqlens` into the capture buffer with `EncoderCudaGraphManager._copy_padded_buffer`. That copy misaligns the q/k/o and v halves of the packed tensor. The vision encoder output then differs between replays of the same image and from eager mode. This registers the existing Qwen2.5-VL helper `_pad_flashinfer_cu_seqlens_buffer` (from #42796) for Qwen3-VL through `EncoderCudaGraphConfig.padding_logics`. SyaOtiLan found the instability and ran the GPU validation below while testing #63809, which adds the same hook for Qwen3-Omni.

## Claims

- Qwen3-VL encoder CUDA graph replays on FLASHINFER keep each half of the packed `cu_seqlens` in its own half of the capture buffer. In the tested cases, replays are identical and match eager mode on the same padded buffers.
- Other attention backends use `_pad_cumulative_seqlens_buffer`, as Qwen2.5-VL does (changed in 3b80be3 after review). It repeats the last offset, so padded entries are zero-length sequences, while the default copy filled them with zeros. The default copy gave no wrong output in the FLASH_ATTN replays of the earlier GPU runs below, and the GPU run of 3b80be3 below shows exact replays on both backends.

## Validation

CPU unit tests (no GPU) in `tests/v1/cudagraph/test_encoder_cudagraph.py`, class `TestFlashInferCuSeqlensPadding`:

```
pytest tests/v1/cudagraph/test_encoder_cudagraph.py -k FlashInferCuSeqlens
```

On this branch, 8 pass. The test pads replay `cu_seqlens` with the padding function Qwen3-VL registers (falling back to `_copy_padded_buffer`, as replay does) and checks that the result equals the `cu_seqlens` computed for the same inputs at the capture batch size. It runs four replay and capture batch sizes on FLASHINFER and FLASH_ATTN. With `qwen3_vl.py` from main, 7 of the 8 cases fail. The one that passes is the FlashInfer case where replay and capture fall in the same batch bucket, so no padding happens. The whole file passes (52 passed, 25 skipped on CPU).

GPU validation by SyaOtiLan ([results](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63809#issuecomment-6557439065), with raw outputs and scripts): RTX 4090 (SM 8.9), FlashInfer 0.7.2.post1, PyTorch 2.14.0+cu130, Qwen/Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct in BF16 through `LLM(mm_encoder_only=True)`, `cudagraph_mm_encoder=True`, budgets [64, 256, 1024], at most 2 vision items and 16 frames per batch, one 224 x 224 image. The values are max abs differences of the vision encoder output embeddings. "Replay vs replay" compares later replays of the same input with the first one, and "Replay vs eager" compares the first replay with eager mode on the same padded buffers. The run used the same `qwen3_vl.py` change on top of 3687acad21, the head of #63809 at the time. `encoder_cudagraph.py`, `mm_encoder_attention.py`, `vit_attn_wrappers.py` and `qwen2_5_vl.py` are identical there and on this branch.

| Input | Replay vs replay, before | Replay vs replay, after | Replay vs eager, before | Replay vs eager, after |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 16 x 16 grid (processor default), 64 tokens | 9.65625 | 0 | 26.984375 | 0 |
| 14 x 14 grid, 49 tokens | 10.875 | 0 | 23.234375 | 0 |

In a [second run](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63809#issuecomment-6557974253) on the same branch, mixed-size and two-image batches, video, alternating input shapes and oversized inputs that fall back to eager were also checked: all 110 graph-covered conditions matched eager on the same padded buffers exactly, and the 1,368 calls of a shape-transition stress test were exact.

Padded and unpadded eager runs of the 49-token input still differ (max 0.28125, RMSE 0.0088). That difference does not involve graph replay, and this PR does not change it. A per-layer trace in the second run found that the first difference appears in `blocks.0.mlp.linear_fc1`, while the patch embedding, norms, QKV and attention before it match exactly, which points to shape-dependent numerics in the linear layer. End-to-end generation quality was not measured.

GPU validation of the current head 3b80be3 by SyaOtiLan ([results](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64984#issuecomment-6570819059), with scripts, raw logs and checksums): same RTX 4090, Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct in BF16, TP=1, `LLM(mm_encoder_only=True)`, budgets [64, 256, 1024], at most 2 vision items and 16 frames per batch, two fresh worker lifetimes per backend. The run reused precompiled extensions from 4135590ffe01 rather than a new wheel, and this PR changes only Python files. Each cell gives two max abs differences of the vision encoder output: a later replay against the first replay, then the first replay against eager mode on the same padded buffers.

| Input | Output tokens | FLASH_ATTN | FLASHINFER |
|---|---|---|---|
| Image 224, matched grid | 49 | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| Image 448 | 196 | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| Image 224, default processor grid | 64 | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| Mixed images 224 + 448 | 49 + 196 | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| Mixed images 448 + 224 | 196 + 49 | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| Video, 2 frames | 49 | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| Video, 8 frames | 196 | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| Video, 16 frames | 392 | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |

The image replays exercise the new tail fill: on FLASH_ATTN, 3 replay offsets go into a 17-entry capture buffer and the last offset fills the 14 tail entries. FLASHINFER keeps its split-half padding (18 replay entries, 34 capture entries). Video replays have the same length as capture on both backends. All 32 case checks and 192 later shape-switch executions passed. These results cover encoder replay correctness, not generation quality or latency.

## Details

For FlashInfer, `MMEncoderAttention.maybe_recompute_cu_seqlens` returns the q/k/o offsets followed by the v offsets, each half padded to a FlashInfer batch bucket (8, 16, 32 or 64), and `flashinfer_wrapper` splits the tensor at its midpoint. The BF16 and FP8 paths both use this two-half layout, and only BF16 was run on a GPU. Qwen3-VL captures with `cu_seqlens` padded to `max_frames_per_batch` (bucket 16 for 16 frames, 34 entries) and pads image replays to `max_batch_size` (bucket 8 for 2 items, 18 entries). `_copy_padded_buffer` zeroes the capture buffer and copies the 18 entries to its start. The q/k/o half then holds the 9 q/k/o offsets followed by the first 8 v offsets, and the v half holds the last v offset followed by zeros. Offsets count elements of the packed QKV buffer, so a v offset is 3 x tokens x hidden size. For one 196-patch image with an illustrative hidden size of 1152, the first two v offsets are [0, 677376] in eager mode and [677376, 0] after the default copy, so the kernel sees a sequence of negative length. That would explain why replays of the same input differ from each other, since the kernel then reads outside the valid range, but I have not confirmed this inside the kernel.

The fix mirrors the registration Qwen2.5-VL already has for the same key (`cu_seqlens`) and layout. Changing how image replays are padded would touch the shared graph manager and every model that uses it, while the hook keeps the change inside Qwen3-VL. Video replays pad to `max_frames_per_batch`, the same bucket as capture, so they are not affected, and video replays on the base commit were stable in the second run.

This PR and #63809 touch different model files. Both add tests to `tests/v1/cudagraph/test_encoder_cudagraph.py`, and this commit cherry-picks cleanly onto #63809, so they can merge in either order.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Kimi-K3] Pin FlashKDA and FlashMLA with NaN fixes
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/64758: under load, some Kimi-K3 requests turn into streams of token 0 (`!!!!`) until `max_tokens`. This PR moves the FlashKDA and FlashMLA pins to commits with two kernel fixes: https://github.com/vllm-project/FlashKDA/pull/16 and https://github.com/vllm-project/FlashMLA/pull/41.

Both kernel PRs are merged, and the pins point to their upstream merge commits.

## Claims

- FlashKDA prefill no longer copies a NaN from one request into other requests of the same batch. On Kimi-K3 with one injected NaN request, other decodes made bad drop from 96/240 to 0/240.
- FlashMLA's SM90 dense decode kernel now waits for the previous kernel (PDL) before it reads the query. A forced race gives NaN in 49/50 calls on stock and 0/50 with the fix.
- On the natural burst reproducer from the issue, bad requests went from 14 on stock to 0 with both fixes.
- No measurable end-to-end performance cost on Kimi-K3.

## Validation

All runs: `moonshotai/Kimi-K3` @ `f831ab66`, 2 x 8 H200, TP8 x PP2 over InfiniBand, V2 model runner, stock flags from the issue, vLLM `063c0c6` (PR #61867 head). The fixes were applied by swapping only `_flashkda_C` and `_flashmla_C`.

Burst reproducer (`repro_natural_burst.py` in the issue), fresh server per arm, same seed:

| | Stock | FlashKDA fix | FlashKDA fix + FlashMLA fix (no-PDL variant) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Run length | 12.5 min | 10.8 min | 25.0 min |
| First-NaN events | 2 | 1 | 0 (about 2.6 expected, P about 0.08) |
| Bad requests | 14 (groups of 2 and 13) | 1 | 0 |

The last arm used the FlashMLA variant that launches without PDL. The `griddepcontrol.wait` variant pinned here was checked with the forced kernel race (49/50 to 0/50, bit-identical outputs) and in the performance A/B below, but not on the burst reproducer.

With one NaN injected into one request by a debug hook, stock made 96 of 240 other decodes bad and the FlashKDA fix made 0. GSM8K was 0.945 on stock and 0.947 with the fix.

Performance, stock against both fixes, one server start per arm:

| Metric | Stock | Both fixes | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| TPOT, batch 1 (ms) | 15.51 | 15.50 | -0.1% |
| TPOT, batch 8 (ms) | 26.38 | 26.31 | -0.2% |
| TPOT, batch 32 (ms) | 44.20 (0.86) | 45.00 (1.3) | +1.8%, within noise |
| TPOT, batch 64 (ms) | 58.17 (3.4) | 59.38 (4.6) | +2.1%, within noise |
| TTFT, 1k-token prompt (ms) | 225.9 | 222.4 | -1.6% |
| TTFT, 8k-token prompt (ms) | 858.2 | 858.7 | +0.1% |
| TTFT, 64k-token prompt (ms) | 5046 | 5054 | +0.2% |
| GSM8K (5-shot) | 0.947 | 0.948 | +0.1% |

Each value is the median of 3 repetitions; brackets give the max-min spread where it matters. Both arms use `-O3 -DNDEBUG` builds whose SASS is identical to the wheel's; the only difference is the two patches. Three repetitions can neither show nor rule out a 1-2% cost at batch 32-64.

Decode: random 32-token prompts, 1,024 output tokens with `ignore_eos`, greedy, 4/16/64/128 prompts at concurrency 1/8/32/64. Prefill: `vllm bench serve` with random 1k/8k/64k-token prompts, 1 output token, concurrency 1, median TTFT. GSM8K: 5-shot, greedy, 1,319 questions, once per arm.

Kernel-level reproducers and tests are in the two kernel PRs.

## Details

**Spread (confirmed): FlashKDA.** Prefill works in chunks of 16 rows. For a sequence's last, partial chunk, it read `beta` and `v` from the rows after the sequence end (the next request in the batch, or the next head) and cancelled them by multiplying by zero. `0 * NaN` is NaN. vLLM runs the decode rows of a mixed step through this kernel together with the prefills, so one NaN request could hit up to 15 decodes and one prefill per step. The fix selects 0 for those rows.

**First NaN (strong suspect, not proven): FlashMLA.** K3's decode path runs `fused_kimi_k3_mla_decode_q_concat_kv_cache_insert`, which writes the query and triggers PDL completion, then FlashMLA's SM90 dense decode kernel. That kernel is launched with PDL but never called `griddepcontrol.wait`, so it could read a query buffer (`torch.empty`) that was not written yet. The fix adds the wait after the prologue. We have not shown that this race causes the natural events; one natural event appeared after the attention output, which it does not explain.

Pin contents:

- FlashKDA: `47fc9fe` (current pin, on upstream `dev`) to `9d9e928`, the merge of vllm-project/FlashKDA#16. No other upstream change comes in.
- FlashMLA: `d1a1c92` (current pin) to `847ef30` on upstream `main`, the merge of vllm-project/FlashMLA#41. It also brings vllm-project/FlashMLA#39, a one-line fix per kernel in the SM100 sparse decode head64 kernels.

Scope and limits:

- The FlashMLA change affects every model that uses the SM90 dense decode kernel, not only Kimi-K3. It adds one wait per CTA and leaves outputs bit-identical. We only measured Kimi-K3.
- CI cannot run Kimi-K3 (two 8 x H200 nodes). The validation above was done outside CI.
- vLLM code is unchanged; only the two pins in `cmake/external_projects/` move.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Benchmark] Keep numeric-string prompts as strings in CustomDataset
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes #65071. `CustomDataset.load_data()` lets `pd.read_json` infer the `prompt` column's dtype, so a JSONL file whose prompts are all numeric strings (`"00123"`, `"00456"`) is loaded as integers. Leading zeros are lost and `sample()` then fails in the tokenizer.

## Claims

- JSON string prompts are kept exactly as written, regardless of what other rows contain.
- `output_tokens` and other columns are unaffected.

## Validation

New regression test `test_custom_dataset_keeps_numeric_string_prompts` (CPU-only, local `WordLevel` tokenizer, no download) builds a real `CustomDataset` and calls `sample()`.

Before the fix (source reverted to `origin/main`):

```text
$ pytest tests/benchmarks/test_custom_dataset_seed.py -k numeric_string
E   ValueError: text input must be of type `str` (single example), `list[str]` ...
1 failed, 2 deselected
```

With the fix:

```text
$ pytest tests/benchmarks/test_custom_dataset_seed.py
3 passed
```

Lint: `pre-commit` hooks pass on the commit (ruff check/format, mypy, forbidden imports, test tethering). The test is picked up by the existing "Benchmarks CLI" step (`pytest -v -s benchmarks/`).

## Details

Root cause: pandas' default `dtype=True` coerces string columns that all parse as numbers. Passing `dtype={"prompt": str}` keeps the column as-is; other columns keep their current inference, so `output_tokens` behaviour is unchanged.

The other two `pd.read_json` callers in `datasets.py` read list-valued columns (`turns` / `messages`), which pandas does not coerce, so they are left alone.

Not a duplicate: no open PR references #65071. #60506 and #61776 also touch `CustomDataset` but address output lengths / audio without a tokenizer in `sample()`, not the `read_json` dtype.

commits.pr_title: [Frontend] Stream derender on /inference/v1/generate
commits.pr_body:
## Overview
  
Adds `stream: true` support for `output_mode: "derender"` on `/inference/v1/generate`. This is Phase 3 of #56851. 

~**Do NOT MERGE before #63148.**~

## Claims

- `stream: true` with `output_mode: "derender"` works now instead of returning a 400. Each chunk carries a chat `delta` (`role`, `content`, `reasoning`, `tool_calls`) and the chat `finish_reason`.
- For the same tokens, the output matches coupled `/v1/chat/completions` streaming because both paths run through the same `ChatStreamProcessor`. There's no second copy of the parse logic.
- No per-chunk `/derender` hop and no `stream_state`. Each choice keeps one parser for the life of the request.
- `n > 1` works. Streaming `/derender` only supports `n=1`.
- A bad `parse_context` or a parser that rejects the tools, returns a 400 before the engine does any work.
- If the stream fails partway, the request is now aborted in the engine. This applies to the `tokens` and `text` levels too.

## Validation

Unit tests use a mocked engine. Parity tests run a real model and compare against coupled chat streaming.

```bash
pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out -v
pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_parity.py -v -k "inline or stream"
pytest tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_stream_processor.py -v
```

The parity cases cover plain text, reasoning shown and hidden, tool_choice auto/required/named, parallel_tool_calls off, stop strings and n=2. For each case they check the concatenated token IDs, content, reasoning, tool calls (name, arguments, ID shape) and finish_reason. Logprobs are covered for top_logprobs, logprob_token_ids and hidden reasoning.

No model evals were run. The generated tokens don't change, only how the output is shaped and the parity tests check that shape against coupled chat.

### Benchmarks (TTFT/TPOT, inline derender vs tokens stream + `/derender` per chunk, plus mixed traffic on one pod)

@shimib benchmarked this on one A100-40G with Qwen3-8B https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63103#issuecomment-6407286233 and Qwen3-VL-8B https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63103#issuecomment-6446448022. The runs compare tokens only (G), tokens plus a per-chunk `/derender` call (B) and inline `output_mode: "derender"` (D). There were over 16,000 requests, zero errors and output tokens matched within 2%.

The RFC (#56851) set out to get rid of the per-chunk `/derender` hop for interactive P/D traffic and this PR does that. D's TTFT is 85–150 ms faster than B's at p50 and only 14–35 ms behind the token floor. That holds for text, tool calls, reasoning and images. D also streams token by token with ITL close to G, while B only keeps its TPOT by batching tokens which means clients get text in bursts. TPOT matches G within 0.5 ms and mixed G/D traffic on one worker doesn't hurt either side.

The weak spot is heavy reasoning load (~1.9k tok/s through the Qwen3 parser). There D's TPOT p95 rises 6 ms and colocated tokens only requests lose about 10–23 ms of TTFT because parsing runs on the API server event loop. `--api-server-count` should help but wasn't tested. E2E latency wasn't measured either.

## Details

- Parsing runs on the API server event loop, the same as coupled chat. An executor hop per chunk would add TPOT and with the default `renderer_num_workers=1`, every derender stream would queue on one thread. `--api-server-count` scales the parsing.
- Text comes from the engine's own incremental detokenizer, so stop strings and the decode flags `/render` set behave exactly as they do in coupled chat.
- `parse_context.history_tool_call_cnt` seeds each parser. Without it, deterministic tool call IDs (Kimi style) would restart at 0.
- When `include_reasoning` is false, `token_ids`, `logprobs` and `sampling_mask` are dropped on every chunk, the same as batch derender.
- The batch and stream generators now pick their logprob settings from one shared helper.

**Two choices I'd like feedback on:**

1. Where `role` goes. `role` is on the first chunk of each choice, the same as streaming `/derender`. There's no role only preamble chunk like coupled chat sends because that would add a chunk before the first token and skew TTFT comparisons.
2. Chunks where the parser emits nothing. Coupled chat drops these unless `return_token_ids` is set. Generate always returns token IDs, so these chunks are still sent while their IDs are visible. P/D clients need every token ID. With hidden reasoning the IDs are hidden, so the chunk is dropped, as in coupled chat.

Out of scope: the Rust frontend, `reasoning_tokens` in generate usage, Cohere citations (#63164), and per-request `return_tokens_as_token_ids` (#63162).
